Claim: Let P0=Bern(a)^d with 0<a<=1/2, target A={1}, p=a^d and integer 0<=k<d. Set D_k=sum_(j=0)^k binom(d,j)((1-a)/a)^j and K=p^-1-D_k. If D_k<=K, the source constructs nonnegative P* with every marginal on at most k coordinates exactly equal to P0, P*(A)=2p and chi-square(P*||P0)=1/K<=2p. This divergence is minimal among laws satisfying those marginal and event-mass constraints. An adaptive assay revealing at most k distinct coordinates from each fresh specimen has identical transcript laws under P0 and P*, even with unlimited specimens. A separate positive regime assumes known product structure and explicit polynomial-size DNF failure modes and composes established product-estimation/weighted-witness methods.
Interface: Known d,a,k and a rare conjunction under a Bernoulli product baseline. The negative pair is indistinguishable from supplied low-order marginals; the assay reveals at most k distinct coordinates per fresh specimen. Reusing a specimen to observe more coordinates changes the contract. The positive regime requires true product structure and explicit DNF representation.
Proof spine: In L^2(P0), split the point-evaluation reproducing kernel at the all-ones vector into degrees <=k and >k. The high-degree residual is orthogonal to every function of <=k coordinates. Adding it to the likelihood ratio doubles target-event mass while preserving all those marginals. Its squared norm gives the chi-square value; Cauchy-Schwarz proves optimality. Transcript coupling handles the stated adaptive fresh-specimen assay.
Costs: The source gives a full-vector relative-estimation lower bound of Omega(1/(epsilon^2 p)) under its stated conditions despite exact supplied marginals through order k. P* has a compact exact rejection sampler with reported acceptance 1/2; constructing it does not reveal which real-world law holds. The positive product/DNF regime charges measurements and arithmetic and uses known methods.
Failure: D_k<=K is required. The divergence optimum is not by itself a finite-sample minimax theorem for every assay. Product and explicit-DNF assumptions are essential to the positive regime. No real failure law or general rare-event capability is established.
Closest comparator: Astra N492 studies rare-event certificate acquisition under a different interface. This result supplies a moment-matching/k-coordinate construction; it does not imply all higher-order validation is impossible.

Claim: For the explicitly constructed rational, nonnegative, pure undisplaced Gaussian pair kernels with operator norm<1/2 and mean photon number<5/12, condition on one photon in every graph mode and leave two output modes unheralded. A classical conditional sampler with adjustable TV error and polynomial runtime in exact input length and inverse error is polynomially equivalent, under the stated reductions, to an FPRAS for perfect matchings of arbitrary unweighted simple graphs, including exact zero detection.
Interface: Restricted supplied Gaussian family and graph; one unit-photon herald in every original graph mode, two output modes remain. The sampler must work uniformly over every nonzero herald. The reductions charge precision, encoded bit length, conditional calls, zero heralds and sample budget.
Proof spine: Attach two leaves to an edge uv. The two remaining modes output only 00 or 11 with q=R^2 p_uv^2/(1+R^2 p_uv^2), where p_uv is a uniform-perfect-matching edge marginal. Dyadic calibration and self-reduction recover the count from conditional samples; approximate counting supplies the reverse direction. Source replays check finite graph/hafnian identities and support.
Costs: The reduction uses O(n^2 log(n/delta)+n^3 epsilon^-2 log(n/delta)) conditional samples plus a coarse-search term; the finest requested TV error is Theta(epsilon/n). Literal herald rejection costs at least (63/128)4^n preparations per accepted calibrated event. The direct sampler is not implemented; proof constants request about 7.3e8 samples already at n=2, epsilon=.1, delta=.01.
Failure: This is an equivalence, not an efficient conditional sampler, matching algorithm or complexity separation. It applies only to the stated family and herald pattern. Variable-subset GBS has a different output law and does not supply the required conditional guarantee.
Closest comparator: Astra N417/N419 cover Gaussian samplers/reductions at distinct interfaces. Hafnian graph encodings and variable-subset GBS are prior art; this result does not claim the broad Gaussian/matching connection as new.
Open verification: Find a proved direct conditional sampler or a materially different resource contract; otherwise obtain expert review of both reduction directions and retain the capability barrier.

Claim: For a supplied rational ten-state generator Q, changed discrete-time chains P_e=I+eQ (e=1,1/2) have stationary six-label observed laws that are time-reversal invariant and pass the stated centered reflection complete-positivity tests, yet an explicit rational statistic W_e on five consecutive letters has nonnegative expectation under every stationary reversible hidden Markov model with deterministic emissions and negative expectation under P_e. The e=1/2 target additionally has positive observable spectrum [0,1], hence completely monotone scalar correlations. A certified empirical-Bernstein test for this half-step target has sufficient budget 2,057,310,156,600,085,612,368 independent stationary windows. This is sufficient for the stated test, not necessary sample complexity.
Interface: The construction changes the continuous-time source process; P_e is not claimed to sample the original CTMC. Competitors are stationary reversible hidden Markov models with deterministic emissions and arbitrary hidden cardinality. The finite test assumes independent stationary five-letter windows and stationary preparation; it is not a guarantee for one correlated trajectory under arbitrary mixing.
Proof spine: Exact rational one-step features and a five-marker left inverse define a bounded five-letter statistic. A universal inequality forces nonnegative expectation for each stated reversible hidden model; exact target algebra makes it negative. Claim: Under a fixed-period model with independent mean-zero division innovations, the report derives conditional within/across-division MSD formulas and an explicit causal delayed response h_l(t)=h_0(t-l). Numerically choosing l≈1.301 hours makes one defined continuous-lag aggregate ratio R=1/2 for T=10.2 hours and chosen integral memory 5.4 hours. The model also predicts suppressed short-lag changes across division, quiet within-cycle intervals and an upturn in growth averaged since birth late in the cycle. Claim: Let a compact group G act orthogonally on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space V by pi, with normalized Haar measure. For independent Haar controls and an m-state Markov simulator whose row-stochastic update P_t(g) may depend measurably on time and the current control, set b_i(t)=E[pi(g_t...g_1)x 1{S_t=i}] and R_t=sum_i ||b_i(t)||. Define kappa_m(pi)=sup_{||v||=1} sup_{||w_1||=...=||w_m||=1} integral_G max_j <w_j,pi(g)v> dg. Then R_t<=kappa_m(pi)R_(t-1), hence R_T<=kappa_m(pi)^T||x||. The adjoint action-compatible transfer is (A_P z)_i=integral pi(g)^(-1)(sum_j P_g(i,j)z_j)dg and has norm at most kappa_m(pi).
Interface: The controls are independent Haar draws; the representation is orthogonal; the state is the only charged persistent record of past controls. Fresh randomness is allowed. The transition rule can depend on time and the current control. The theorem bounds unnormalized conditional means, not only pure or initially orbit-valued states.
Proof spine: The conditional-mean recursion expresses each next state vector as a sum of group-averaged stochastic transitions. Align one unit vector with each resulting integral. Row-stochasticity bounds their sum by the orbit-code maximum defining kappa; the triangle inequality and summation over states give the one-step contraction. The transfer operator is the corresponding adjoint map.
Costs: A state-retention theorem only. The description size of P_t, gate acquisition, precision, barycentric compilation and sampling costs are not bounded. Persistent seeds, correlated external noise and external continuous controllers must be charged or are outside the model.
Failure: This does not lower-bound signed-coordinate or unrestricted numerical simulators. Correlated external noise changes the memory contract. The Haar one-step coefficient cannot be applied unchanged to arbitrary finite control alphabets; see N546.
Closest comparator: The representation-valued transform and spherical quantization ingredients are known mathematics. The source presents the operational contraction/composition interface as its candidate contribution; novelty is UNKNOWN. N507 is a scoped comparison only and is not used as a proved premise.
Open verification: Independently verify the conditional-mean contraction for the stated measurable transition class and compare the transfer operator with prior representation-transform literature.

Claim: For the standard SO(d) action, eta_(m,d)=sup_(v_1,...,v_m in S^(d-1)) integral max_j <u,v_j> d sigma(u) is the constrained spherical quantization coefficient. The source proves R_T<=eta_(m,d)^T with equality attainable for the retention problem; eta_(m,2)=m sin(pi/m)/pi; eta_(m,3)<=1-1/m (no equality claim); and 1-eta_(m,d)=Theta_d(m^(-2/(d-1))) for fixed d. For p_*(+|x,g_1,...,g_t,u)=(1+delta<u,g_t...g_1 x>)/2, 0<delta<=1/d and 0<epsilon<delta/(2d), the minimum number of positive Markov states uniformly simulating all preparations, readouts and gate words through horizon T is Theta_(d,delta,epsilon)(T^((d-1)/2)). The static positive factorization size is exactly d+1.
Interface: Fixed dimension d>=2; x,u range over the Euclidean unit ball; each supplied gate is in SO(d); controls in the retention experiment are independent Haar draws. The simulator has an m-state Markov memory, arbitrary time/current-gate measurable stochastic updates and uniform additive probability error epsilon. The exponent is fixed-d and the constants depend on d, delta and epsilon.
Proof spine: The spherical coefficient equals one minus half the optimal mean squared nearest-codeword distance. A conditional-mean argument gives the exact retention contraction and a nearest-codeword construction attains it. Cap covering and packing establish the fixed-d quantization rate. A bounded terminal score converts retention into the state lower bound; a circumscribed polytope and barycentric stochastic updates give the matching upper bound. A regular simplex gives the exact static d+1 factorization and rank lower bound.
Costs: The theorem counts states, not bits or runtime. Gate acquisition, net generation, triangulation, barycentric map size, probability precision, transition-table description and sampling are not bounded. For d=3, T-state order means Theta(log T) classical bits under ideal state encoding, not Theta(T) bits.
Failure: Continuous Haar controls are essential to the displayed coefficient. The result does not imply a lower bound for signed coordinates or an ordinary finite-precision simulator without charging its full persistent memory and numerical resources. Finite groups can admit bounded-state exact constructions.
Closest comparator: Spherical quantization and manifold approximation have established literature and are not claimed as inventions. The candidate contribution is the operational positive-composition retention law and its matching state-count construction; priority remains UNKNOWN.
Open verification: Independently check the exact attainment argument and the conversion from the bounded score to a uniform state lower bound; complete a focused prior-art comparison before any novelty claim.

Claim: Fix D>=2, n=D^2-1, r_0=sqrt((D-1)/D), and H_0(D), the real Hilbert space of traceless Hermitian D by D matrices with Hilbert-Schmidt inner product. Let K_D={A_rho=(rho-I/D)/r_0: rho>=0, Tr(rho)=1}. For supplied unitaries U_1,...,U_t with V_t=U_t...U_1 and any B in the Hilbert-Schmidt unit ball, the target bit law is p_*(+|A,U_1,...,U_t,B)=1/2(1+delta Tr(B V_t A V_t^*)). For fixed D, 0<delta<=1/n and 0<epsilon<delta/(2n), the minimum number of classical Markov states that uniformly approximates all preparations, terminal queries, and words of length at most T is Theta_(D,delta,epsilon)(T^(D-1)). The static positive factorization size is exactly D^2; the quantum realization uses Hilbert-space dimension D; the state-count law corresponds to (D-1)log_2 T+O_(D,delta,epsilon)(1) classical bits.
Interface: The preparation rho=I/D+r_0 A ranges over all density matrices; B ranges over the Hilbert-Schmidt unit ball; controls are arbitrary supplied unitary words; the binary effect is E_B=1/2(I+delta B/r_0). The classical simulator must meet uniform additive error epsilon for all inputs and all word lengths <=T, with arbitrary measurable time/current-unitary stochastic transitions. Only the finite internal state stores history; no persistent seed, correlated external noise or stored continuous state is free.
Proof spine: For independent Haar unitaries, unnormalized conditional means contract by kappa_(m,D). A uniform small-ball bound for every unit traceless-Hermitian conjugation orbit follows by selecting a nontrivial eigenvalue gap and comparing nearby conjugates to complex Grassmannian projection balls. This yields 1-kappa_(m,D)=Theta_D(m^(-1/(D-1))) without claiming equality of repeated powers. A bounded terminal score gives the Omega(T^(D-1)) state lower bound. A projective net and an inflated convex polytope with barycentric stochastic updates give O(T^(D-1)); a regular simplex proves the separate exact D^2 static factorization size.
Costs: Fixed-D asymptotic state count only. The theorem does not bound the size or precision of the transition maps, construction of projective nets/polytope triangulations, barycentric evaluation, sampling, gate compilation or runtime. It is not a general computational quantum speedup and is not uniform jointly in D,T,delta,epsilon.
Failure: No sharp state law is established for the fixed five-gate qubit alphabet in N546. No lower bound follows for an unrestricted floating-point simulator unless all persistent numerical state is charged. The source explicitly does not assert R_T=kappa_(m,D)^T.
Closest comparator: The source identifies Montina 2008/2010 and correlated-noise models as important predecessors; detailed comparison with those full papers and the 2026 finite-memory preprint is incomplete. No priority claim is made. N507 is unreviewed context only, not an imported theorem.

N546-finite-control-retention-block-profile-and-gate | A block retention profile handles finite controls while the fixed five-gate state law remains unresolved
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported internally derived written arguments and finite checks from a single assistant research session; not independently reconstructed, externally reviewed, formally certified, or priority-cleared during intake. The historic foundational objective remains NOT ESTABLISHED. The fixed-alphabet state law is unresolved in this investigation, not asserted globally open.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For a probability law nu on SO(d), define eta_m(nu)=sup_(||v||=1,n_1,...,n_m in S^(d-1)) integral max_j <n_j,g v> dnu(g). The source derives R_T<=inf_(1<=k<=T) eta_m(nu^(*k))^floor(T/k). If nu has support size at most m, eta_m(nu)=1, so a one-step coefficient gives no contraction in that regime. A finite group of rotations nevertheless admits a uniform-in-horizon exact weak-readout realization using a finite invariant polytope. The sharp law m_*(T)=Theta(T) for A={I,R_x,R_x^(-1),R_z,R_z^(-1)}, with the two named-axis rotations having cosine 3/5 and sine 4/5, delta=1/3 and epsilon=1/72, is explicitly unresolved in this investigation.
Interface: Independent controls with law nu, finite-state Markov updates, and all persistent classical memory charged. The block bound is an interface for products of k controls. The five-gate question uses the same d=3 state-count contract as the sphere theorem. The stated unresolved status is local to this investigation and does not assert the question is globally open.
Proof spine: Apply the one-step conditional-mean contraction to k independent controls jointly, whose product has law nu^(*k), for floor(T/k) blocks; leftover steps have coefficient at most one. If support size is <=m, choose codewords containing the images of each state under every supported control, giving eta_m(nu)=1. The finite-group exact realization uses the group translates of a circumscribed simplex. These facts limit direct use of the continuous-Haar exponent.
Costs: The block profile is a state-retention bound. The finite-alphabet five-gate asymptotic state count is unknown here. Compilation, gate acquisition, precision, and runtime are not established.
Failure: The Haar one-step coefficient cannot be substituted for the fixed alphabet. The density of the specified gate group establishes density only, not a quantitative lower bound. Solving this question would still require separate significance and priority review.
Closest comparator: Finite-control block products, finite cyclic code formulas and invariant polytopes are the packet comparators. No global open-problem or novelty claim is made.
Open verification: Prove or refute m_*(T)=Theta(T) for the exact five-gate qubit alphabet at delta=1/3 and epsilon=1/72 under the charged Markov-memory interface; perform a dedicated prior-art review before calling it open.

N547-weighted-stationary-current-cancellation-identity | Pairwise controlled stationary laws cancel unknown currents into a weighted diffusion identity
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported independent analytic derivation and finite consistency checks; this intake did not reconstruct the proof or rerun code. External correctness, formal certification, priority and physical validation remain UNKNOWN. No historic-scale or 9–10/10 breakthrough was established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Let the same smooth unknown drift b and constant symmetric D≻0 govern controlled diffusions on R^d with vanishing boundary flux/integrability, or on a flat torus. Under known smooth controls u_i, strictly positive stationary C² densities p_i and divergence-free currents J_i=(b+u_i)p_i−D∇p_i, set r=p_i/p_j, w=∇log r and δu=u_i−u_j. For every admissible scalar q for which the integrations are justified, the source derives D:E_{p_i}[q(r)wwᵀ]=E_{p_i}[q(r)δu·w]. Thus full rank of the collected symmetric matrix features M_{ij,q}=E_{p_i}[q(r)wwᵀ], in dimension d(d+1)/2, identifies the constant D uniquely.
Interface: All regimes share b and constant state-independent D; intervention fields are known; stationary laws are exact and fully observed for the theorem. The feature-rank condition is a hypothesis to check, not a consequence of having multiple regimes. The test-function class for q and the required boundary/integrability conditions are not fully enumerated in the source.
Proof spine: Use J_i=rJ_j+p_i(δu−Dw). Choose f with f′(r)=q(r)/r, multiply the stationary divergence equation by f(r), cancel the J_j term as a gradient against a divergence-free current, and integrate the remaining divergence by parts. The resulting identity is linear in the symmetric entries of D.
Costs: No finite-sample or numerical acquisition bound. The features require density-ratio gradients and stationary expectations; acquiring or estimating these, waiting for each regime to mix, and calibrating controls are uncharged. An algebraic perturbation bound is conditional on the exact design singular value and feature errors.
Failure: Rank deficiency prevents unique D recovery; two-regime weighted features can be ill-conditioned despite full rank. The exact identity does not supply a statistical estimator for general smooth densities or a physical snapshot-acquisition protocol.
Closest comparator: Fokker–Planck inversion and weak-form/Stein generator identities have established prior work. The source reports a partial literature check and leaves the exact weighted current-cancellation identity priority UNKNOWN.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the identity with an explicit admissible q class and boundary conditions; verify the symmetric-feature vectorization and assess exact-identity prior art.

N548-conditional-generator-identifiability-and-invisible-current-gauge | Full generator recovery is conditional on rank, while two stationary laws leave an invisible current
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported analytic derivation and synthetic numerical diagnostics; no external proof review, formal verification or physical system identification was performed at intake. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Let s_i=∇log p_i and T_i=∇²p_i/p_i for d+1 controlled experiments, and define W(x)=[s_1−s_0,…,s_d−s_0]. For i=1,…,d define h_i=D:(T_i−T_0)−∇·u_i−u_i·s_i+∇·u_0+u_0·s_0. Under the source’s smoothness and exact-law assumptions, if the pairwise matrix features identify constant D and W(x) is invertible almost everywhere, subtracting stationary Fokker–Planck equations identifies b(x)=W(x)^{−T}h(x) almost everywhere. Conversely, for a compatible pair of positive stationary densities on T², known D and controls do not identify general b: adding v(x)=p_0(x)^{−1}S∇(p_1/p_0), for a nonzero constant skew matrix S, preserves both stationary laws but changes their currents.
Interface: The sufficient theorem assumes full-state, exactly known positive stationary densities, common smooth b, constant D, known controls, full rank in the D-feature system and almost-everywhere pointwise rank of W. The counterexample is on the flat two-dimensional torus and retains the same D and controls. Neither statement is a finite-sample result.
Proof spine: Subtract the stationary Fokker–Planck equations to obtain d linear equations in b(x); invert W wherever it has full rank. For the obstruction, p_0v=S∇r has zero divergence, and p_1v=rS∇r also has zero divergence because S is skew and Hessians are symmetric.
Costs: The nonparametric formula uses density scores, second derivatives, pointwise matrix inversion and conditioning. Statistical error, regularization, regions where W is nearly singular, mixing, finite samples and partial observation have no guarantee.
Failure: A singular or poorly conditioned W prevents stable drift recovery. The two-regime gauge refutes unrestricted full-drift identification from those two laws, but it does not refute recovery of D or the d+1 rank-conditional theorem. A radial or latent projection does not satisfy the full-state interface.
Closest comparator: The source cites prior Fokker–Planck algebra and intervention-identifiability work; no complete proof-level priority audit is reported. N498 is a useful projection-loss contrast, not a theorem premise.
Open verification: Independently verify the almost-everywhere uniqueness statement and the two-law gauge for the declared boundary conditions; quantify what changes under partial observation or noisy estimated scores.

N549-affine-stationary-tilt-generator-rigidity | Exact affine density tilts determine diffusion and a nonreversible generator under a full-rank force contract
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported written derivation with synthetic diagnostics; this intake did not independently reconstruct or externally review it. Exact-tilt assumptions, sample-access costs and prior-art limits remain explicit. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: On R^d, suppose p_i(x)=Z_i^{−1}p_0(x)exp(a_iᵀx) for i=1,…,d, with A=[a_1,…,a_d] nonsingular, known constant forces U=[u_1,…,u_d], a common drift and constant D≻0. Under consistency and normalizability, the source derives B=UA^{−1}, D=sym(B), K=skew(B), and b(x)=B∇log p_0(x), with stationary current J_i=K∇p_i. Thus an arbitrary nonlinear log p_0 is allowed within this exact-tilt family and the circulation can be nonzero. Fewer than d independent tilt directions cannot guarantee full generator identification in the worst case within the family.
Interface: The tilt relation is exact, A is full rank, controls are known constant forces, and D is constant symmetric positive definite. The identification result assumes exact stationary laws; classifier estimates of tilt slopes from independent stationary samples are a separate statistical procedure. Estimating b or entropy production still requires score information.
Proof spine: Use the pairwise identity with q=1 and constant w=a_i−a_j to recover the symmetric part of UA^{−1}; the score-difference matrix is A, so the stationary Fokker–Planck subtraction gives b. Conversely the skew part produces a divergence-free stationary current. If fewer directions are observed, perturb B by a nonzero E annihilating all observed a_i while preserving positive definiteness of sym(B+E).
Costs: No finite-sample rate for estimating A, B, D or b is proved. Accuracy depends on force amplitudes, density overlap and conditioning of A; physical preparation of independent stationary regimes and time to equilibrium are not charged.
Failure: The formula is specific to exact exponential tilts with invertible A. It does not extend automatically to arbitrary density ratios, unknown/state-dependent diffusion, changing drift across interventions, latent state, or finite-sample high-dimensional estimation.
Closest comparator: The source recognizes OU intervention and broader stationary SDE identifiability literature; exact priority for this nonlinear-base affine-tilt formula is UNKNOWN. The route is a conditional structural result, not a general identification algorithm.
Open verification: Independently verify both directions of the affine-tilt corollary and the fewer-than-d worst-case intervention obstruction; compare the exact model with prior stationary-intervention results.

N550-synthetic-stationary-snapshot-diagnostics-and-acquisition-limits | Synthetic stationary-snapshot diagnostics are model-conditional and do not establish physical acquisition
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported finite synthetic diagnostics; archive and result records were checked, but scientific code was not executed during intake. No real-system validation, external review, formal verification or historic-scale breakthrough is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: The packet reports three synthetic diagnostics. In a three-dimensional non-Gaussian quartic exact-i.i.d. tilt model, 25 repetitions at 32,000 accepted draws per regime produced mean relative Frobenius errors 1.70% for B, 1.71% for D and 1.52% for K; local generation/fitting time excludes physical preparation and equilibration. A two-dimensional non-affine torus calculation used deterministic stationary-grid solutions, not random observed samples: at grid side 192, three-regime D error was 0.0288%, while the two-regime weighted system had condition number about 198 and 3.74% error. A quartic-family entropy-production estimate reported 1.63% mean relative error at 32,000 draws per regime over 12 repetitions, with the quartic potential family supplied and an independently sampled reference based on 750,000 additional baseline draws. These are source-reported synthetic outcomes, not empirical scientific validation or finite-sample theorems.
Interface: The 3D study uses exact independent synthetic stationary draws and a specified quartic potential; the torus study solves a discretized stationary PDE and computes grid scores/Hessians; the entropy-production study supplies the quartic potential family and draws a separate reference. None uses real physical data or charges physical stationary preparation.
Reported diagnostic scope: The handoff records generated sample populations, numerical stationary grids, estimates, errors, replication counts and selected controls. The finite proof-check output tests floating-point consistency only. The packet scripts/results are preserved; no script or experiment was rerun during repository intake.
Costs: Reported CPU timings omit physical perturbation, calibration, mixing/equilibration and instrument costs; the entropy-production reference uses 750,000 additional exact independent baseline draws (1,050,000 rejection proposals). Grid computation is exponential in dimension. No costed physical or noisy-correlated stationary-snapshot acquisition is demonstrated.
Failure: The source explicitly reports model-misspecification, rank/conditioning, score/Hessian acquisition and high-dimensional sample barriers. The two-regime torus estimate is ill-conditioned despite full rank; deterministic-grid precision is not sample-based recovery.
Closest comparator: The 3D finite-force Gaussian-moment comparator is not state of the art. The source separately supplies a stronger same-sample score-moment comparison in N551. No broad estimator dominance or novel physical capability is claimed.
Open verification: Replicate with independently generated finite noisy stationary data under charged mixing/preparation costs and controlled misspecification; first establish that the needed density-ratio gradients or score structure can be estimated in the intended dimension.

N551-weak-generator-moments-and-matched-score-comparator | Supplied-basis weak moments are familiar, and a matched score estimator removes a dominance claim
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported synthetic computation and prior-art assessment; no scientific code was executed during intake. Weak-form methods are acknowledged prior art, and no estimator dominance or historic-scale result is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: The packet’s weak stationary-generator regression replaces density derivatives with empirical weak-form generator moments only after supplying an eight-function Fourier drift basis: on its synthetic 2D torus model, 12 repetitions with 80,000 samples per regime (240,000 total) report mean drift-coefficient error 4.01% and D error 5.50%. The source itself demotes this strategy as established weak Fokker–Planck/Stein prior art. In a separate 25-repetition paired same-sample comparison on the 3D quartic model, at 32,000 samples per regime the logistic density-ratio estimate had 1.78% mean B error versus 1.62% for score moments that additionally use the known quartic potential family; the reported paired 95% interval for the logistic-minus-score error difference is [−0.048,+0.360] percentage points and includes zero. The experiments establish no general estimator dominance.
Interface: The weak-moment linear system assumes a supplied finite drift basis and known test functions; data are generated by a numerical stationary simulator. The matched comparator reuses the same sample populations, while the score-moment method receives the quartic potential family. Reported intervals describe repetitions of one synthetic distribution, not population-science uncertainty.
Method and comparison scope: Weak integration by parts expresses stationary generator moments using observed positions and known test functions. The paired score-moment comparator uses a_i=−E_{p_i}[∇log p_0] after fitting the supplied-form quartic potential. The source reports errors and comparison intervals, but this intake does not independently run either method.
Costs: The finite drift basis and quartic family are supplied structural information. The simulations omit physical acquisition and equilibration. No nonasymptotic guarantee, real-data confirmation, or broad efficiency comparison is given.
Failure: Without the basis or potential-family information, the source’s shortcuts do not solve generic high-dimensional score acquisition. The weak method is prior art, and the score estimator sometimes outperforms the logistic estimator; do not claim a new dominant algorithm.
Closest comparator: The source cites published weak Fokker–Planck/Stein methods and a matched same-data parametric score-moment comparator. This card records an explicit prior-art demotion and negative dominance result, not a novelty claim.
Open verification: Verify the matched information sets and uncertainty calculation, audit the cited weak-form prior art, and require an acquisition-complete comparator before claiming algorithmic advantage.

body:
N552-mixed-family-approximate-broadcasting-maximal-instability | Unbounded mixed-state families allow near-perfect marginal broadcasting with maximal EB and commuting error
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The attached source supplies a self-contained analytic argument and author-internal algebraic/finite checks (112 construction and 44 finite-design checks). The repository intake only preserves and routes the source; it did not run scripts, independently reconstruct the proof, or conduct external or formal review. Historical priority and practical resource-bounded significance remain UNKNOWN. No historic-scale or 9–10/10 breakthrough is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Let T(ρ,σ)=½‖ρ−σ‖₁. For every finite recipient count m≥2 and ε,η>0, the source constructs finite d,L, a finite family F={ρ_{ψ_x}} on H=⊕_{r=0}^L Sym^{m^r}(C^d), and one fixed positive finite prior (w_x), such that a full-domain permutation-symmetric CPTP map B:H→H^{⊗m} has every one-recipient marginal error at most 1/L≤ε, while every common entanglement-breaking map E:H→H and every family of commuting replacement states diagonal in one common basis have worst-case error at least 1−η. The same lower bounds hold as averages under the fixed prior. For the corresponding classical–quantum state ω_XH=Σ_x w_x|x⟩⟨x|⊗ρ_{ψ_x}, each XH_j marginal can be broadcast within 1/L, yet its trace distance from every state classical on H is at least 1−η, even when the comparator may change its X marginal. Consequently the suprema of EB and commuting reconstruction error are one for every positive broadcasting tolerance at fixed finite m. The proof gives formulas a=(1/L)Σ_{r=1}^L(k_r+1)/(k_r+d), β=min{1,√(Σ_{r=1}^L D_{k_r}/D_{2k_r})}, with k_r=m^r and D_s=binom(d+s−1,s); choose L large and d sufficiently large (or d=m²m^{2L}) so a,β→0. One common finite weighted projective 2m^L-design supports all comparators and bases simultaneously.
Interface: All maps act on finite-dimensional full matrix algebras and are CPTP; T is half trace norm. The input family consists of rank-L mixed direct-sum states ρ_ψ=0_{H_0}⊕(1/L)⊕_{r=1}^L p_ψ^{⊗m^r}, p_ψ=|ψ⟩⟨ψ|, with a fixed finite design prior. The construction's input already contains a classically uncertain number of genuine unknown-state copies, up to K=m^L. The EB comparator is one common physical measure-and-prepare channel for all family states, with arbitrary finite outcomes. The commuting comparator must use one common basis. The cq comparator can choose a different X marginal but must be classical on H. The source's marginal error is exactly 1/L for its constructed channel; the optimal broadcast error is only bounded above by 1/L. Outputs need not be close to the product family and are highly correlated.
Source-reported proof spine: Let H_r=Sym^{k_r}(C^d), k_r=m^r. The explicit isometry partitions each symmetric k_r-copy block into m groups of k_{r−1}; the full-domain channel maps each sector down one level and sends H_0 to a fixed product output. Only the top and bottom blocks differ in each marginal, giving exact half-trace error 1/L. A fixed decoder extracts one qudit; composing it with any EB map and applying the pure-state estimation bound (k+1)/(k+d) yields the prior-average EB lower bound. For commuting families, the support projections Q_ψ=Lρ_ψ obey a second-moment bound summed over an arbitrary common orthonormal basis; the finite exact 2K design preserves the needed moments. A measurement of X and Q_{ψ_x}, followed by data processing and Cauchy–Schwarz, handles arbitrary changes to the comparator's X marginal. Explicit parameter choices make the bounds approach one while the marginal error tends to zero.
Costs: K=m^L genuine copies occur in the highest sector, dim H=Σ_{r=0}^L D_{k_r}, and the Carathéodory finite prior may require up to D_{2K}² points. The explicit algebraic cubature also has (ceil((2K+1)/2)(2K+1))^{d−1} points; the paper does not establish an efficient construction at large parameters. No cost is supplied for preparing the input from one unknown qudit; such preparation is not part of the contract. The channel is an explicit mathematical CPTP map on a very large space, not a demonstrated resource-bounded physical implementation. Global cloning error approaches one; for L≥2 the source also gives ‖Φ−Φ²‖_diamond=2. Small marginal trace distance therefore does not imply global product fidelity or near-idempotence.
Failure: This refutes only dimension-independent, statewise trace-distance stability without dimension/resource restrictions. It does not refute exact no-broadcasting, bounded-Holevo-capacity conclusions, small-Holevo-loss conclusions, or the pure-family theorem N534. The constructed states are mixed (choose L≥2), and dimension, copy number and Holevo capacity diverge. The exact capacity/loss boundary is routed separately in N553. No NPT bound-entanglement result, FEI solution, efficient one-qudit acquisition, practical experiment, or historic-scale breakthrough is claimed.
Closest comparator: Exact no-broadcasting and finite pure-state estimation/design results are cited as predecessors; the pure-state estimation inequality is reproved in the source. The source reports a targeted but non-exhaustive prior-art search, not historical priority. N534 assumes pure inputs and is not contradicted by this mixed, unbounded-resource family.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the direct-sum CPTP map, the one fixed finite-prior EB bound, the basis-uniform commuting bound and the changed-X-marginal cq argument. Check all norm conventions, finite-design moment order, quantifiers and resource dependencies; then assess priority against the exact prior literature.

Along the explicit sequence d=m²K² this δ diverges. Thus this construction does not satisfy N368’s bounded-capacity premise or N371’s small-Holevo-loss premise and does not resolve N371. For a reweighted level distribution p_1,…,p_L, the same shift channel has marginal error ½(p_1+p_L+Σ_{r=1}^{L−1}|p_{r+1}−p_r|)≥max_r p_r, so error at most b forces L≥1/b and H(p)≥log(1/b) for this construction. This last inequality is not a universal lower bound for arbitrary broadcasters.
Interface: The formulas use the same finite-dimensional direct-sum family and marginal channel as N552. C is the Holevo capacity supremum over finite priors on that finite family; δ is evaluated for the stated exact finite design prior. The reweighting bound applies only to the described level-shift broadcaster. It does not quantify a universal optimum over channels, input families or reweightings outside this construction.
Scope and resource accounting: The source computes the block-diagonal average state and the entropy of each rank-L family state to obtain C. The marginal shift removes the top copy sector, giving the exact difference δ. A dimension lower bound along d=m²K² shows divergence. For reweighted sectors, total variation between the initial and shifted level distributions gives the stated endpoint/variation expression, bounded below by the maximum weight; the support and Shannon-entropy consequences follow only for this shift mechanism.
Costs: The same K=m^L copy resource and rapidly growing symmetric-space dimension as N552 apply. It establishes no matching lower bound for N368’s logarithmic rate and closes no N371 gate. The reweighting inequality concerns only this shift construction; it is not a general converse for approximate broadcasting.

N554-unitary-quotient-distortion-three-hilbert-embedding | Unitary bases modulo column permutations admit a dimension-free distortion-three Hilbert embedding
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The attached packet reports a complete written proof candidate and focused algebra check. The intake preserved and routed the source only; it did not independently reconstruct the proof, execute the supplied random numerical checks, or establish external correctness, formal verification, historical priority, or a 9-10/10 breakthrough.

Claim: For each integer d>=1, let Q_d identify U and U P for P in Sym(d), with q_d([U],[V])=min_P ||U-VP||_F/sqrt(d). Define Delta_copy e_i=e_i tensor e_i and Phi_d([U])=(U tensor U)Delta_copy U*/sqrt(d), viewed in the complex Hilbert space Hom(C^d,C^d tensor C^d) with Frobenius norm. The source proves q_d([U],[V]) <= ||Phi_d([U])-Phi_d([V])||_F <= 3 q_d([U],[V]). Thus this quotient metric has a Hilbert embedding with distortion at most 3 uniformly in d. For a finite irreducible reversible Markov kernel with spectral gap gamma, this yields the stated squared-distance Poincare bound with factor 9/gamma; a separate conductance bound controls unsquared distances with factor 3/h.
Interface: The quotient is by the right action U~UP of permutation matrices only; it is not a quotient by monomial matrices or phases. q_d is normalized Frobenius distance after optimal column matching, not its square. Delta_copy is the copying map and is local notation. The Poincare consequences assume a finite irreducible reversible kernel and its stated spectral-gap or conductance convention.
Proof spine: The copying map is invariant under simultaneous permutation of its basis labels. For the lower distortion bound, expand the mixed tensor difference; |U_ij|^2 is doubly stochastic, so Birkhoff averaging bounds its assignment score by the nearest permutation trace score. For the upper bound, telescope the three unitary factors and bound each term by ||U-P||_F. Apply the ordinary Hilbert-valued Poincare inequality to Phi for the squared-distance consequence; use scalar level sets and Gaussian projections for the unsquared version.
Costs: The displayed map has d^3 coordinates and can be evaluated directly; the proof requires neither Haar integration nor a nearest-permutation algorithm. No cost or algorithmic guarantee for the subsequent repair/stability applications follows from this embedding alone.
Failure: The theorem uses exact orthonormal bases and permutation matching; it does not extend as stated to arbitrary matrices modulo column permutations. The copying-comultiplication encoding is established prior art. A dimension-free quantitative estimate does not by itself supply an efficient permutation repair or establish the broader Aldous-Lyons application.
Closest comparator: Coecke-Pavlovic-Vicary establish the copying-comultiplication basis encoding. The attached focused comparison says the checked Auddy-Yuan real odeco perturbation interface does not directly yield the normalized Frobenius estimate, while leaving priority unresolved. Chapman-Lubotzky Section 6.4 is the cited quotient-Poincare motivation.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the global lower and upper distortion bounds with the stated quotient convention, then verify both graph Poincare consequences and complete a version-aware prior-art review of the quantitative estimate.

Claim: Let G be a finite group, S a generating list sampled with weights mu, rho:G->U(d) an exact representation, and P_s prescribed permutation matrices. Put delta^2=E_s ||rho(s)-P_s||_F^2/d. On Hom(C^d,C^d tensor C^d), define R(g)A=(rho(g) tensor rho(g))A rho(g)* and let Pi project onto the invariant subspace. If E_s||R(s)A-A||_F^2 >= kappa||A-Pi A||_F^2 for every A, with kappa>0, then an exact action h:G->Sym(N) exists with d<=N<=(1+197316 delta^2/kappa)d and E_s d_h(P_s,h(s)) <= (1+330354/kappa)delta^2. Here d_h charges every added label: it is one minus the fraction of the N labels agreeing with the original d-label input.
Interface: An exact finite-dimensional representation rho and a uniform mixed-copy energy gap are supplied hypotheses. The original permutation matrices are compared with the representation in normalized Frobenius square. d_h counts added labels in the denominator N; no compact-group or Haar-selection step is used.
Proof spine: The three-factor estimate from N554 bounds the copying vector defect by 9d delta^2. The gap controls its distance from invariant vectors; exact invariance yields an approximate map from the finite group to permutations. The multiplicative defect is at most 18 eta^2. Apply the finite-source Becker-Chapman theorem and track both degree growth and generator error, retaining the added-sheet charge.
Costs: This is an existence theorem, not an efficient repair algorithm. Enumerating the finite group may be much more expensive than reading its presentation. It requires an exact representation and a gap; approximate permutation generators alone do not furnish that representation.
Failure: No efficient algorithm or polynomial presentation-time guarantee follows. The conditional rounding theorem does not itself produce rho or prove the energy gap for an arbitrary group. Compact/Haar extensions are unnecessary and are not part of the stated proof.
Closest comparator: The attached source invokes Becker-Chapman Theorem 1.2 only in its finite-source case. N554 supplies the quantitative three-factor quotient estimate used in the argument.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the invariant-vector defect, constants, finite-source approximate-action repair and charged-degree bookkeeping; verify that every use of the supplied exact representation and energy gap is explicit.

Claim: Let C be a binary linear code of length L, dimension k and relative distance Delta_C>0, and G=F_2^L/C^perp with its L coordinate generators. Suppose the specified finite presentation and relation distribution have a unitary stability modulus f in the source precise sense: relation defect epsilon yields an exact representation rho:G->U(D), rank-r partial isometry w:C^d->C^D and eta=f(epsilon), with average_i ||U_i-w*rho(s_i)w||_F^2/d<=eta and both normalized rank deficits <=eta. For epsilon<=1/2, the attached derivation gives flexible permutation stability with F(epsilon)=min{1,2,000,000 f(2epsilon)/Delta_C}; where the second entry is below one, an exact action on N>=d labels has N<=(1+2,000,000f(2epsilon)/Delta_C)d and average generator error at most 2,000,000f(2epsilon)/Delta_C in the charged metric. For the CVY v2 Reed-Muller/Hadamard application, the reported modulus retains its q^(-c) floor and its separate presentation-dependent linear alternative.
Interface: The finite code presentation, coordinate generator distribution and relation sampling distribution are fixed as in the cited CVY Theorem 4.1. The unitary input guarantee includes both partial-isometry rank deficits; their dimension changes are charged before applying N555 with the character gap kappa=4Delta_C. For larger error the trivial action is the stated fallback. Delta_C denotes code relative distance, not N554 copying map.
Proof spine: Convert normalized Hamming relation error to the unitary Frobenius convention, use the code minimum distance to give every nontrivial character energy at least 4Delta_C, and apply the N555 mixed-copy rounding theorem. Embed the finite-dimensional partial-isometry corner in a common coordinate space, extend missing coordinates trivially, and charge all added labels. Substitute the source CVY parameters and preserve the additive q^(-c) floor.
Costs: This is a stability/existence transfer, not a polynomial-time decoder. The stated presentation is quasi-polynomial in k for the concrete sequence; the packet does not meet the sharper polynomial-in-k presentation target. No uniform floor-free poly(log k) epsilon^b guarantee for every positive epsilon is established.
Failure: Do not erase the additive q^(-c) term, the separate presentation-dependent linear alternative, or the charged added-label convention. This does not establish arbitrary-code permutation testability, a non-sofic group, or the random-complex first-stage repair. It is conditional on the precise external CVY and Becker-Chapman theorem interfaces.
Closest comparator: The packet cites Chapman-Vidick-Yuen arXiv:2311.04681v2 Theorem 4.1 and Becker-Chapman arXiv:2005.06652v1 Theorem 1.2, and compares its motivation with Chapman-Lubotzky arXiv:2311.06706v3 Section 6.4. The source notes the permutation presentation problem was described as open in the cited July 2026 CVY version; current priority is not established here.
Open verification: Independently check the exact CVY unitary modulus and relation distributions, finite-dimensional corner and rank charges, code character gap, all constants in the common-space transfer, and the parameter/error regime without removing the additive floor; then review later prior art.

N557-amplifier-entropy-photon-number-inequality-internally-reviewed-candidate | A complete internally reviewed candidate proof targets the independent-input all-finite-mode amplifier entropy photon-number inequality
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The campaign reports a complete written proof candidate after three end-to-end model-assisted internal reviews; the reviewers identified repairs that were applied and reported no remaining blocking gap. This intake performed static source/archive checks only and did not execute research scripts or independently reconstruct the mathematics. External correctness, formal verification and historical priority remain unresolved; no independently established 9-10/10 breakthrough is claimed.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Let n>=1 be finite, G>1, and rho_A,rho_B be independent n-mode states of finite mean total photon number; internal entanglement among the n modes of either input is allowed. For the retained output gamma_G of the quantum-limited phase-insensitive amplifier with c_j=sqrt(G)a_j+sqrt(G-1)b_j^dagger, define g(x)=(x+1)ln(x+1)-x ln x and \mathcal{N}(rho)=g^(-1)(S(rho)/n), with natural-log von Neumann entropy. The manuscript presents a complete written proof candidate for \mathcal{N}(gamma_G(rho_A,rho_B)) >= G \mathcal{N}(rho_A)+(G-1)(\mathcal{N}(rho_B)+1). Independent product thermal inputs attain equality; uniqueness is not claimed.
Interface: Both input groups have the same finite mode count n and form a product state across groups; no product assumption is imposed within a group. The gain is finite and greater than one. The claim does not include correlated A/B inputs, shared quantum references, infinite mode count, or an acquired experimental channel/state interface.
Proof spine: The source reports a corrected multiplier-invariant four-weight interpolation argument; explicit finite-composition weighted Fock-domain and generator estimates for the non-passive squeeze; regularized negative-minimum and signed thermal-metric steps; defect cancellation; and a thermal recurrence/limit passage. The assembled manuscript contains the complete candidate and an attributed interpolation appendix. Three end-to-end model-assisted reviewers requested repairs; the source reports those repairs applied and no remaining blocking gap.
Costs: This is a universal information inequality candidate, not an algorithm for acquiring entropy, preparing states, calibrating a channel, or experimentally testing the claim. The source does not establish a finite sample requirement, physical acquisition protocol, uniform infinite-mode or infinite-gain result, or uniform numerical runtime.
Failure: The target is not externally accepted or independently validated by this intake. No proof assistant formalization or kernel replay for the active-channel extension is supplied. Internal reviewer agreement is not external correctness or historical priority. Secondary mutual-information, pure-input entanglement and Holevo consequences are conditional on the candidate theorem.
Closest comparator: The campaign identifies the amplifier form of the entropy photon-number conjecture of De Palma-Mari-Giovannetti and distinguishes the pinned September 2026 passive beam-splitter result and weaker entropy-power results. The interpolation appendix is attributed to the pinned OpenAI Math manuscript; it is not claimed as a new invention.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the fixed finite-gain amplifier proof from the source-complete manuscript, especially the corrected multiplier-invariant four-weight interpolation and its passage through the infinite-dimensional variational minimum; then seek external specialist or proof-assistant scrutiny and source-complete priority review.

body:
N558-exact-amplifier-interpolation-and-dilation-counterexamples | Exact counterexamples delimit the amplifier proof assumptions and refute a stronger phase-space dilation shortcut
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The source reports exact derivations and a portable exact-arithmetic replay receipt. The receipt and code are preserved but were not executed or independently checked in this intake. These examples delimit assumptions and refute a shortcut; they do not establish the main amplifier theorem or a historic-scale discovery.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: The campaign reports four scoped counterexample boundaries: (i) without multiplier-invariance of the source test space, an abstract four-comparison interpolation implication fails (the reported comparison is 296650/101277 versus 248/75), while the physical application uses the invariant test space; (ii) reversing the creation-port thermal orientation is necessary, with the correct scalar comparison 103/72<=105/62 and incorrect all-down comparison 133/72>105/62; (iii) independence of the two amplifier inputs cannot be dropped, even for separable classical coherent-state correlations with amplitudes sqrt(G-1)z and -sqrt(G)conjugate(z) that cancel the retained displacement, leaving output tau_(G-1) while the purported bound exceeds it by 2G(G-1)Var(z); and (iv) for rho=diag(15,74,11)/100 and phase-space dilation parameter t=3/2, an exact rational photon-law and entropy enclosure, using the one-mode convention \mathcal{N}(rho)=g^(-1)(S(rho)), gives \mathcal{N}(D_(3/2)rho)<(3/2)(\mathcal{N}(rho)+1/2)-1/2, violating the stronger universal physical-endpoint dilation entropy inequality by more than 0.0322153811310172 nats. The dilation counterexample does not refute the physical amplifier EPnI.
Interface: Each falsifier is local to the stated abstraction or assumption. The multiplier example refutes a bare lemma without the required invariant test-space hypothesis, not the corrected physical application. The creation-port example fixes scalar data and compares orientations. The independence example uses correlated inputs, outside N557 assumptions. The dilation example is a positive endpoint state construction, not a claim that intermediate dilation maps are physical channels.
Proof spine: The source supplies explicit exact scalar witnesses for missing multiplier invariance and port orientation, a coherent-state correlation construction that cancels the retained displacement, and a three-level rational input whose phase-space-dilated photon probabilities are q_m=16(198m^2+324m+1)/(3125*5^m). The report cites rational logarithm enclosures and a geometric-polynomial tail bound for the strict entropy comparison. Portable receipts are preserved but were not rerun here.
Costs: The counterexamples are explicit analytic/rational constructions with finite exact checks. Their ingestion cost was static file and archive verification only. The large campaign worker count is provenance, not proof or novelty evidence.
Failure: None of these examples refutes the corrected independent-input finite-mode amplifier candidate. The dilation example refutes only the stronger shortcut. The correlated-input example is outside the theorem contract. All exactness and replay claims remain source-reported at intake.
Closest comparator: N392 already records a phase-space nonpositivity obstruction; N15 records a distinct conditional/reference obstruction. These new examples refine those scopes and the interpolation/creation-port interfaces without invalidating N388-N392 or the unconditional amplifier target.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct each exact witness, the rational entropy enclosure and the counterexample-to-target scope boundaries; verify that the repaired candidate does not rely on the refuted abstract statement or dilation shortcut.

N559-positive-hazard-support-peeling | Positive departure hazards expose sparse reactant supports under exact reset and endpoint access
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The attached source reports conditional derivations and internal checks. This intake preserves the source and routes scoped claims only; no research code or receipt was executed, no independent mathematical reconstruction or external/formal verification was performed, and historical priority remains UNKNOWN. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For a nonexplosive stochastic mass-action CTMC with at most R non-null reactions, input order at most k, positive rates bounded below by known kappa_min, and the stated deterministic reset interface, let x(S)_i=M 1[i in S], M=max(k,1). The infinitesimal departure hazard is q(S)=sum_{A subseteq S} theta_A, hence q(b)=sum_A theta_A product_{i in A} b_i is a nonnegative sparse multilinear polynomial whose nonzero monomials identify exactly the distinct reactant supports. The source gives PositivePeel using O(R[(k+1)log(d+1)+2^k]) exact correlation/point-query types.
Interface: d labeled species; known bounded input order k, rate floor kappa_min, rate ceiling, and controlled exact molecule-count resets; complete labeled destructive endpoint states and calibrated short observation times. Duplicate reactions sharing a reactant support are aggregated at this stage. Randomized finite-sample recovery additionally assumes independent runs, known rate/resource bounds, and no hidden species or readout noise.
Proof spine: The t-downarrow-0 departure rate is a positive sum of enabled channel propensities. On binary occupancy masks it is a sparse nonnegative multilinear polynomial. Positive Fourier differences D(B,H) test for an extension support; binary peeling recovers a maximal support, and Boolean Möbius inversion extracts its aggregate coefficient before subtraction.
Costs: The query count is not experiment count: each correlation is estimated from short-time endpoint samples. Finite-sample guarantees depend on kappa_min, time bias, rates, R, k, ell and confidence. Very small rates, high order, reset fidelity, complete counting, computation, sample volume and raw-data retention may dominate.
Failure: Support recovery does not identify product complexes or separate channels with identical reactant and product complexes. It excludes null reactions; exact controlled resets and complete state observation are essential. The attached note provides no supporting code or run receipts, and does not establish realistic cell-scale acquisition.
Closest comparator: Positive sparse polynomial and weighted-hypergraph reconstruction are established neighboring problems; the attached note explicitly does not claim an optimal decoder or novelty of those ingredients.
Open verification: Independently review the positivity/peeling proof and its finite-sample thresholds, then identify a physically justified reset/readout interface with a complete acquisition and noise budget.

Claim: For each nonzero net jump nu, the infinitesimal endpoint intensity has the finite expansion j_nu(x)=sum_alpha kappa_(alpha,alpha+nu) product_i binom(x_i,alpha_i). For every candidate alpha with |alpha|_1<=k and alpha+nu>=0 coordinatewise, the aggregate coefficient is isolated by the multivariate forward difference (Delta^alpha j_nu)(0). Under bounded reaction orders and the source interface, this identifies observable directed reactant/product complexes and their aggregate rates.
Interface: Uses the same exact-reset, independent-run, complete labeled endpoint, calibrated-time stochastic mass-action contract as N559. It concerns infinitesimal jump intensities reconstructed through short-time endpoint laws; no reaction-event trajectory is assumed. Finite-sample rate recovery is epsilon-accurate under an explicit positive rate floor and known bounds.
Proof spine: Expand each jump intensity in the binomial/Newton basis. The identity Delta binom(x,a)=binom(x,a-1) makes evaluation at zero after Delta^alpha isolate the coefficient at alpha. The displayed alternating finite sum gives the inversion.
Costs: Candidate seed states scale as (k+1)^k per recovered support; endpoint sample costs depend on short-time bias, confidence, rate floors, number of possible jumps and full-state readout. The source provides conservative batch and arithmetic bounds, not a cost-free exact real-rate oracle.
Failure: Net-zero reactions are invisible, identical (alpha,beta) channels are only recovered through summed rates, and incomplete/latent species observation invalidates the contract. Theorem concerns non-null bounded-order channels; no simultaneous estimation of arbitrary hidden rates is claimed.
Closest comparator: Finite differences in the binomial basis are standard. The contribution claimed by the source is their use with positive-hazard support peeling and a fully charged active endpoint interface, not a new difference calculus.
Open verification: Independently check the short-time bias and union-bound constants, and assess whether realistic endpoint assays can recover all labeled non-null jumps at the required precision.

Claim: Within the report’s weak-coupling collision functional and susceptibility chi^R(q,E,T)=Z/[f(q)+A T^alpha W(E/T)], suppose the current-weighted soft volume N_W(epsilon)=integral W_x(q) 1[f(q)<epsilon]dq is regularly varying as C_W epsilon^nu with 0<nu<2. Subject to its stated smoothness, ultraviolet and transport assumptions, the resulting conditional law is Delta rho(T) ~ C_rho T^[1+alpha(nu-1)]. It is a model-conditional asymptotic, not a conductivity theorem for an arbitrary interacting lattice Hamiltonian.
Interface: Temperature is measured in energy units (k_B=hbar=1); W_x is the nonnegative current-relaxation weight, distinct from the susceptibility scaling function W. A smooth-band weak-coupling description, equilibrated bosonic modes with a specified momentum sink, matched neutron-visible/electron-coupled response, and collision functional controlling resistance are assumptions, not acquired facts.
Proof spine: Rescale energy E=T x and soft stiffness epsilon=A T^alpha y in the Stieltjes spectral integral. Regular variation gives the transport spectrum scale T^[alpha(nu-1)]; inserting it into the stated thermal collision integral contributes the extra factor T.
Costs: The exponent depends on alpha, nu, the current vertex and model assumptions; it is not a universal amplitude or material prediction. The report quotes the measured alpha as an input, but does not acquire or reanalyse raw neutron/resistivity arrays or fit a new mechanism.
Failure: No experimentally established mechanism follows. Cold parallel conduction, vertex zeros, multiband effects, electron feedback, drag and the momentum sink can change or invalidate identification of the collision functional with measured resistivity.
Closest comparator: Soft-mode phase-space scaling and fractional critical susceptibilities have prior literature according to the report. No historical priority or new law claim is made.

N562-strange-metal-soft-mode-microscopic-attempt-failure-boundaries | The proposed J1–J2 strange-metal soft-mode explanation fails its current-weight and lattice tests
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The attached report presents a conditional transport calculation and a failed material-specific mechanism attempt. No raw experimental arrays were acquired or reanalysed. This intake preserves and routes the report only; source-reported internal numerical checks were not rerun, external review and historical priority are unresolved, and no new physical law or historic-scale breakthrough is established.

Claim: For the specified scalar cubic J1–J2 exchange trial, J1=4J2 gives a quartic R-point line junction: unweighted soft volume scales as epsilon^(3/4), which under the report’s alpha=0.88 conditional formula suggests T^0.78. A forward intraband current weight proportional to |k| instead yields N_1(epsilon)~(3pi/2)epsilon log(1/epsilon), hence Delta rho=C1 T log(T0/T)+C2 T+o(T), not a pure leading T law. Separately, at J1=2J2 the two-coupling scalar spectrum cannot make R and X both minima; a J3 example gives competing isolated minima, and a force-balance model shows a fluctuation spectrum alone is not a resistance mechanism.
Interface: These are scoped calculations for the displayed scalar exchange, smooth-band and force-balance models. The J1–J2 lattice is a trial model rather than an established microscopic model of Ce3Pd20Si6; the actual band, internal multipolar structure, electron-coupled operator, vertex, incommensurability and momentum sink remain unresolved.
Proof spine: Factor the exact exchange polynomial at J1=4J2; compute the quartic junction volume. Then include the current-vertex weight in a finite-cutoff soft-volume integral, whose m=1 term has a logarithm. Compare R/X corner energies for the J1=2J2 candidate and use coupled drift force-balance to expose dependence on momentum relaxation.
Costs: The report’s scale and exponent calculations are conditional. No raw arrays, residual-resistance fit, joint covariance, confidence interval, or material-specific coupled transport calculation was performed. Source-reported numerical diagnostics were not rerun by this intake.
Failure: Does not exclude other Kondo-breakdown or nonperturbative explanations. The J3 counterexample refutes the inference that competition alone forces a soft continuum; it is not an empirically validated replacement model.
Closest comparator: Soft-mode transport, frustrated exchange, current-vertex corrections and drag have prior literature as cited in the report. The calculations are restrictions and failure tests, not a novelty claim.
Open verification: Obtain a controlled microscopic derivation tying measured fluctuations to current-relaxing modes and a momentum sink; acquire and analyse the relevant raw neutron and resistivity data before testing a material-specific prediction.

status=source_derived_unreviewed; This is an unresolved proof investigation. Its two proposed sufficient inequalities remain unproved, and its exact finite computations and counterexamples are source-reported only; the referenced code and receipts were not attached or rerun. Claim: For a finite union-closed family F, descending-frequency coordinate order defines S(F)=sum_i(2p_i-1)H(X_i|X_1,...,X_(i-1)); a separate first-difference pair count defines C(F)=sum_i(2c_i-|F|)D_i. The source proves that either universal nonnegativity assertion would imply Frankl’s half-frequency conclusion, but neither assertion is proved. An exact three-member chain refutes the proposed permutation-averaged symmetric-weight precursor; a concrete map used toward C is noninjective. The unrestricted conjecture remains unresolved in this investigation.
Interface: Finite family of subsets of [n], closed under pairwise union and containing a nonempty set; X is uniform on F, c_i and p_i are coordinate frequencies. Entropies are in bits. Assertions S and C are candidate sufficient inequalities only, not established theorems.
Proof spine: Use the entropy chain rule and nonnegative conditional entropies to show S>=0 would preclude every p_i<1/2. For C, count ordered distinct pairs by first differing coordinate. The symmetric-weight precursor is evaluated exactly on a chain; a separate proposed injection has two distinct inputs with identical outputs.
Costs: The implication from S or C to Frankl is mathematical if its premise is established; that universal premise is the missing step. Finite tests through n=5 are source-reported only and do not prove either inequality for unrestricted n.
Failure: Does not prove or refute Frankl, does not establish S or C, and does not show every approach to those inequalities is impossible. The n<=5 enumeration and independent implementation were described but their code and receipts were not attached or rerun.
Closest comparator: The report’s selective comparisons cover contemporary lower bounds and related entropy/coupling work. The candidate inequalities’ historical originality is not established; prior art was not exhaustively reviewed.
Open verification: Find a valid union-closure argument controlling one of the globally weighted quantities, or construct a counterexample to S or C; then obtain independent proof and priority review.

status=source_derived_unreviewed; The packet reports complete written derivations under stated hypotheses, finite diagnostics, and an imported Bourgain–Gamburd spectral-gap theorem for the concrete SO(3) instance. Claim: For compactly supported probability measures eta<=cx mu on R^d, let gamma_r=N(0,r^2 I), f_mu=mu*gamma_r and E_r(mu)=D(f_mu||gamma_r), using the same Gaussian for smoothing and reference. The source proves E_r(mu)>=E_r(eta)+D(f_mu||f_eta). The matching-reference condition is essential; this is not monotonicity of arbitrary relative entropy or of mutual information alone.
Interface: Convex order uses all finite convex test functions; measures are compactly supported and r>0. Gaussian reference covariance matches the smoothing covariance exactly.
Proof spine: Write log(f_eta/gamma_r) as a log-Laplace transform, hence a convex function. Gaussian addition preserves convex order, and subtraction of the two relative entropies gives the claimed nonnegative integral plus D(f_mu||f_eta).
Costs: This is an analytic lemma, not a low-cost convex-order decision procedure. The source identifies convex order and reverse KL triangle inequalities as established neighboring ideas; originality of this exact formulation remains uncertain.
Failure: Changing the reference Gaussian breaks the claim; mutual information alone can move in the wrong direction under mean-preserving compression. The source includes explicit counterexamples. This intake did not reconstruct the proof.
Closest comparator: Convex order and reverse KL triangle inequalities have prior literature cited in the packet. The source does not claim those ingredients as new primitives.
Open verification: Independently check integrability and convex-order steps, then compare the exact matched-Gaussian inequality against prior formulations and identify a theorem-level consequence beyond this lemma.

Claim: Let A be a finite subset of SO(3) with positive gate law nu and sphere averaging operator Q. Under the absolute L2 spectral-gap condition ||Qf||_2<=lambda||f||_2 for mean-zero f, lambda<1, the source defines F_m(T) as the supremum l1,2 operator norm over arbitrary time-inhomogeneous m-by-m row-stochastic positive lifts and proves F_m(T)<=2 exp(-c_nu T/m), c_nu=(1-lambda^2)log(2)/98305. For m>=16 a fixed lift gives (1-8/m)^T<=F_m(T), so 1-rho_m=Theta_nu(1/m).
Interface: Gates are drawn independently from the fixed positive law. Every row-stochastic transition may depend on the current gate and time; no commutativity, reversibility or stationary-kernel assumption. The theorem is conditional on the stated spectral gap; concrete constants are not optimized.
Proof spine: A matched-Gaussian convex-order Lyapunov controls the evolution of the conditional-mean measure for every stochastic encoder. A spherical isoperimetric/profile argument and accumulation over time yield the upper bound. A polytope containing the ball supplies a fixed positive lift with eigenvalue 1-8/m for the lower bound.
Costs: The result bounds an operator profile, not total runtime, memory bits, precision, or data acquisition. The constant c_nu is small and nonoptimized. The external spectral gap needed by the concrete gate corollary is separate and imported in the packet.
Failure: A one-step contraction claim is false for finite alphabets: F_m(1)=1 for m>=5. The proof requires accumulation. No gap-free uniform polynomial rate follows from density alone; the packet gives a Liouville rotation counterexample.
Closest comparator: Positive realizations, convex order, joint spectral radius, spherical geometry and related memory results are established areas. The exact quantified bridge’s priority is UNKNOWN; no foundational novelty is established.

Claim: For a finite orthogonal gate alphabet in a finite-dimensional real space, with all gate weights positive and the identity included, the source proves rho_m=1 if and only if the generated group has a nonzero unit-vector orbit of size at most m. A dense SO(3) action therefore has rho_m<1 for each fixed m, even without a quantitative spectral gap; this argument gives no rate as m grows.
Interface: rho_m is the asymptotic growth rate of the stated positive-lift operator family. The identity gate and strictly positive weight for every alphabet member are part of the theorem. It does not cover arbitrary action sets or signed implementations.
Proof spine: A finite orbit gives a permutation lift and nonzero fixed dual vector. Conversely, compactness attains a finite-horizon norm-one maximizer; equality forces each active conditional direction to be deterministic. Identity and positive gate weights give nested active direction sets, and a repeated finite set yields a gate-invariant orbit.
Costs: Qualitative fixed-m contraction does not quantify 1-rho_m. The source’s separate spectral-gap theorem is needed for the quantitative Theta(1/m) result.
Failure: The assumptions on identity and positive weights cannot be silently omitted. This intake has not independently checked the compactness/equality argument.

The source proves nu<=cx mu if and only if Phi_(r,eta)(nu)<=Phi_(r,eta)(mu) for all such probes. Claim: Let C be a nonzero closed convex semialgebraic cone of completely positive maps on M_d, invariant under arbitrary CP pre- and postcomposition. The source candidate proves: if every member of C has some entanglement-breaking power, then there is N(C) such that every length-N(C) word of independently chosen members of C is entanglement breaking. Claim: For an algebraic CP map Φ on M_d let L=lcm(1,…,d). The source candidate characterizes eventual entanglement breaking by nilpotence of the cross transfer at every proper invariant corner of Φ^L; testing the d^2-th power gives a finite real-algebraic criterion. It also reports that a negative certificate yields one fixed pure qubit-ancilla input whose output remains NPT at every serial iterate, with no positive lower bound on the residual entanglement.
Interface: One algebraically presented CP map on M_d, its invariant corners after the L-th power, and associated cross-transfer maps. Exact real-algebraic input is assumed for the decision claim.
Proof spine: The period-clearing power Φ^L aligns invariant subspaces; cross-transfer nilpotence across proper corners characterizes eventual EB. The finite-dimensional Cayley–Hamilton bound reduces nilpotence to a fixed power test.
Costs: The source gives a finite algebraic test; it makes no practical complexity promise. A negative certificate fixes an ancilla input but promises no uniform positive NPT margin.
Failure: This concerns one algebraic CP map and its powers, not arbitrary nonstationary words. No robust storage or positive-capacity conclusion follows from an NPT witness whose margin may decay.
Closest comparator: The source compares exact algebraic decidability with cone criteria and retains a focused review of Sections 1–4; later source comparison and scope consequences are separate.

status=source_derived_unreviewed; Preserved source-derived candidate and its stated internal evidence only; intake did not run research scripts or independently reconstruct proofs. Claim: For d≥2 and a length-n serial word T of maps on M_d that are both completely positive and 2-copositive (CP ∩ 2-CoPos), n≥d−1, the source gives entanglement-breaking CP maps E,F with E=q_nT+F, E*(I)=T*(I), F*(I)=(1−q_n)T*(I), where q_n=[1+4√2 d²(1−1/(8d))^floor(n/(d−1))]^−(d−1). For every reference and positive joint input X, ||(id⊗(T−E))(X)||_1≤2(1−q_n) tr[(id⊗T)(X)]. For trace-preserving words, the source gives a sufficient O(d² log(d/η)) length for diamond error at most η.
Interface: Every counted serial factor must lie in CP ∩ 2-CoPos (both CP and 2-copositive); factors may vary and need not be trace preserving. The output effect is matched exactly. The conditioned-output guarantee is via the trace-relative bound for positive joint inputs, avoiding an inverse success-probability penalty.
Proof spine: A Gaussian concurrence gap supplies an explicit contraction; depolarizing repair constructs an EB component, and effect matching controls the successful output trace under postselection.
Costs: Explicit q_n above; for trace-preserving words the stated sufficient length is (d−1) ceil[8d log(8√2(d−1)d²/η)] for η∈(0,2). This is conservative and does not include an efficient measure-and-prepare decomposition cost.
Failure: An averaged PPT map does not imply each branch is CP/2-copositive. No arbitrary network or tensor-power impossibility follows. Earlier exactness barriers show approximate EB replacement alone does not settle exact EB for unrestricted nonunital words.
Closest comparator: The source credits Gaussian concurrence, Bell-flag/2-EB iteration and filtered prior results, while keeping exact arbitrary-word membership and approximation distinct.
Open verification: Independently check the concurrence contraction, CP/2-copositive branch condition, exact effect identities, trace-relative bound and constants. Compare against cited 2-EB and concurrence mechanisms before quantitative reuse.

Costs: Source claims bit work polynomial in n,p,B,w,s with conservative constants. A uniformly terminating certified implementation and practical complexity have not been demonstrated.

Costs: Four source-reported cases; the largest completed case B=8,s=20 used 125 panels and source-reported 10.415 seconds of numerical/acquisition/certificate/witness work, with separate startup accounting. The 30-second CF4 row at B=8 is censored.
