N580-dual-kernel-exact-joint-sampling | Dual-kernel lifting yields exact uniform samples under a certified collective-rank bound
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported exact sampler and conditioning proof candidate with exact finite checks and a native smoke record. Intake only preserved and hashed the packet; mathematical scripts were not run. The collective-rank promise and coordinate-specific acquisition boundary remain essential. External correctness and historical priority are UNKNOWN; status remains source_derived_unreviewed.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Let q be a prime power, A_1,…,A_m∈F_q^{p×n}, c_i∈F_q^n, and let g:F_q^p→F_q^m be efficiently evaluable. Suppose a certified integer R satisfies rank(Σ_i λ_i A_i)≥R for every nonzero λ∈F_q^m. For F(x) with rows xᵀA_i+c_iᵀ, the source derives an exact rejection sampler whose output conditioned on success is uniform over every pair in S_g={(x,y):F(x)y=g(x)}, including singular fibers. For R≥m+1, its expected number of trials is at most (1+α)/(1−α/(q−1))<3, where α=(q^m−1)q^(−R). In the pure bilinear fixed-target case c_i=0 and g(x)=b, R≥m suffices for fewer than four expected trials. For x=x_0+Pu of codimension a and a graph restriction Dy=h(x) with k independent rows, the source proves a transformed rank bound R−a−k; the <3 guarantee persists when R−a−k≥m+1.
Interface: Finite field F_q; matrices A_i and offsets c_i are supplied; g is evaluated as a supplied circuit/algorithm. The exact output domain is all satisfying joint pairs, sampled uniformly, not a chosen affine chart or only full-rank fibers. A valid collective-rank lower bound R must be certified. The stated closure covers affine restriction of x and a full-row-rank affine graph constraint on y with efficiently evaluable h; arbitrary added polynomial constraints are outside the interface.
Proof spine: For each dual λ and affine-kernel point x, the proposal/kernel factors give each admissible pair (x,y) the same one-trial probability q^(−p)/(1+α); counting the dual annihilator of F(x) yields the identical mass q^(m−p−n)/(1+α) for every solution pair. A projective union bound controls row-deficient x and supplies the expected-trial bounds. Under the stated conditioning, substitution through a right inverse and a basis for ker D transforms A_i to PᵀA_iQ and loses at most a+k rank.
Costs: Per trial: polynomially many finite-field operations in (m,p,n), one evaluation of g, exact linear-system solves, and O((m+p+n)log q) expected unbiased bits; the certified regimes give fewer than three or four expected trials. For square n×n matrices, the source gives a structured Moore-interpolation certificate R=n−s using O(n³+mn²) extension-field operations after a verified F_{q^n} representation. Field construction/search and verification are charged; the certificate is coordinate-dependent, and finding a favorable hidden basis is not included.
Failure: A high collective-rank certificate is a strong promise; individual A_i ranks do not suffice, and general minimum-combination-rank acquisition is not solved. The Moore certificate can weaken under an unknown basis scramble. Uncharged nonlinear identification can make a conditioned system empty (the alternating-matrix y=x example); rank loss and added constraints must be charged. Outside the certified regimes rejection may fail to terminate on an empty solution set, so this is not a general decision procedure or generic constraint solver.
Closest comparator: The source identifies Moore interpolation, linearized-polynomial/rank-metric bounds, and the pivot-chart triangular argument as established ingredients; it cites exact sampling for a single quadratic equation. The specific multi-constraint dual-kernel law and charged nonlinear conditioning are a targeted, unresolved prior-art question; absence from this search is not novelty evidence.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the equal-mass law including singular fibers, the projective deficiency bound, exact random-bit allocation, the R−a−k conditioning charge, and the square-map Moore certificate. Check empty-set behavior, hidden-basis degradation, all cost terms, and the exact multi-constraint prior-art boundary before reuse.

body:
N581-affine-mixture-envelope-obstruction | Affine-mixture rejection envelopes can incur exponential overhead even for an easy product target
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-derived representation-specific rejection-envelope obstruction and exact finite records; intake did not rerun code or independently verify the proof. The target has a simple exact product sampler. No general hardness or historic-scale breakthrough is claimed; status remains source_derived_unreviewed.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For π(λ)=2^(−wt(λ))/(3/2)^m on F_2^m, equivalently independent Bernoulli(1/3) bits, let Q be any mixture of at most K uniform laws on affine subspaces and assume π(λ)≤ρQ(λ) pointwise. For integers 0≤D<m and t with positive numerator, the source derives ρ≥[Pr(Bin(m,1/3)≤t)−K(2/3)^(m−D)]/Pr(Bin(D+1,1/2)≤t). For m divisible by 8 it gives the weakened bound ρ≥[1−exp(−m/288)−K(2/3)^(m/8)]exp(m/112) for a stated choice of D,t, when the bracket is positive; hence polynomial K entails exponential overhead in that regime. Separately, the simpler rank-bound affine-cover construction obeys C/Z≥(4/3)^m/K. The target itself is exactly sampled by independent bits, so this is an affine-mixture representation barrier, not intrinsic sampling hardness.
Interface: Target distribution π on F_2^m; proposal Q is a mixture of at most K uniform distributions on affine subspaces. The lower bound concerns pointwise domination π≤ρQ, the condition used for rejection sampling. The affine-cover inequality applies to the separately stated uniform-rank-cover construction.
Proof spine: For an affine subspace of dimension at most D, its target mass is bounded by (2/3)^(m−D). For higher-dimensional pieces, information-set coordinates are unbiased under their uniform law, which bounds their mass on the low-Hamming-weight tail by a Bin(D+1,1/2) probability. Remove the union of low-dimensional components from {wt≤t}, compare remaining target mass to proposal mass, and derive the displayed ratio.
Costs: No sampler cost lower bound follows: π is sampled exactly with m independent Bernoulli(1/3) bits. The source supplies an exact finite formula and reports enumeration of every affine subspace through m=6 plus exact rational examples at m=100,250,500; intake did not rerun that checker.
Failure: Applies only to mixtures of uniform affine subspace laws under pointwise domination and to the specified envelope construction. It does not rule out multiplicative factorizations, product sampling, dual-kernel sampling, or other compact representations; the example is deliberately easy to sample.
Closest comparator: The source distinguishes product sampling, affine stratification and weighted/code-like models. It makes no claim that these models or exact sampling are novel; the result is a scoped obstruction to this proposal representation.
Open verification: Reconstruct the low/high dimensional mass bounds and the finite domination formula, verify constants and rounding in the m divisible by eight corollary, and preserve the product-sampler escape when interpreting the asymptotic rejection lower bound.

N582-binary-coordinate-rank-ascent-trap | Binary single-coordinate rank ascent can stall despite arbitrarily high collective rank
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported exact counterexample family to one local rank-ascent heuristic. Finite code checks were not rerun at intake; external correctness and priority remain UNKNOWN. This is not a general hardness claim; status remains source_derived_unreviewed.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For every integer d≥2, the source constructs two matrices A_1,A_2 over F_2 with 2d+1 input coordinates and d columns such that rank(A_1)=rank(A_2)=rank(A_1+A_2)=d. At x_0=e_0 the 2×d matrix F(x_0) has rank 1; changing any one binary coordinate yields rank at most 1 (the e_0 flip yields zero), while the two-coordinate move x=e_0+e_1+e_2 yields rank 2. Thus a single-coordinate rank-ascent rule can stall despite minimum nonzero-combination rank d. The source reports exact script checks for d=2,3,5,8.
Interface: Finite field F_2; a two-output linear matrix map F:F_2^(2d+1)→F_2^(2×d), for each d≥2. The obstruction is only to procedures whose next move changes one input coordinate at a time while seeking a larger rank.

N583-thermal-attenuator-environmental-kernel-rare-mixture-obstruction | An exponential-moment seed class has an exact environmental-kernel obstruction to rare mixtures
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported internal analytic reconstruction with scoped diagnostics. This intake checked preservation only and did not run source scripts or independently audit the proof. Heavy-tail, varying-mixture and collective-code cases remain UNKNOWN; no capacity threshold or historic-scale breakthrough is claimed.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For the single-mode thermal attenuator Phi_{eta,nu}, 0<eta<1 and nu>0, set G=1+(1-eta)nu and assume eta>G-1. Let R=(eta-(G-1))/(G-1)>0. For a normalized pure seed psi=sum_{j>=0} psi_j|j> satisfying sum_{j>=0}(j+1)R^j|psi_j|^2<infinity, the source constructs a nonzero normalizable vector g_* in the kernel of the full two-mode Stinespring-environment coefficient map. For every fixed distinct normalized pure finite-energy competitor phi, define q_phi=||T_phi g_*||^2/||g_*||^2>0, with T_phi the coefficient map for its complementary output. Then rho_p=(1-p)|psi><psi|+p|phi><phi| obeys limsup_{p down to 0} I_c(rho_p,Phi_{eta,nu})/[p log(1/p)] <= -q_phi < 0 (natural logarithms), hence has negative coherent information for all sufficiently small p. The source reports this sign without a finite receiver-relative-entropy assumption.
Interface: One use of a single-mode thermal attenuator with the full complementary output, including the thermal-environment purifier. The seed is pure, finite-energy and obeys the stated exponential-moment condition; the competitor is a fixed, distinct pure finite-energy state. The mixture weight tends to zero while both states remain fixed. This does not cover competitors depending on p or general entangled block-code inputs.
Proof spine: An explicit entangled Bargmann multiplier gives a normalizable vector in the seed complement kernel; its norm is an exact weighted photon-moment expression. Contracting the same vector with a competitor produces a Wronskian f h′-f′ h, nonzero exactly when the pure states differ, so an environmental measurement leaks probability q_phi>0 only under the rare component. A binary-label conditional-entropy continuity argument gives the asymptotic negative p log(1/p) term without a finite receiver-relative-entropy assumption.
Costs: No algorithmic or physical acquisition cost is claimed. The restriction is a weighted exponential photon-number moment depending on eta and nu; the sign conclusion is for each fixed seed/competitor pair and all sufficiently small mixture weights, with no uniform threshold in p supplied.
Failure: This excludes only the stated rare binary mixtures around seeds satisfying the moment condition. Sufficiently heavy tails outside the condition, varying seed/competitor limits, faithful complementary outputs outside this class, and general collective codes remain unresolved. It does not prove zero capacity or rule out a positive rate from another family.
Closest comparator: This is a single-letter rare-mixture obstruction for the thermal attenuator. It does not alter the cited primary paper reported positive witness at eta=0.7841 or establish the capacity threshold. The proof and diagnostics are source-reported internal work, not external validation.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the normalizable Bargmann kernel and exact norm criterion, verify the Wronskian leakage and binary-label continuity argument with the full complementary channel, then map precisely which seed tails and mixture limits remain outside the result.

body:
N584-antidegradable-boundary-finite-block-energy-resource-lower-bound | Near antidegradability, high qubit entanglement fidelity requires a large energy-limited block
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported internal resource lower bound, not a capacity converse. The 1392 evaluation is source-reported; intake performed no research-code or numerical replay. External correctness and priority remain UNKNOWN.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For m uses of the single-mode thermal attenuator Phi_{eta,1}, any deterministic qubit encoder/decoder with total mean input photon number E obeys F_e <= 3/4 + |arccos(sqrt(eta))-pi/6| sqrt(3E+m). If E<=10m, eta=0.751 and target entanglement fidelity F_e>=0.99, the source reports the necessary lower bound m>=1392 channel uses. More generally, for E<=mN and F_e>=1-epsilon with epsilon<1/4, m >= (1/4-epsilon)^2/(|arccos(sqrt(eta))-pi/6|^2(3N+1)).
Interface: The channel is the memoryless thermal attenuator with bath mean photon number nu=1. The result applies to arbitrary deterministic qubit codes over m channel uses, with total average input energy E and entanglement fidelity F_e; it does not assume a maximum photon cutoff or a specific code family. The 1392 example additionally assumes average energy at most 10 photons per use and target fidelity 0.99.
Proof spine: At eta0=3/4 the channel is antidegradable, giving the qubit symmetric-extension fidelity ceiling 3/4 for every deterministic code. An angle-continuity estimate for the Stinespring beam-splitter dilation bounds the change in decoded entanglement fidelity by |theta-pi/6| sqrt(3E+m), yielding the displayed inequality and the necessary blocklength bound.
Costs: The resource variables are channel uses m and total mean input photons E; no decoder runtime, preparation procedure, maximum per-use energy, or sufficient construction is provided. The numerical threshold 1392 is a source-reported evaluation of the exact necessary bound.
Failure: This is not a quantum-capacity converse: it permits reliability with growing blocklength/energy and does not rule out positive coherent information or positive asymptotic capacity above eta=3/4. It applies to the stated deterministic qubit entanglement-fidelity task at nu=1, not arbitrary fidelity thresholds or assisted capacities.
Closest comparator: The primary source reports a positive finite-energy coherent-information witness at eta=0.7841 and antidegradability through eta=0.75; the exact threshold remains open. This finite-block resource lower bound does not extend that capacity bracket.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the antidegradable symmetric-extension bound and angle-continuity estimate for arbitrary deterministic encoders/decoders; audit the energy convention and reproduce the 1392 rounding from the exact formula without treating it as a capacity converse.

body:
N585-index-two-lattice-repetition-explicit-coherent-information-gate | An index-two self-dual lattice repetition family reduces an ideal code to an explicit integral gate
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-derived ideal-code candidate with a conditional sufficient criterion. The source-reported lattice diagnostics were not rerun and do not establish global failure. Infinite-energy ideal codewords and unproved physical transfer prevent a positive thermal-channel capacity claim.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Let Lambda_0 be a full-rank symplectically self-dual k-mode lattice of volume (2pi)^k and chi:Lambda_0->Z_2 a nontrivial homomorphism. Choose t with exp(i t^T Omega lambda)=(-1)^chi(lambda), so 2t belongs to Lambda_0. The index-two lattice Lambda_n={(lambda_1,...,lambda_n) in Lambda_0^n: sum_j chi(lambda_j)=0 mod 2} is a valid commuting lattice encoding one qubit. For additive Gaussian noise with density f_v=N(0,v I_{2k}) per block and a fundamental cell C_0, define g_lat(s)=sum_{lambda in Lambda_0} f_v(s+lambda), f_chi(s)=sum_{lambda in Lambda_0}(-1)^chi(lambda)f_v(s+lambda), r(s)=f_chi(s)/g_lat(s), and g_t(s)=g_lat(s+t). Set rho(v)=integral_{C_0} f_chi(s)^2/g_lat(s) ds and beta(v)=integral_{C_0} sqrt(g_lat(s)g_t(s)) ds. For a uniform bit T with conditional iid syndrome densities g_lat or g_t, let H_shift(n)=H(T|Y_1,...,Y_n); let H_parity(n)=E_{S_j iid g_lat} h_2((1+product_j r(S_j))/2), with binary entropy in bits. The source-defined ideal analog stabilizer decoder obeys I_c(n)=1-H_parity(n)-H_shift(n) and I_c(n)>=rho(v)^n/(2 ln 2)-beta(v)^n, so rho(v)>beta(v) is sufficient for positive ideal coherent information at finite n. At bath occupation nu=1, sender preamplification maps v=2(1-eta); however, no lattice meeting the condition near v=1/2 is supplied.
Interface: The result concerns an ideal infinite-energy lattice-code family and analog syndrome decoding for a Gaussian additive-noise channel. The transfer to the thermal attenuator uses sender preamplification with v=2(1-eta) at nu=1. A physical finite-energy code additionally requires a charged envelope, Gram orthonormalization, syndrome instrument, finite precision and cutoff-error bound; these are not established by the integral criterion.
Proof spine: A nontrivial character of the self-dual base lattice defines a half-shift t. The parity-kernel sublattice has index two and its dual yields four logical cosets, giving a pure ideal qubit repetition family. Decomposing the decoded logical error into shift and parity bits gives I_c=1-H_parity-H_shift exactly. The binary entropy series lower-bounds 1-H_parity by rho^n/(2 ln 2), while a Bhattacharyya bound gives H_shift<=beta^n.
Costs: A block of n repetitions over a k-mode base uses kn physical modes per logical qubit. For the stated additive-channel simulation the source counts a sender preamplifier and a thermal-channel use per physical mode. No finite-energy preparation, decoder precision, outer coding or runtime bound is included.
Failure: The sufficient gate rho(v)>beta(v) is not met by the reported square, rectangular and tested hexagonal lattice seeds near v=1/2; the reported image-sum values are floating-point diagnostics, not a certified global search. No actual thermal-attenuator positive coherent-information witness near eta=0.75, finite-energy transfer, or complete decoder is proved. Failure of these examples is not impossibility for other lattices or codes.
Closest comparator: This is an ideal conditional construction route, distinct from the published finite-Fock positive witness at eta=0.7841. It neither improves the checked capacity frontier nor establishes an operational or physical code. The exact threshold remains UNKNOWN.
Open verification: Reconstruct the exact syndrome identity and entropy bounds; then find a rigorously certified self-dual lattice with rho(v)>beta(v) for v<1/2, or delimit the gate, and separately establish a finite-energy encoder/decoder transfer for the actual thermal channel.

body:
N586-conditional-amplifier-entropy-photon-number-strengthening-counterexample | A finite-energy Gaussian reference refutes a conditional amplifier entropy-photon-number strengthening
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported interval-checked counterexample to a proposed conditional strengthening only. The reported five scoped replay checks were not rerun during intake. It neither promotes nor invalidates the separate unconditioned amplifier proof candidate.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Let g(x)=(x+1)ln(x+1)-x ln x and N(X|R)=g^{-1}(S(X|R)) when the conditional entropy is nonnegative. Prepare R,A by a two-mode squeeze of parameter 1/4 applied to tau_{1/2} tensor tau_{1/2}; take an independent vacuum B and apply a one-mode quantum-limited amplifier of gain G=6/5 to A,B. The source reports outward interval bounds N(A|R)>0.3895 and N(C|R)<0.6607, whereas the proposed conditional extension would require N(C|R)>=(6/5)N(A|R)+1/5>0.6674. Both conditional entropies are positive. Thus this finite-energy product-with-vacuum example refutes that reference-conditioned strengthening. The A and B input marginals remain independent and the unconditioned candidate inequality is saturated by the thermal marginals.
Interface: One mode in each amplifier port; ancillary input B is vacuum and independent of the reference-correlated A. The reference R is correlated with A by a two-mode squeezed thermal state. Vacuum covariance is 1/2 and entropies use natural logarithms. Only the proposed replacement S(X)->S(X|R) followed by g^{-1} is refuted; the independent-input unconditional theorem has no shared-reference premise.
Proof spine: The RA covariance has blocks aI,aI,cZ with a=cosh(1/2), c=sinh(1/2). Under gain 6/5, the output covariance blocks determine two symplectic eigenvalues. The source encloses S(A|R) and S(C|R) with outward intervals, then uses monotonicity of g to establish inverse bounds separated by more than 0.0067. The retained receipt reports an interval check; intake did not run the supplied mpmath code.

Claim: Let {D_n}_{n>=1} be finite-valued nonnegative functionals on strictly positive finite probability simplices, normalized by D_n(q,q)=0. Assume data processing under rectangular stochastic maps whose input and output distributions have full support, and for each fixed q assume continuity in p on the open simplex and C^2 regularity away from p=q. The source states that universal convexity of t↦D_n(p exp(tL),q) for every finite alphabet, full-support p,q and irreducible q-reversible continuous-time Markov generator L is equivalent to one alphabet-independent Ψ in C([0,infinity))∩C^2((0,infinity)) with D_n(p,q)=Ψ(χ²(p||q)), Ψ(0)=0, Ψ'(s)>=0 and Ψ'(s)+sΨ''(s)>=0. No tensor-additivity or trace-form premise is needed. As separate corollaries, tensor additivity forces D_n=c log(1+χ²), c>=0 (the order-two Rényi divergence); within that additive class, requiring D'''(t)<=0 along every finite reversible relaxation forces D=0. Under the same data-processing and regularity assumptions, convexity along every irreducible finite stationary generator, including nonreversible ones, forces D=0 without tensor additivity.
Interface: Finite alphabets, full-support row distributions p,q and rectangular stochastic maps with full-support outputs. A generator has nonnegative off-diagonal entries, zero row sums and acts by p_t=p exp(tL); q is stationary, and q_i L_ij=q_j L_ji in the reversible theorem. For each fixed q, regularity is in p only: continuity on the open simplex and C^2 away from p=q. The source does not assume differentiability at equality or regularity in q. Here n indexes alphabet size; the additive conclusion is named “order-two Rényi divergence” and is not denoted D_2.
Proof spine: Sections 2–3 derive exact refinement invariance, transverse Hessian scaling and a rare-clone curvature identity; taking the clone mass to zero forces gradient chord slopes to agree. Section 4 makes the gradient affine in likelihood ratio and establishes global constancy on chi-square level sets, including rational and irrational references. Section 5 identifies exactly the scalar convexity conditions. Section 6 solves the tensor-additive functional equation and the third-derivative obstruction. Section 7 uses nonreversible cycle generators to force the zero functional.

Failure: The main classification is finite-state and depends on data processing plus the stated p-regularity. It does not classify arbitrary divergences without these assumptions. Section 8 of the attached note separately states a regularity-free additive result on bounded Polish-space experiments, but points to a companion proof file not supplied or located; this ancillary statement is not included in the registered theorem. Claim: For every finite alphabet, let D_n be finite-valued and nonnegative on strictly positive probability distributions, with D_n(q,q)=0. Assume continuity in p throughout each open simplex, C-infinity regularity near each full-support q, and invariance under independent uninformative augmentation in both tensor orders: D_nm(p⊗r,q⊗r)=D_n(p,q) and D_mn(r⊗p,r⊗q)=D_n(p,q), without presuming relabeling invariance or full tensor additivity. If for every full-support p,q and every irreducible q-reversible continuous-time Markov generator L, t↦D_n(p exp(tL),q) is completely monotone for t>0, then and only then there is one alphabet- and q-independent power series Ψ(z)=Σ_{k>=1} a_k z^k, a_k>=0, with infinite radius of convergence, such that D_n(p,q)=Ψ(χ²(p||q)). Data processing follows from the classification and is not a premise. For s=χ²(p||q)>0 and every integer N>=1, the source gives D_{n^N}(p^⊗N,q^⊗N)>=((1+s)^N-1)/s · D_n(p,q), sharply attained by D=cχ². Thus no nonzero tensor-additive member, or member growing only O(N) under independent replication, lies in the class.
Interface: Finite-state distributions only. Each fixed q has continuity throughout the open simplex and C-infinity regularity in a neighborhood of q; no analyticity, nondegenerate Hessian or differentiability in q is assumed. Independent augmentation identities are explicitly required in both tensor orders; full tensor additivity is not assumed. Complete monotonicity means (-1)^k d^k/dt^k D_n(p exp(tL),q)>=0 for every integer k>=0 and t>0, for every irreducible q-reversible generator. The result does not cover nonreversible generators or a no-smoothness setting.
Proof spine: The proof represents each relaxation as a positive Laplace transform, then uses asymptotic spectral extraction and valid near-reset reversible generators to realize arbitrary q-orthonormal eigenbases. Positivity forces each smooth Taylor jet to be radial. A positive-measure argument recovers the global function without assuming analyticity. Independent augmentation identifies one alphabet-independent series and forces nonnegative coefficients; conversely, each monomial chi-square power is completely monotone along reversible relaxation, and the stated data processing and replication consequences follow.
Costs: No algorithmic, physical or runtime improvement is claimed. The source contains one illustrative exact third-derivative example, but its symbolic-check script was not supplied or rerun. No benchmark or empirical dynamics are involved.
Failure: Scope is finite-state and reversible, with C-infinity regularity near equilibrium and independent uninformative augmentation. It does not classify nonsmooth functionals, nonreversible relaxation, empirical or quantum dynamics, or Polish-space divergences. The exact example calculation is source-reported only; no formal proof-assistant verification or external correctness review is supplied.
Closest comparator: Compared with N587, this is a narrower profile class (nonnegative entire power series) with stronger complete-monotonicity and augmentation hypotheses; it does not assume data processing. Every profile classified here satisfies the scalar conditions of N587, but neither result is a proof dependency of the other. Do not transfer N587’s nonreversible zero conclusion to this theorem.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the Bernstein/Laplace spectral extraction, the admissible generators realizing arbitrary eigenbases, radiality of all Taylor jets, the global recovery argument without analyticity, and the augmentation step that identifies nonnegative coefficients. Check exact quantifiers and assumptions. Verify the attached note’s stated Bernstein citation edition/theorem number; the cited example checker was not supplied.

Claim: Let independent X~N(0,I_p), Y~N(0,I_n), F(x)_{i,:}=x^T A_i+c_i^T, H(x,y)=F(x)y-g(x), S(x)=F(x)F(x)^T, E_g(x)=g(x)^T S(x)^(-1)g(x), and W_g=E[det(S(X))^(-1/2) exp(-E_g(X)/2)]. The target is the Gaussian residual-disintegration/delta-conditioning law, whose x density is proportional to phi_p(x)det(S(x))^(-1/2)exp(-E_g(x)/2), followed by the Gaussian conditional Y|F(x)Y=g(x). If an explicit integer R>m and s>0 satisfy sigma_R(A_lambda)>=s||lambda|| for every lambda, then v(lambda)<=h(lambda)=(1+s^2||lambda||^2)^(-R/2). Propose lambda=Z/(s sqrt(V)), Z~N(0,I_m), V~chi-square_(R-m), accept by v/h, sample X|lambda from N(mu_lambda,K_lambda^(-1)) using the completed-square Gaussian formulas, then accept by exp(-E_g(X)/2) and draw the conditional Y. In ideal arithmetic each trial succeeds with probability W_g/C and has expected trial count C/W_g, where C=2^(-m/2)s^(-m)Gamma((R-m)/2)/Gamma(R/2).
Interface: This is the residual/delta-conditioned measure, not intrinsic Hausdorff surface measure; on regular fibers it includes the coarea Jacobian. Full-row-rank fibers are assumed almost everywhere with finite positive W_g. The singular-value lower bound and target-energy evaluation are supplied and verified inputs, not hidden oracles. For a verified uniform E_g<=beta, Jensen gives expected trials <=exp(beta/2) C sqrt(det T), T_ij=tr(A_iA_j^T)+c_i^T c_j. The zero-target theorem has the simplest interface; affine and nonlinear targets incur separate explicit correction costs.
Proof spine: The positive inverse-determinant Gaussian lift represents det(S)^(-1/2) as a Gaussian integral. Completing the square yields a positive dual density v(lambda) and a conditional Gaussian for X. The R-th singular-value condition bounds det(I+A_lambda A_lambda^T) below by (1+s^2||lambda||^2)^R, whose Student-t envelope has an explicit normalizer and exact sampler. Multiplying by the two acceptance factors recovers the stated x marginal; Gaussian projection supplies the correct fiber conditional. Tonelli and the finite envelope integral control normalization.
Costs: Exactness is stated in an ideal-real model with exact Gaussian, chi-square and uniform variates. Each trial uses finite-dimensional matrix factorizations and linear solves; expected trials are exactly C/W_g and can be large. R=Omega(m^2), aggregate near-isotropy, and a bounded target energy give a sufficient constant expected-trial regime with polynomial certificate/per-trial arithmetic. The useful orthonormal subspace U and elliptic Q are not automatically found. No uniform finite-bit, generic nonlinear, or condition-independent polynomial-time implementation follows.
Failure: Rank alone and an arbitrarily loose valid envelope do not bound useful acceptance. The scalar product-zero example has a nonnormalizable positive auxiliary envelope even when a different target construction may exist. Fourier duality is oscillatory for a nonzero target. Arbitrary nonlinear target composition can encode rare-event conditioning, so no generic acceptance bound follows. Projection of Y with an unconditioned X prior misses the determinant weight. Surface-area and delta-conditioned laws differ. These are scoped failures, not complexity lower bounds.
Closest comparator: Gaussian auxiliary-field identities, coarea/manifold conditioning, Gaussian conditional laws, Wishart sampling and MCMC determinant-cancellation precede this construction. Ellam et al. (2017) is cited as a close Gaussian auxiliary-variable/MCMC comparator. The exact combined independent-envelope formulation has unresolved historical priority; intake did not perform an independent literature search.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the residual-disintegration identity and both rejection stages; audit the R-th singular-value certificate, normalizers, singular-fiber limit and target-energy cost. Then check prior art for the exact combined theorem without conflating delta conditioning with surface-area sampling.

Claim: Let rational linearly independent p-by-n matrices A_i have Frobenius Gram H_ij=tr(A_i A_j^T), s(lambda)=lambda^T H lambda=||A_lambda||_F^2. If integer r>m satisfies the collective stable-rank bound ||A_lambda||_op^2<=s(lambda)/r for every lambda, then the homogeneous positive dual v(lambda)=det(I+A_lambda A_lambda^T)^(-1/2) obeys exp(-s/2)<=v(lambda)<=(1+s/r)^(-r/2). Either rational certificate M_p=sum_ij(H^(-1))_ij A_iA_j^T<=I_p/r or M_n=sum_ij(H^(-1))_ij A_i^T A_j<=I_n/r suffices. An exact ideal sampler proposes lambda=sqrt(r)H^(-1/2)Z/sqrt(V), V~chi-square_(r-m), accepts by v/h_r, then samples the conditional Gaussian X and projects Y onto ker F(X); its success is at least a_(r,m)=(2/r)^(m/2)Gamma(r/2)/Gamma((r-m)/2). Separately, the source states that for rational homogeneous g=c=0 inputs, a native M_p certificate and r>=4(m+1)^2 yield a finite-random-bit algorithm with W1 joint-law error<=epsilon and residual norm<=epsilon, using time/bits polynomial in input bit length, dimensions and log(1/epsilon). This finite-output theorem is not exact finite-bit equality conditioning and is not TV approximation to a continuous law.
Interface: The exact sampler assumes independent standard Gaussian prior coordinates, rational A_i, full-rank input family and a native collective stable-rank certificate. The finite-output theorem is narrower: homogeneous zero target, rational inputs, M_p certificate, r>=4(m+1)^2, rational 0<epsilon<1, independent uniform random bits, and W1 plus a residual guarantee. The theorem and the accompanying implementation are distinct evidence: the source prototype handles two 128x128 int64-numerator matrices with denominator 4096 and recomputes a native certificate r=62>=36 (m=2); arbitrary dimensions and rational encodings are not implemented.
Proof spine: The rational Gram matrix converts the span to conceptual Frobenius-orthonormal coordinates. PSD certificates bound both matrix-side operators and imply ||A_lambda||_op^2<=s/r. Concavity of log(1+u) yields r log(1+s/r)<=log det(I+A_lambda A_lambda^T)<=s; hence the Student-t envelope. Integrating the lower Gaussian bound yields the exact acceptance lower bound. The source’s finite-output proof separately charges the trial cap, normal tails, small singular values, arithmetic/coupling errors and output residual to obtain W1 control; it is a written analytic candidate, not certified by the finite examples.
Costs: The PSD sufficient verifier and per-trial matrix work are polynomial in dimensions and rational bit lengths; it is not a complete recognizer. Expected exact trials are at most 1/a_(r,m); r=Omega(m^2) suffices for a dimension-independent bound, while subspace restriction consumes up to a+b units of r. Finite-output polynomial bit/time is claimed only under the stated homogeneous theorem and independent-uniform-bit model. The included implementation is fixed-input-format prototype evidence; its three saved single draws and timings are not benchmarks and do not prove the law or uniform performance.
Failure: No arbitrary nonlinear-target or generic affine finite-bit theorem follows. A finite output cannot have TV distance below one from a non-atomic continuous target; the source correctly uses W1 and a residual bound. The stronger theorem’s one-input prototype does not establish distributional accuracy or generic matrix support. Receipt checks reuse producer code and were not rerun here. Large-rank physics use remains unestablished; the source does not claim practical speed or novelty.
Closest comparator: This extends the source’s earlier minimum-singular-value envelope in a scoped homogeneous interface; it also relates to classical Gaussian augmentation, Wishart/Student sampling and determinant-cancellation methods. The exact collective-stable-rank acquisition and finite-output combination require broader priority review; no novelty claim is established.

Claim: For D harmonic traceless-Hermitian k-by-k coordinate/momentum pairs, m=k^2-1 and G=-i sum_a[X_a,P_a], the positive dual on traceless Hermitian Lambda is v_D(Lambda)=det_R(I+L_Lambda L_Lambda*)^(-D/2). If the eigenvalues mu_a sum to zero, Weyl reduction gives v_D=product_{a<b}[1+(mu_a-mu_b)^2]^(-D), and the normalized eigenvalue density is proportional to product_{a<b}[(mu_a-mu_b)^2/(1+(mu_a-mu_b)^2)^D] on the trace-zero hyperplane. The source proves that the normalizing integral of this real-D family is finite iff D>1+1/k. In particular D=2 is normalizable for every finite k>=2, despite the generic stable-rank condition r>m failing at sufficiently large k. The gap density has a positive half-Cauchy product envelope and so an ideal-arithmetic rejection sampler exists, but no favorable acceptance scaling in k is established. The physical target is the classical high-temperature, zero-coupling harmonic Spin Matrix Theory phase-space ensemble with a common positive oscillator frequency; it is not interacting BFSS/BMN dynamics.
Interface: Here D is the number of independent harmonic matrix pairs in the physical model and is a positive integer. The integrability theorem separately extends the eigenvalue density to real D>0. k is gauge SU(k) size, independent of D. The law is residual/delta-conditioned, not intrinsic orbit-volume or Hausdorff surface measure; no additional spatial angular-momentum constraints are included. The commutator representation has structural stable rank r=Dk when explicitly supplied or accompanied by a checkable representation witness; the generic Casimir certificate alone returns only r<=D. At D=9, fixed SU(3)/SU(4) constants are source-reported, but the large-k D=9 regime is not efficient under these bounds.
Proof spine: Diagonalize Lambda. Each unordered eigenvalue pair contributes two real commutator singular directions of magnitude |mu_a-mu_b|, yielding the determinant product. Weyl’s change of variables contributes the Vandermonde square; ordered gaps give a positive density. For D=2, bounding nonadjacent factors by one and retaining adjacent Cauchy factors proves finite normalization at each k. For real D, the source proves necessity by a large-radius cone and sufficiency by ordered-gap sectors, assigning each pair to its largest intervening gap and integrating the resulting logarithmic variables; the threshold is D>1+1/k.
Costs: The gap dimension is k-1, followed by an independent Haar eigenbasis. The D=2 half-Cauchy rejection proposal establishes existence in ideal arithmetic only; its acceptance as k grows is not bounded favorably. The generic stable-rank envelope gives explicit fixed-rank constants for D=9 and SU(3)/SU(4), but r=Dk eventually fails r>m at fixed D. The finite-output theorem as originally stated requires r>=4(m+1)^2 and does not literally cover these D=9 examples; the source gives a checked fixed-(D,k) argument for r>2m with constants, but no implemented multiprecision physical sampler or practical timing claim.
Failure: Finite normalization is not efficient acquisition. The D=2 squared inverse-determinant L2 control used by the source’s finite-output argument diverges logarithmically near the origin for every k, so that precision proof cannot be extended merely by sharpening stable-rank constants. No replacement Lp or small-ball argument is proved. At fixed physical D=9, large gauge rank is not efficient under these bounds. The result is not a new physical law, quantum singlet sampler, interacting BFSS/BMN solution, or established historical novelty.
Closest comparator: The source identifies the target with Harmark–Orselli (2014) classical zero-coupling Spin Matrix Theory and distinguishes it from interacting classical matrix dynamics and Gaussian quantum thermal-circle methods. It also cites Cauchy-determinant and difference-eigenvalue-model antecedents; these citations and the physical convention were not independently checked during intake. No direct speed comparison or historical novelty evidence is claimed.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the commutator singular-value and Weyl Jacobian reduction, then audit both directions of the real-D integrability threshold including the trace-zero induced measure. Recheck the D=2 near-origin L2 divergence and the mapping to the cited Spin Matrix Theory ensemble. Determine whether a charged large-k eigenvalue proposal or replacement precision estimate exists; no polynomial sampler is assumed.

N592-rarity-uniform-product-chain-first-passage-approximation | Maximum-rate stratification gives a finite-bit approximation to rare product-chain hitting times
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source reports a complete internal proof and finite-bit specification. Intake performed static preservation and routing checks only; external correctness, formal verification, and historical priority remain UNKNOWN. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Let n independent two-state continuous-time Markov chains have rational stationary target probabilities p_i in (0,1), rational relaxation rates lambda_i>0, target-to-other rates (1-p_i)lambda_i and other-to-target rates p_i lambda_i, and the stationary product initial law. Let H be the first time all components occupy their designated joint target, with H=0 if initially there. For rational epsilon,delta in (0,1/2), the source specifies a randomized Turing algorithm outputting a nonnegative rational Hhat and proves an internal coupling claim P(|Hhat-H|>epsilon H)<=delta. Its asserted expected bit complexity is polynomial in total input bit length, n, epsilon^-1 and log(delta^-1), with no polynomial dependence on inverse target probability q^-1=(product_i p_i)^-1 or on rate ratios. It also derives sup_t |P(Hhat<=t)-P(H<=t)| <= delta-log(1-epsilon)/e. These are source-reported proof claims, not independently reconstructed by intake.
Interface: The target is one joint state and the initial law is the stationary product distribution. Only one approximate hitting time is returned. The source does not provide a trajectory, arbitrary-start hitting law, arbitrary target-set law, relative rare-tail error, exact continuous sampling, or total variation for the unquantized continuous law. Total variation is stated only for a requested finite binning with a separately charged boundary-error term.
Proof spine: The classical stationary renewal transform gives a geometric sum of exponential increments. The construction stratifies the activated Bernoulli rate sum by its maximum active rate, realizes the law as a Cox/Poisson mixture, and replaces only sufficiently large stratum sums by sample means. The finite-bit specification uses bounded dyadic uniforms, slack at the branch threshold, capped finite Poisson tables, explicit coupling budgets, and charged rational bit lengths; it avoids a Poisson oracle whose mean scales like q^-1.
Costs: The ideal-real construction reports O(n^3 epsilon^-2 log(4n/delta)) elementary increment work. The finite-bit theorem reports expected bit complexity polynomial in input bit length, n, epsilon^-1 and log(delta^-1); rare target probability and extreme rate ratios affect arithmetic representation length, not a polynomial number of simulated transitions. The source Python programs are floating-point demonstrations and do not implement or certify the finite-bit specification.
Failure: Brown’s exact stationary hitting-time representation is established prior art, and non-enumerative product-chain approximations already exist. The source only identifies the maximum-rate-stratified compressed coupling and its encoded complexity as potentially distinct; priority is UNKNOWN. Its numerical checks are finite floating-point observations, not the theorem proof. No unquantized TV or relative rare-tail guarantee follows.
Closest comparator: Brown (1974 report/1975 publication), as stated by Fill–Lyzinski, supplies the exact stationary geometric-sum representation. Horvath–Paolieri–Vicario (2025) give a non-enumerative product-chain ODE approximation. The source also credits established exponential-mixture, mixed-Poisson, and large-jump mean-replacement methods. The claimed distinction is only the combined maximum-active-rate stratification and rarity/rate-uniform finite-bit coupling bound; no priority clearance is established. Source prior-art notes: updates/CK/package/distinct_capability_20261010/04_prior_art_notes.md.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the finite-bit coupling and all probability/bit-cost budgets, then compare the exact encoded contract with the cited first-passage and mixed-Poisson literature. Keep the floating-point prototype separate from the Turing algorithm theorem.

N593-chebyshev-signed-particle-fast-forwarding-obstruction | Chebyshev fast-forwarding has exponential signed-mass cost on regular-tree walks
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The exact tree calculation is source-reported and was not independently reconstructed by intake. It rules out one stated estimator mechanism only. External review and any general fast-forwarding conclusion remain unresolved.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For simple random walk P=A/d on the infinite d-regular tree, d>=3, the Chebyshev polynomial T_k(P) has signed endpoint mass satisfying sum_y |T_k(P)(x,y)| >= [2(d-1)/d]^(k-1), for k>=1. The same witness applies in a finite d-regular graph when the radius-k neighborhood of x is a tree. Consequently any single signed-particle estimator W delta_Y with E[W 1{Y=y}]=T_k(P)(x,y) has E|W| at least this large and E[W^2] at least its square. This is a source-reported exact obstruction to the proposed signed-particle representation.
Interface: Classical simple random walk on a d-regular tree, Chebyshev first-kind polynomial, and an unbiased one-particle signed representation of the polynomial endpoint measure. The result concerns this estimator form and this local tree witness, not arbitrary access to a finite transition matrix or global algorithms.
Proof spine: At distance k, lower powers vanish and P^k(x,y)=d^-k. The leading coefficient of T_k is 2^(k-1), and there are d(d-1)^(k-1) vertices at distance k. Summing the absolute mass over that sphere gives the exponential lower bound. Unbiasedness forces E|W| to dominate the l1 norm, and Jensen gives E[W^2]>=(E|W|)^2.
Costs: For d>=3 the base 2(d-1)/d exceeds one, so the l1 mass and second-moment requirement grow exponentially with k for this representation. A positive universal-cover/nonbacktracking representation is also given, but its expected reduced path length remains linear in t for d>=3; the d=2 diffusive case is standard.
Failure: This is not a general classical fast-forwarding lower bound, a lower bound for all signed decompositions using multiple particles, or an obstruction to explicit global-state access. The separate bounded-radius locality observation applies only to local-output procedures. The broader proposed capability was stopped at this mechanism gate.
Closest comparator: The source credits established Chebyshev/nonbacktracking representations, including Apers–Sarlette quantum fast-forwarding, Alon–Benjamini–Lubetzky–Sodin nonbacktracking walks, and Biswas–Pyne–Rubinfeld local random-walk access. These works use distinct access models; the present obstruction does not subsume them.
Open verification: Test a different positive or global-access mechanism against this signed-mass obstruction without inferring a general no-fast-forwarding theorem from it.

N594-cubic-network-observability-criterion-and-canonical-minimal-model | Weighted cubic closure characterizes exact one-port recovery and the canonical minimal realization
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Complete internal derivations and a targeted internal audit are reported in the packet. No proof was independently reconstructed by intake. External correctness, formal verification, and historical priority remain UNKNOWN; no 8–10/10 breakthrough is established.

Claim: For a finite-dimensional system xdot=-Kx-diag(alpha)x^{circ3}+e_1 u, y=x_1, x(0)=0, with real symmetric positive-definite K and unknown positive alpha_i, let W be the smallest linear subspace containing e_1, K-invariant, and closed under T(v,w,z)=alpha componentwise-multiplied by v,w,z. Under the source’s exact zero-initial ordered-pulse endpoint-germ interface, known physical dimension N is globally identifiable up to hidden signed permutations fixing e_1 if and only if W=R^N. If W is proper, changing K by a positive perturbation on W-perp can preserve all input-output responses. Without a supplied N, the complete exact input-output germ determines a unique minimum-dimensional realization within the same positive heterogeneous cubic class, of dimension dim W. The source also parameterizes all larger equivalent realizations by weighted signed coordinate blocks, inactive coordinates, and arbitrary positive-definite dynamics on the orthogonal complement. These are source-reported internal theorem candidates.
Interface: The port, input/output scales, zero initial state, exact cubic constitutive law, symmetric SPD K, and positive nodewise cubic coefficients are part of the model. Observations are exact endpoint germs of ordered positive-duration pulses with amplitudes 0 and 1; exact mixed derivatives/IO word coefficients and exact Hankel/Gram rank decisions are assumed. The full-model result is modulo hidden signed permutations fixing e_1. The all-dimension minimality theorem is only within finite-dimensional symmetric-SPD positive-heterogeneous-cubic models.
Proof spine: Directional cubic derivatives yield positive atomic moment sequences whose support projections identify active coordinates without observing hidden states. Lie-bracket/observable identities construct K action and weighted triple products on paired directions; exact Gram closure recovers W and proves necessity/sufficiency. After rescaling by diag(sqrt(alpha_i)), every ternary-closed subspace is a span of disjoint signed block indicators. The quotient coefficient is alphabar_B=(sum_{i in B} 1/alpha_i)^-1, and K restricts to the canonical quotient while an arbitrary SPD operator remains on W-perp.
Costs: The source gives finite exact word-jet and adaptive positive-Hankel/Gram certificates, including when N is not supplied, but exact real derivatives, rank/equality tests and root decisions are ideal information. Conservative jet-depth bounds grow rapidly; no stable finite-noise estimator or useful physical acquisition cost follows. In general physical dimension and residual hidden dynamics are not identifiable.
Failure: A proper W leaves K on W-perp invisible; all equivalent realizations can differ in inactive coordinates, block refinements and residual SPD dynamics. Exact flatness and zero Gram residuals are not statistical tests. The source’s focused internal audit found no blocking algebraic gap under its exact class, but this intake did not reconstruct the proof; external correctness, formal verification and priority remain UNKNOWN.
Closest comparator: Nonlinear input-output identifiability, Volterra methods and signed-permutation gauges have established predecessors, including Albertini–Sontag (1993) and Vanelli–Hendrickx, arXiv:2412.08472v4. The source distinguishes known-topology or local identifiability from its exact dense/sparse one-port closure criterion and cross-dimensional minimal quotient; this is not priority clearance.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the positive-moment support recovery, paired K/T closure, cross-dimensional stopping certificate, and exhaustive weighted signed-block classification. Keep exact-word-germ identifiability distinct from finite-noise or physically acquired recovery, then assess the cited nonlinear-identification prior art.

N595-homogeneous-m-matrix-cubic-network-node-census | A homogeneous cubic law reveals physical node count from the exact one-port quotient
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source reports a complete internal census derivation. Intake did not independently reconstruct it. External correctness, formal verification, and priority remain UNKNOWN; this result does not establish practical noisy node counting.

Claim: Assume the exact model and input-output germ of N594. If every physical node has the same unknown alpha>0, K is symmetric positive definite with K_ij<=0 for i!=j, and its off-diagonal graph is connected, then each active synchrony block B has reduced cubic coefficient alphabar_B=alpha/|B|, no physical coordinates are inactive, and |B|=alpha/alphabar_B is an integer. The one-port coefficient identifies alpha, so the exact germ determines the physical node count N=sum_B alpha/alphabar_B, even though hidden internal connections/eigenvalues can remain unidentifiable. This is a source-reported exact-data consequence, not a noisy census procedure.
Interface: Homogeneous positive cubic coefficient at every physical node, irreducible symmetric SPD M-matrix coupling (off-diagonals nonpositive and connected), same zero-initial single-port input/output and exact endpoint-germ interface as N594. Unknown alpha is allowed because it is identified at the port. No finite-noise observation contract is provided.
Proof spine: The canonical quotient of N594 has reduced block coefficient alpha/|B|. Irreducible SPD M-matrix positivity gives K^-1 e_1 strictly positive; K-invariance places this vector in W, excluding inactive coordinates and mixed-sign blocks. Thus all blocks are ordinary synchronized node blocks and their multiplicities are recovered as alpha/alphabar_B.
Costs: The count follows from the exact adaptive quotient/finite-jet certificate of N594 and exact identification of reduced cubic coefficients. This does not identify hidden within-block stiffness or transverse residual dynamics, and exact integer/rank decisions do not provide finite-noise sample costs.
Failure: The common-alpha and connected SPD M-matrix hypotheses are material. Signed off-diagonal couplings can leave inactive coordinates; heterogeneous alpha can produce the same harmonic coefficient sum for different block sizes. Weak coupling makes the exact census arbitrarily ill-conditioned. The formula is not a general node-count method.
Closest comparator: Local network-size estimation can return minimal realization order while merging synchronized nodes; Tang et al., New Journal of Physics 22 (2020), 093031, is cited in the source. Brovia et al. (2026), DOI 10.1063/5.0318179, is a close modern predecessor. The proposed distinction is using the homogeneous cubic coefficient to lift a one-port minimal quotient to physical multiplicities; priority remains UNKNOWN.
Open verification: Reconstruct the inverse-positivity and signed-block argument, check both necessity counterexamples (signed couplings and heterogeneous coefficients), and search prior work on inferring multiplicities from a nonlinear minimal quotient.

status=source_derived_unreviewed; The exact contraction and generic recovery are source-reported internal derivations. No proof was independently reconstructed by intake. The campaign reports no practical advantage or external validation; historical priority remains UNKNOWN.

Claim: For the first-order model xdot=-Kx-diag(alpha)x^{circ3}+e_1u, y=x_1, with real symmetric SPD K, positive nodewise alpha_i and known dimension, the source derives an exact H1/H3 contraction. On a generic subclass with simple K eigenvalues, nonzero port modal overlaps, and nonzero pairwise-distinct hidden weights beta_i=alpha_i K_{i1}^2, the contraction B(s,t)=sum_{i>1} beta_i q_i(s)q_i(t), q(s)=(sI+K)^-1e_1, forms a symmetric matrix in the H1 modal basis whose eigenvectors recover the physical coordinates up to hidden signed permutation. The argument targets the needed contraction and does not reconstruct the full ambient quartic tensor. This remains an internally derived source candidate with an unverified acquisition interface.
Interface: Exact linear response H1 and cubic Volterra response H3 for the known first-order constitutive model, zero initial state and a single driven/measured coordinate. The original coefficient is recovered using a high-opposite-frequency limit or a finite-R extrapolation; H1 supplies modal poles and port weights. This is an exact kernel identity, not an assumption that hidden states or the full H3 tensor are directly measured at no cost.
Proof spine: The high-opposite-frequency pair separates the port contribution from hidden-node terms in H3. After subtracting the port term, the coefficient is a bilinear sum over hidden resolvent coordinates weighted by beta_i. In the H1 modal basis this is U^T diag(0,beta_2,...,beta_n)U; distinct eigenvalues of that matrix expose the physical mode rows, after which K and the nodewise nonlinear coefficients follow.
Costs: The source describes finite low-frequency evaluations after the asymptotic identity, but the first-order high-frequency route is noise-sensitive and the inverse can be exponentially ill-conditioned. No end-to-end acquisition, stable finite-noise bound, or advantage over nonlinear identification is established. The O(n^3) bounded-frequency query count belongs to a separate second-order oscillator model recorded in N597, not this first-order card.
Failure: Zero direct port coupling, repeated hidden beta values, repeated K eigenvalues or zero modal overlap defeat this particular reconstruction step but are not impossibility theorems for other kernels. High-frequency cancellation can suppress the hidden signal severely. The source’s focused prior-art review identifies parallel Wiener–Hammerstein/Volterra branch separation as a strong structural overlap; the exact physical-coordinate recovery distinction and priority remain unresolved.
Closest comparator: The source compares the cubic branch sum with parallel Wiener–Hammerstein identification and cites established Volterra/tensor methods, nonlinear frequency-response identification, and Vanelli–Hendrickx arXiv:2412.08472v4. These precedents prevent claims of novelty for branch separation or nonlinear network identifiability in general.
Open verification: Independently derive the H1/H3 contraction and the physical-coordinate recovery under every nondegeneracy condition; reconcile it with the source’s acquisition audit and compare with parallel Wiener–Hammerstein physical-parameter recovery.

status=source_derived_unreviewed; The packet contains a conditional s41 resource derivation and an h16 gate that disputes uniform stability/acquisition scope. The exact query construction is source-reported; uniform robust performance remains unresolved. No external proof or physical validation.

Claim: For the distinct second-order model qddot+gamma qdot+Kq+diag(alpha)q^{circ3}=e_1u, y=q_1, the source gives a rational-residue construction for the H1/H3 physical-coordinate matrix using 4n^3 exact cubic-kernel oracle values before symmetry savings, at bounded frequencies O(sqrt(M)) under stated spectral, overlap, coupling and damping promises. Its frozen s41 derivation also states a conditional polynomial resource bound including phase cycles, settling, noise repetitions and modal calibration. The packet’s focused h16 gate narrows this status: O(n^3) counts exact H3 kernel queries, not end-to-end laboratory samples, and it reports that a uniform Cauchy-condition bound under the stated promises is not established there. Therefore intake retains the algebraic query construction and the conditional resource claim as source evidence, while the robust uniform stability/acquisition theorem remains unresolved.
Interface: Known dimension, identity mass, known scalar damping gamma>0, symmetric SPD K, positive nodewise cubic coefficients, one real input/output port. The source’s sufficient promise uses bounded eigenvalues m<=lambda_i<=M, a known eigenvalue gap delta, modal overlaps bounded below by a_min, hidden beta separation b (including separation from zero), and gamma<=Delta0/(400n) for Delta0=min(delta/(2sqrt(M)),sqrt(m)); independent sub-Gaussian readout noise is used in its sampling calculation. H3 values are obtained by phase-cycled finite real waveforms, not supplied free by the physical device.
Proof spine: At each low-frequency pair, the third-order response is a rational function of the opposite-frequency parameter with 4n known poles. Interpolation from bounded imaginary frequencies recovers the desired high-order residue coefficient; 4n samples per each of n^2 low-frequency pairs give 4n^3 H3 kernel queries. The resulting symmetric modal matrix can be diagonalized to recover physical coordinates under distinct hidden weights. Phase cycling extracts a cubic kernel estimate from 64 real waveform runs per replicate, with a finite-amplitude remainder and settling/reset budget stated in s41.
Costs: The O(n^3) figure is exact H3-kernel query count only. The s41 source additionally claims polynomial dependence on n, spectral range/gaps, damping, overlaps, beta separation, target error and failure probability, with 64 phase-cycled runs per kernel replicate and H1 calibration. The h16 gate says the Cauchy interpolation condition number is not uniformly bounded/proved in n under its stated promises and that physical query acquisition costs are not the O(n^3) count. The campaign’s operational forecast gives no advantage over a matched physical-likelihood baseline; no physical acquisition is reported.
Failure: This is a different second-order oscillator, not the first-order model in N596. s41_primitive.txt presents a conditional conditioning/resource proof, while h16_gate.txt describes the stability result as not established and the O(n^3) count as an oracle-query count. Intake cannot resolve that source-internal tension; do not promote the polynomial uniform stability claim until the promised Cauchy bound and the exact sample/resource interface are independently reconciled. Small damping may also imply long settling. No favorable realistic sample count is claimed.
Closest comparator: The focused source review identifies parallel Wiener–Hammerstein Volterra-kernel identification as the strongest structural predecessor and describes the H3 branch representation as exactly a PWH cubic kernel, while distinguishing the physical symmetric-K recovery target. Hald’s Jacobi reconstruction, nonlinear frequency-response methods, and Vanelli–Hendrickx network identifiability are also credited for their narrower interfaces. Historical priority remains UNKNOWN.
Open verification: Resolve the s41/h16 discrepancy by proving a uniform Cauchy interpolation condition bound from the exact stated promises or weakening the claim to an algebraic oracle query count. Then acquire H1/H3 from raw scalar measurements, charge calibration, phase cycling, settling, resets, noise, drift and computation, and compare with a matched PWH/nonlinear-identification baseline.

status=source_derived_unreviewed; The proof and diagnostic/forecast record are source-reported. Intake did not reproduce them. External validation and physical acquisition remain absent; no practical advantage or foundational breakthrough is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For the source’s bounded-input weak-coupling family K_epsilon=[[a,epsilon b^T],[epsilon b,B]] and a hidden orthogonal rotation of the unobserved block, the one-port linear transfer is identical and the hidden matrices can remain O(1) apart while the port-output difference is O(epsilon^4) over the stated finite-horizon/control class. With independent Gaussian scalar readout noise of scale sigma, the source derives KL(P_K,P_Kprime)<=N C^2 epsilon^8/(2 sigma^2), hence N=Omega(sigma^2 epsilon^-8/C^2) samples for fixed-success discrimination; continuous white-noise observation charges total time in the same way. This rules out a uniform robust finite-noise recovery bound over the unrestricted generic SPD family under that interface, but does not refute exact identifiability. Separately, the source reports an n=8 conditional forecast with 145.7 million scalar samples and 32.9% K RMS error, versus a 2.59% local-oracle likelihood benchmark; these are not theorem bounds or executed global estimators.
Interface: First-order zero-initial cubic model, scalar bounded adaptive input, single scalar output, hidden-block orthogonal alternatives with equal linear transfer, stability/hidden-block lower bounds as stated in reports/s45_realization.txt, and independent additive Gaussian sample noise. The continuous-time white-noise analogue charges observation time. The finite n=8 forecast assumes supplied H1, common alpha and a specified perturbative acquisition protocol; reset/calibration and residual nonlinear costs remain unresolved.
Proof spine: Dissipativity bounds the state and makes hidden-state amplitudes O(epsilon). Rotating the hidden cubic coordinates changes the port dynamics only at O(epsilon^4). The Gaussian KL chain rule then makes the n-sample information O(N epsilon^8/sigma^2), and a two-point testing argument yields the sample lower bound. This acquisition obstruction is independent of a particular estimator within the stated observation model.
Costs: The lower bound diverges as coupling epsilon tends to zero even for O(1)-separated hidden matrices. A separate source forecast for n=8, gamma=.03, common known alpha reports 1.457e8 scalar samples and 0.32901 relative K RMS error; its local likelihood comparator reports 0.02587. This is a conditional numerical forecast, not an acquired result or universal performance guarantee. The tested n=3 first-order full nonlinear fit outperformed the cubic-truncated fit; n=5 recovery failed for both in the recorded test.
Failure: The obstruction is not a structural nonidentifiability theorem: exact germs can still distinguish the models at every positive coupling. It does not rule out stronger input/output interfaces, instance-dependent costs, or uniformly conditioned subclasses. The n=8 forecast and synthetic fits are finite/model-specific diagnostics, and the likelihood comparator is a local oracle benchmark rather than an executed globally convergent estimator.
Closest comparator: The packet compares the cubic route with full nonlinear ODE grey-box system identification, a competent matched local-likelihood benchmark, and established Volterra/PWH methods. It reports no checked practical advantage. This is a scoped operational barrier, not a claim that every nonlinear identification method requires this cost on every subclass.
Open verification: Reconstruct the uniform output-contrast and KL bounds with the exact adaptive-control/noise assumptions; preserve the distinction from structural identifiability. Then demonstrate a physically justified, globally reliable code or estimator that beats a matched nonlinear baseline after charging H1 calibration, excitation, reset, time, noise and computation.

Claim: For the report’s averaged subsystem-purity coordinates p_k=binom(4,k)^(-1) sum_|S|=k Tr(rho_S^2), it gives p=(1,7/16,3/8,1/2,1/2) and states that this vector satisfies all 53 margins in a specified relaxation. Substitution into q_4(P)=4 sum_k binom(4,k)(-1/2)^(4-k)p_k gives 4p_4-8p_3+6p_2-2p_1+(1/4)p_0=-3/8. The intake rechecked this displayed rational arithmetic exactly. The 53 constraints and checker were unavailable, so their feasibility is source-reported; no quantum state or global rank-two operator realizing this profile was found or claimed.
Interface: Four qutrit copies; normalized rank-two projection state rho=P/2; p_k is the average purity over k-site reductions. The profile is a point in a reported linear/semialgebraic relaxation, not an established quantum marginal vector.
Proof spine: The linear functional simplifies to 4p4-8p3+6p2-2p1+(1/4)p0. Exact Fraction arithmetic gives -3/8 for the displayed vector. Feasibility against the 53 constraints and compatibility with an actual global rank-two operator are separate questions and were not established by this intake.
Costs: The result is about a finite relaxation only; it has no physical acquisition or experimental implication.
Failure: This does not give q_4(C)<0 for any physical rank-two C, a distillation witness, a counterexample to the Werner endpoint, or an all-copy result. It shows only that the reported 53-margin relaxation, if accurately specified and feasible at that vector, is insufficient by itself.

body:
N601-fei-complex-phase-relaxation-obstruction | A unit-modulus complex phase family breaks a broader FEI proof relaxation, not Boolean FEI
status=source_derived_unreviewed; This is a source-derived intake from the pasted report. The referenced source ZIP and underlying research artifacts were unavailable; the report’s research checks were not replayed. No historic-scale breakthrough is claimed.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: The unrestricted target remains H(fhat^2)<=C I(f) for real Boolean f:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1}. The report gives the actual coordinate-restriction entropy increment Delta_i(f) in terms of the paired coefficients A_T=fhat(T), B_T=fhat(T union {i}), and observes that a dimension-free essential-coordinate bound Delta_i(f)<=C I_i(f) would close the usual induction; it explicitly does not prove such a bound. It also gives F(x)=product_j(sqrt(1-epsilon)+i sqrt(epsilon)x_j), for which |F|=1, H(F)=n h_2(epsilon), and I(F)=n epsilon, so the ratio diverges as epsilon decreases to zero. This F is complex-valued, not Boolean, and is not an FEI counterexample; it refutes only an attempted relaxation relying on normalization and unit modulus alone.
Interface: Boolean FEI concerns real-valued {+/-1} functions under the report’s Fourier entropy and influence normalization. The phase-family calculation concerns a complex-valued unit-modulus function and the corresponding Fourier probability/degree statistics; those are not the same theorem domain.
Proof spine: The product Fourier law has independent per-coordinate squared magnitudes (1-epsilon, epsilon), so its spectral entropy is n h_2(epsilon), while its expected Fourier degree is n epsilon. Thus h_2(epsilon)/epsilon diverges, but the construction leaves the Boolean codomain and cannot refute Boolean FEI. The proposed Boolean coordinate inequality remains an unproved sufficient route.
Costs: The example is an exact algebraic obstruction to a broader proof relaxation; no computational or experimental cost claim is made.
Failure: It does not refute FEI, prove a Boolean counterexample, or establish the essential-coordinate inequality. The older Astra card N529 concerns a different absolute-product coordinate-selection criterion and does not imply failure of the actual entropy-increment criterion stated here.
Closest comparator: The report cites the 2026 FEI paper as restricted-class work and a coordinate-splitting route, not a proof of unrestricted FEI. The intake checked its arXiv version metadata and abstract only.
Open verification: For the actual Boolean domain, either prove a dimension-free essential-coordinate bound for Delta_i(f)/I_i(f), find a distinct universal argument, or replace this route with a rigorously checked Boolean counterexample.

N602-finite-bit-rare-clock-implementation-replay-certificate | An exact-arithmetic finite-bit implementation records compressed rare-clock acquisitions
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The exact-arithmetic code, mathematical certificate, audit, fixtures and 17-test result are source-reported. This intake preserved them, checked supplied hashes and repository routing, and did not execute the code/tests or independently reconstruct the proof. The input-bit assumption, external correctness, formal verification, historical novelty and broader practical capability remain unresolved. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For four independent two-state continuous-time Markov chains with stationary product initial law, dyadic target probabilities p=(1/8,1/16,1/32,1/16), relaxation rates (1,2,4,8), and one joint target, the source provides a Python-standard-library implementation that returns a nonnegative rational approximation to the stationary first-hitting time using integer and exact-rational arithmetic. Under its stated independent-unbiased-input-bits assumption, the source certificate gives the requested instance epsilon=1/4, delta=1/20 and conservative failure bound 59429/5242880 < 0.011336. For a deterministic recorded tape, the source reports an exact rational same-tape enclosure with relative discrepancy upper bound 0.001652145 for every extension of its accepted finite uniform cells. A separate q=2^-200 fixture reports all four strata compressed using 29,401 exponential cells; one OS-backed acquisition and its exact prefix replay are also recorded. The packet reports 17 passing implementation tests and an internal code-and-mathematics audit. This is an implementation supplement to N592, not a second general theorem.
Interface: The implementation gate accepts dyadic target probabilities strictly between zero and one, positive rational relaxation rates, rational epsilon and delta, and an independent stationary product initial law for one joint target. Component i has target-to-other rate (1-p_i)lambda_i and other-to-target rate p_i lambda_i. The moderate replay uses exactly n=4, p=(1/8,1/16,1/32,1/16), lambda=(1,2,4,8), q=1/65536, epsilon=1/4 and delta=1/20. The theorem-level rational-input contract remains the broader source-reported N592 construction. Randomized guarantees assume independent unbiased bit streams; the recorded SHA256 fixtures are deterministic, and the single OS entropy acquisition does not certify physical independence.
Proof spine: The implementation preserves the maximum-activated-rate strata and Brown/Cox representation used by N592. It encloses finite dyadic-cell exponential values by rational intervals using an atanh-series logarithm, makes branch decisions with explicit slack, samples small-stratum counts through bounded exponential-arrival cells, and compresses large strata with a fixed sample mean. The certificate separately accounts for cell rejection, branch ambiguity, count caps, large-stratum concentration, finite arithmetic and output error. The code and certificate are source-provided; intake did not independently reconstruct them.
Costs: For the specified moderate preflight, the source bounds expected exponential calls by 142,884. A deterministic SHA fixture records 15,849 exponential cells and 1,619,385 input bits; the same-tape reference uses 55,468 marks. The q=2^-200 fixture records 29,401 cells and 5,313,694 bits (about 0.91 seconds on the source environment). The single OS-backed acquisition records 14,769 cells and 1,514,177 bits. These are source-reported bounds and finite measurements, not uniform wall-clock guarantees or a statistical accuracy study.
Failure: The probability bound is conditional on mutually independent unbiased input bits; finite deterministic fixtures and one OS-backed acquisition do not validate that source assumption. The exact same-tape discrepancy is specific to the recorded finite-cell extension and is not a relative rare-tail or statistical failure-rate guarantee. The implementation only admits dyadic target probabilities, even though the broader N592 theorem candidate states a rational-input result. The audit and 17-test receipt are internal source reports, not a machine-checked proof or an independent intake reproduction. There is no exact path sampler, arbitrary-start result, arbitrary target-set result, continuous-law total-variation claim, external validation, or historical-priority determination.
Closest comparator: The packet credits Brown’s stationary first-hitting-time representation as exact prior work and cites a non-enumerative product-chain ODE approximation by Horváth, Paolieri and Vicario. The source presents its proposed distinction as a finite-bit rarity/rate-uniform guarantee and a concrete exact-arithmetic realization; this intake does not establish priority or a historic-scale capability.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the N592 coupling and probability/bit-cost proof, inspect and replay the exact integer/rational implementation including the recorded SHA and OS-prefix paths, and compare its accepted dyadic input/output contract with the broader theorem statement. Keep the N592 gate open until correctness, source assumptions, and prior-art scope are independently addressed.

Claim: Use the source convention ||X||_{2,n}^2=Tr(X*X)/n even on a corner of C^n. For an orthogonal projection P, Q=I-P, U in U(n), A=QUQ restricted to Q C^n, and T=QU*PUQ restricted to Q C^n, the report gives inf_{V in U(Q C^n)} ||A-V||_{2,n}^2 = Tr((I_Q-sqrt(I_Q-T))^2)/n, between Tr(T^2)/(4n) and Tr(T^2)/n. With B=PUQ, T=B*B, so the cost is controlled by Tr((B*B)^2)/n, not rank alone. It also gives, for every integer q>=2, n=q^4 and a swap of two q^2-dimensional spaces for which an error of normalized size epsilon=q^-2 is killed by deleting an epsilon fraction, while the compressed unitary needs repair distance q^-1=sqrt(epsilon).

Claim: Suppose rho:Gamma->U(n) is an exact irreducible representation and a finite S, kappa>0 satisfy max_{s in S}||rho(s)Xrho(s)*-X||_{2,n}>=kappa||X||_{2,n} for every traceless X. The representation is exact, finite-dimensional, and irreducible; P has rank k and the normalized metric denominator remains n. Claim: Let U_s in U(n), supplied skew-adjoint corrections b_s satisfy max_s||b_s||_{2,n}<=C epsilon, and w be a relator word of length L. Define F_b(t)=w((e^{t b_s}U_s)_s), D=F_b(0)-I, and L_U(b)=F_b\prime(0). Assume E=D+L_U(b) satisfies ||E||_{2,n}<=eta. For tau,sigma>0 the report claims an exact decomposition F_b(1)-I=R_diffuse+R_debt with ||R_diffuse||_{2,n}<=eta+(L^2/2)tau C epsilon, rank(R_debt)/n<=2L|S|C^2 epsilon^2/tau^2+eta^2/sigma^2, and ||R_debt||_op<=2+sigma+(L^2/2)tau^2. Each corrected generator remains unitary and moves by at most C epsilon in normalized Hilbert-Schmidt norm.
Interface: Corrections b_s are supplied, skew-adjoint, and small in normalized Hilbert-Schmidt norm; the linearized residual E is also supplied through the assumption ||E||<=eta. The word length L, number of generators |S|, and cutoffs tau,sigma are explicit. This is not an algorithm for finding b_s.
Proof spine: The source splits b_s=l_s+h_s by spectral cutoff tau, bounds rank(h_s)/n by C^2 epsilon^2/tau^2, Taylor-expands the low-frequency path, telescopes high-frequency and inverse-letter changes into a rank-bounded term, and splits E by singular-value threshold sigma. The diffuse and debt terms are defined by that construction.
Costs: No end-to-end runtime or method for acquiring b_s is provided. For tau=epsilon^alpha the diffuse nonlinear term is O(epsilon^(1+alpha)) and rank debt O(epsilon^(2-2alpha))n, but the bounded debt may have Hilbert-Schmidt size O(epsilon^(1-alpha)), larger than epsilon.
Failure: Existence of suitable corrections, admissibility of the linear residual, and a compatible o(n)-enlargement that removes the debt are unproved. The source explicitly says this is not a superlinear total-error bound and supplies no flexible-stability conclusion.
Closest comparator: This is a conditional matrix update, not a proof of the flexible group-stability target. N607 separately records why generic low-rank debt cannot be completed for all approximants.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the spectral truncation and Taylor estimates, especially inverse letters, the 2L|S| rank factor, operator-norm debt, and the singular-value split. Then identify a justified source of corrections and a compatible completion theorem before using it for group stability.
