Claim: The report uses Gamma=BS(2,3)=<a,t | t a^2 t^-1=a^3> and v=[a,t a t^-1], nontrivial by Britton normal form but killed in every finite quotient. It states every finite-dimensional unitary representation kills v, since its finitely generated linear image is residually finite in characteristic zero, and invokes sofic permutation approximations with defining-relator rank o(n) but ||v(U)-I||_{2,n}->sqrt(2). If exact enlarged generators V_s on dimension n+m satisfy the presentation and their n-by-n compressions approximate U_s within delta in norm normalized by n, the source derives ||U_s direct-sum I_m - V_s||_{2,n}^2<=delta^2+6m/n and sqrt(2)-o(1)<=8 sqrt(delta^2+6m/n). Thus m=o(n) forces delta>=1/(4 sqrt(2))-o(1) for this obstruction.
Interface: The approximation is permutation/sofic for the stated finitely presented group; the comparator exact tuple is a finite-dimensional unitary representation. The enlarged representation has dimension n+m. The compression error and all displayed comparison norms use denominator n. The word v has length eight.
Proof spine: Finite quotients kill v; residual finiteness of the finitely generated linear image transfers that fact to every finite-dimensional complex linear/unitary representation. Sofic approximants retain v as a nonidentity word on asymptotically almost all points. Padding by I_m bounds top-left, cross, and lower-right block errors; an eight-letter telescoping estimate then gives the stated lower bound.
Costs: This is a qualitative asymptotic obstruction; no concrete efficient sofic approximation, finite presentation encoding, or computational complexity estimate is supplied.
Failure: It rules out a universal completion principle that would handle this source-reported family with o(n) enlargement and vanishing generator edits. It does not rule out completion for a restricted group class, a different correction construction, or the flexible-stability target in full generality. The cited soficity input and derivation were not checked externally.

Claim: For a central extension 1->Z->tilde Gamma->Gamma->1 with finite abelianization of tilde Gamma, the report observes H^1(tilde Gamma;R)=0. The five-term sequence contains 0=H^1(tilde Gamma;R)->Hom(Z,R)->H^2(Gamma;R); because Hom(Z,R) is nonzero and the map is injective, H^2(Gamma;R) is nonzero. Therefore a vanishing-H^2 hypothesis cannot be applied directly to this base group under these assumptions.
Interface: The kernel is infinite cyclic and central; the total group has finite abelianization; cohomology has trivial real coefficients. The conclusion is a necessary compatibility condition, not a classification.
Proof spine: Finite abelianization gives Hom(tilde Gamma,R)=0. The low-degree five-term exact sequence for the extension injects Hom(Z,R) into H^2(Gamma;R) because the preceding H^1 term is zero; Hom(Z,R) is one-dimensional over R.

status=source_derived_unreviewed; The attached note supplies a theorem proof candidate and source-reported numerical checks. This intake preserved and routed the originals and checked hashes only; no sampler or verifier was run, no proof was independently reconstructed, formal/external correctness and priority remain UNKNOWN, and no historic-scale breakthrough is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: The source states an exact sampler for the joint stationary law of any fixed finite batch of raw coordinates at specified times in a finite-depth, finite-field network whose same-level update is affine, whose deterministic forcing depends only on strictly lower levels, whose parent count is at most k, and whose site-time category has Haar-reset probability s>0. If m coordinates are requested, c is the fixed depth, h=kc^2, and Q is the number of distinct update categories exposed, its bound is E[Q] <= (m/s) sum_{j=0}^{c-1}(1+h/s)^j. The category oracle is shared across levels so reset/gate correlations are preserved. The source also gives an exponential backward-depth tail for fixed c,m,k,s. These are source-reported theorem claims, not independently reconstructed here.
Interface: States lie in F_q^c. At a site-time one shared category chooses independent uniform Haar values for all coordinates with probability s, a locally known residual reset with probability r, or a gate with probability 1-s-r. At level ell the gate is linear in level-ell parents plus a deterministic function of strictly lower-level inputs; same-level nonlinear feedback is excluded. Parent acquisition, forcing descriptions and their evaluation are charged. Rational s,r support ideal exact random-bit draws; the reference implementation covers prime q, while the note states a mathematical finite-field generalization.
Proof spine: Process same-level dependencies in descending time while tracking coefficient vectors and the span V generated by independent Haar contributions. If a coefficient lies in V, an independent uniform vector U_V absorbs any unknown contribution in V in distribution (U_V+vZ has law U_V); this is distributional masking, not pathwise coalescence. Otherwise expose the category, propagate affine coefficients, retain lower-layer forcing terms without expanding them, and recurse on lower levels using the same memoized category field. A layer induction yields exact joint laws; negative-binomial domination gives the displayed expected-query bound.
Costs: At most cQ site-layer visits and kcQ parent incidences are reported. For fixed c the source states expected arithmetic/bit cost polynomial in m,k,1/s,log q and the acquired forcing-description/evaluation costs; its exponent and constants may grow sharply with c. The source reports a failed costly million-site run at k=5,s=.09 and a completed source-reported run at k=3,s=.20. These demonstrations were not rerun by intake.
Failure: No same-level nonlinear feedback, unbounded parent access, arbitrary nonlinear cellular automaton, full-state efficient sampling, or general full-chain O(log N) mixing theorem is established. Fixed-depth is essential to the recursive bound; low reset probability and larger depth can be practically prohibitive. Exactness assumes ideal independent randomness and does not follow from the source's pseudorandom statistical checks.
Closest comparator: The source cites coupling from the past, perfect sampling for probabilistic cellular automata, algebraic decomposition of nonlinear cellular automata, and noisy-CA ergodicity results as overlapping prior art. The exact novelty of this rank-absorbing layered construction is explicitly unverified; citations were not independently checked.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the adaptive memoized-category and cross-level conditional-independence arguments, verify the negative-binomial and exponential-tail bounds including forcing acquisition costs, and perform a full prior-art review before treating this as a theorem or novelty claim.

Constants may depend on the fixed observable batch and model parameters.

For multiple requested observation times, their prescribed separation must be accounted for separately; the simple terminal-time local mixing bound is not a global joint mixing guarantee.

The finite-depth rank/masking certificate closes before a random ancestry horizon with exponential tail and makes a target cylinder's law independent of all initial values on that event. The remaining total-variation discrepancy is bounded by the tail event; hence invariant measures agree on every finite cylinder and are equal.

Claim: For a closed glutamate pool with symmetric isotope-independent racemization, each isotope-class handedness imbalance m_j contracts by the same factor e^(-2K), and positivity implies 2K <= -ln(max(|e_14|,|e_15|)). The report converts the three published central values to e_14=0.0527903 and e_15=0.0175575, giving at most 4.24 handedness-halving times under this model. For a racemic background plus one L-biased source followed by isotope-independent racemization, the source's heavy-nitrogen fraction is q_excess=(q_L-d q_D)/(1-d), with d=D/L; the central measurements imply delta15N_excess about -590.5 per mil. A fit with a typical-range source remains compatible with individual quoted spreads after modest shifts, so the central-value inference is not a calibrated exclusion.
Interface: Mix isotope delta values only after conversion to heavy-atom fractions q=R/(1+R), R=R_AIR(1+delta/1000). The racemization inequality assumes a closed pool without later formation, exchange, selective destruction or protected compartments. The one-source invariant assumes the stated background/source mixture and isotope-independent racemization. The printed measurement uncertainties use different definitions and raw replicate covariance was unavailable.
Proof spine: Write n_j=L_j+D_j and m_j=L_j-D_j. The closed symmetric racemization equations conserve n_j and solve m_j(t)=m_j(0)e^(-2K); requiring |m_j(0)|<=n_j(0) yields the positivity bound. In the source mixture, isotope-heavy fractions mix linearly in q, and solving the L/D-weighted mass balance for the excess source gives q_excess.
Costs: The source reports a typical-source compatibility fit with D/L=0.8124, D delta15N=275.82 per mil, L delta15N=220.29 per mil and source delta15N=-20 per mil, each within one quoted spread under its separate definition. It also describes an illustrative D/L standard-error interpretation. No joint likelihood was reconstructed from raw scans.
Failure: The -590.5 per mil source value is model-dependent and unstable as D/L approaches one; the uncertainty fit prevents treating it as a required exotic reservoir. The closed-pool racemization bound is not an age estimate and does not apply to open histories. This does not establish contamination, overturn the source paper, or identify a chemical history.
Closest comparator: The source notes precedents for static isotope-of-excess calculations and preserves published measurement controls; those source comparisons were not independently checked. No novel chemical mechanism is claimed.
Open verification: Independently verify the isotope-probability conversion and mixture algebra, then obtain replicate-level isotope scans/covariances and test source histories under explicit open-pool and racemization assumptions.

Claim: For the two native backbone carbon indicators, let p=E(X_1+X_2)/2, c=P(X_1=X_2=1), r=P_1/(2P_0) and t=P_2/P_0. The source gives the exact inversion p=(r+t)/(1+2r+t), c=t/(1+2r+t); thus the singly substituted ratio alone does not identify mean heavy-carbon abundance. Under a source-mixture model where molecules form independently within reservoirs with heavy-carbon fraction P, c-p^2=Var(P). If every source lies in [a,b], Var(P)<=(p-a)(b-p), a sharp endpoint bound. The report's equal-marginal correlated benchmark predicts P_2/P_0 23.71 times its independent-backbone alternative for Bennu and 6.18 times for Murchison; these are conditional native-isotope predictions, not observed peaks. For the stated Bennu organic-material interval, the source reports a maximum covariance 134.28 times below its benchmark requirement, excluding that bounded source class under the chosen interface.
Interface: All probability equations refer to corrected native carbon probabilities. The source uses the displayed VPDB-ratio-to-probability interface, but applying that correction to this pair model is unverified. A derivatization reagent adds carbon, so native double-substitution ratios require the stated generating-polynomial deconvolution. Two 13C substitutions and one 18O substitution are separated by only 0.00246468 Da; calibrated line shapes, standards and integration are needed.
Proof spine: Express P0=1-2p+c, P1=2(p-c), P2=c and solve the ratio definitions for p,c. In a reservoir mixture c=E[P^2], p=E[P], so covariance equals Var(P); the pointwise inequality (P-a)(b-P)>=0 gives the sharp interval bound. Independent-position unequal marginals alone move r in the opposite direction. The source reports additional LP and generated-distribution checks, not replayed by intake.
Costs: The source reports Bennu and Murchison benchmark quantities and says the bounded Bennu source interval permits covariance at most 1.40165e-5 while the candidate needs 1.88210e-3. Raw isotope spectra were not acquired; fragment/reagent contributions and mass-line overlap prevent interpreting a nominal mass-plus-two count as the native carbon-pair signal.
Failure: The equal-marginal correlation distribution is one feasible construction, not a unique source history. The interval bound applies only to the cited organic-material source class, not every historical carbon-bearing phase; extreme reservoirs remain possible but unconnected to the amino acid. The central mechanism of mixing-induced isotope clumping is acknowledged as known prior art. No β-alanine origin or chirality mechanism is established.
Closest comparator: The source identifies prior work on mixing-induced doubly substituted species and apparent site-specific isotope effects. It explicitly demotes the general mechanism as prior art; the quantitative application and instrument caveats are source-reported, not a novelty claim.

Claim: Let A be a complete synchronizing deterministic finite automaton on m>=2 states with at least two letters a,b. The source constructs B by adjoining m-1 proxy states p_i and retaining every original transition, with p_i a=q_i a and p_i b=q_{i+1}b; every further letter maps p_i into the original image Qc. Every nonempty word has exactly the same image from B as from A, so their nonempty reset languages and reset thresholds agree. The pair-specific unit merges form a spanning path, forcing the pair-distance MST weight K(B)=|Q_B|-1=2m-2. Applied to the classical m-state Cerny family, |Q_B|=2m-1 and rt(B)=(m-1)^2=(|Q_B|-1)^2/4, so rt(B)/K(B)=(|Q_B|-1)/4 and no universal constant C gives rt<=C K (even with a fixed additive constant).
Interface: Complete deterministic automata; at least two alphabet letters; the core automaton is synchronizing. Pair distance is the shortest word merging a specified pair; K is the minimum spanning-tree weight using these distances. The construction is not strongly connected: the original states form a closed subautomaton.
Proof spine: For every letter c, the new states map into Qc while original states still have image Qc; induction on a nonempty word gives Q_B w=Q_A w. The pairs {q_i,p_i} merge under a and {p_i,q_{i+1}} under b, giving a unit-weight spanning path. Since every edge weight is at least one, this attains the |Q_B|-1 MST lower bound. The classical Cerny threshold then yields the unbounded ratio.
Costs: The extension is written with O(m times alphabet-size) transition assignments. Pair distances are polynomial-time computable by reverse search on unordered pairs. This does not provide a short-reset algorithm or improve general reset-word upper bounds; exact subset BFS appears only as a finite check in the source.
Failure: This refutes the specific proposal that a fixed multiplicative rescaling of pair-distance MST universally pays for a single common reset word. It does not refute the Cerny conjecture, all polynomial-size potentials, or the same claim restricted to strongly connected automata. Historical priority is UNKNOWN.
Closest comparator: The construction uses the classical Cerny family and the source cites established reset-threshold literature. The exact extension formulation was not independently checked against prior art during intake; no novelty or priority claim is made.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the reset-language equality and MST calculation, audit the precise extension against automata literature, and separately test whether an analogous obstruction can satisfy strong connectivity without changing the claimed scope.

N618-stationary-joint-neighborhood-repair-counterexample | A 160-vertex triangle-free regular digraph refutes a stationary joint neighborhood repair
status=source_derived_unreviewed; CQ preserves the exact independent-investigations directory and indexes only scoped claims and failures. Source-reported proofs, finite checks, extracted figure measurements, selective raw-data provenance and literature boundaries were not independently reproduced; no supplied research script was executed. External correctness, formal certification, historical priority, physical acquisition and claimed scientific interpretation remain UNKNOWN. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: The source gives an explicit strongly connected, oriented, triangle-free 52-outregular 0/1 digraph on n=160 vertices. For the stationary distribution pi of its uniform-outneighbor walk, with s(v) the number of exact two-step outneighbors excluding v and its first outneighbors, it reports E_pi[d^-(v)+s(v)] = 104 - 2493/485524 < 2r=104. Thus the proposed universal stationary joint inequality is false even under equal row degree, strong connectivity and directed-triangle exclusion. The same construction family at n=64,r=20 separately gives E_pi s=20-29/1186<r. Since 160>3*52, these examples do not contradict the directed triangle case of Caccetta–Häggkvist.
Interface: Finite oriented directed graphs with adjacency entries in {0,1}, equal outdegree r, strong connectivity, and no directed 3-cycles. pi is the unique stationary distribution of the uniform-outneighbor Markov chain. s(v) counts vertices reachable in exactly two steps but not at distance zero or one.
Proof spine: The source builds a 16-vertex row-4 block H and substitutes it into a triangle-free regular outer digraph F_q, adding complete inter-block arcs. It derives the stationary law from R sigma=q*1+H^T sigma and gives exact rational group masses. At q=3, n=160,r=52; direct rational evaluation yields the displayed deficit. The source reports a second exact implementation and full adjacency/stationary certificates.
Costs: The witness is finite and explicit; the report states that two exact-rational implementations verify adjacency, stationary coordinates, connectivity, triangle exclusion and neighborhood counts. This intake checked file hashes and routes only and did not run either implementation.
Failure: The counterexample falsifies only the proposed stationary second-neighborhood inequality and the specific indegree-paid joint repair. It is not a counterexample to Caccetta–Häggkvist, does not establish an impossibility theorem for stationary methods, and does not create a new CH barrier. The valid reverse-step entropy lemma is separate from the failed charging step.
Closest comparator: The report cites established Caccetta–Häggkvist background and related average second-neighborhood conjectures. The exact witness priority was not established; the cited literature was not independently audited during intake.
Open verification: Reconstruct the block substitution and stationary equations independently from the full adjacency certificate, verify the rational expectations, and preserve the strict distinction between this false intermediate inequality and the still-open Caccetta–Häggkvist question.

status=source_derived_unreviewed; CQ preserves the exact independent-investigations directory and indexes only scoped claims and failures. Source-reported proofs, finite checks, extracted figure measurements, selective raw-data provenance and literature boundaries were not independently reproduced; no supplied research script was executed. Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: The broad claim E_pi |N_2(v)| >= E_pi d^+(v), for the stationary law of the uniform-outneighbor walk on every strongly connected oriented graph, is false. One four-vertex witness has arcs 0->1,0->3,1->2,2->0,3->1,3->2, stationary law (4,3,4,2)/13, outdegrees (2,1,1,2), and exact second-neighborhood sizes (1,1,2,1), giving expectations 19/13 and 17/13. A separate strongly connected triangle-free eight-vertex cyclic-block graph with variable outdegree has E_pi d^+=17/7 but E_pi |N_2|=2. These examples obstruct broad stationary-weighted extensions; neither refutes the existential Seymour conjecture, the minimum-outdegree formulation, or a row-regular triangle-free statement.
Interface: Finite strongly connected oriented digraphs; pi is stationary for the uniform-outneighbor transition. In the first witness outdegree is variable and directed triangles exist. The second witness is triangle-free but variable-degree, with exact second neighborhoods defined to exclude the start and first outneighbors.
Proof spine: For the four-vertex graph, multiply the stated rational row vector by the transition matrix and enumerate exact two-step neighborhoods. For the triangle-free example, arrange four two-vertex blocks cyclically, put one internal arc in each block and all arcs to the next block; the exact stationary weights are 3/28 on each u_i and 4/28 on each v_i, while each exact second neighborhood has size two.
Costs: The examples have explicit adjacency lists and exact rational stationary laws. The package retains finite-discovery and exact-check scripts; they were not executed during intake.
Failure: These witnesses do not test or falsify the regular triangle-free averaging route covered separately by N618, do not refute Seymour’s existential conjecture, and do not imply a general obstruction to stationary methods. They are scoped counterexamples to the stated weighted inequalities only.
Closest comparator: The report makes no novelty claim. Its purpose is to prevent importing a broad stationary-weighted theorem without proof.
Open verification: Recompute both stationary distributions and exact second neighborhoods from the adjacency lists, then retain each failure only at its stated variable-degree scope.

Claim: Under x'(t)=A x(t) with Metzler A, known positive initial population p, neutral inherited binary tags whose initial fractions W_ji are known, a sufficient declared-state model, and at most s off-diagonal incoming rates per state, the source derives f'_ji(0)=sum_{k!=i} lambda_ik(W_jk-W_ji), where f_ji=x_ji/x_0i and lambda_ik=A_ik p_k/p_i. With an (s+1)-disjunct code, lambda_ik is the minimum eligible derivative over rows W_ji=0,W_jk=1. Separately, for a time-homogeneous A and occupation-integrated tagged counts U_j=integral_0^T exp(-lambda t)x_j(t)dt, endpoint quantity H_j=exp(-lambda T)x_j(T)-x_j(0) satisfies (A-lambda I)U_j=H_j; the source derives a row equation Z_i a_i=D_i for the off-diagonal rates. If every at-most-2s-column submatrix of Z_i has full column rank, the s-sparse row is unique. The source reports exact rational finite examples, including recovery of 16,256 rates.
Interface: Requires known/observed initial abundances and tag fractions, tag neutrality and inheritance, all declared-state classification, calibrated measurements, and no tag-dependent dynamics. The finite-interval identity additionally requires one common time-independent A and occupation-integrated measurements, not just endpoints. Hidden heterogeneous subtypes can invalidate the mean model.
Proof spine: Apply the quotient rule to tagged and total population equations; the diagonal A_ii terms cancel. Nonnegative incoming rates plus disjunctness make the min decoder exact. For finite intervals, integrate the linear dynamics with exponential weight, integrate by parts, then subtract F_ji times the untagged coordinate equation so diagonal and lambda terms cancel. Uniqueness follows because the difference of two s-sparse solutions is a null vector on at most 2s columns.
Costs: The reported 128-state derivative example uses 49 tags and O(n^2 q^2) comparisons for the stated polynomial code. Finite-interval support enumeration is combinatorial in s; conditioning, population balance, discretization/assay error and independent replicate-population variation require separate accounting. Exact rational code tests are source-reported and were not rerun.
Failure: The derivation does not construct a physical state-dependent tag writer or establish neutral tags, lumpability, feasible destructive-cohort sampling, or acquisition advantage over ordinary barcoding/tracer tomography. Exact-real identifiability is not a finite-precision stability guarantee. No new coding theorem or transformative capability is claimed.
Closest comparator: The source explicitly places the construction alongside known prospective lineage barcoding, group testing, compressed sensing and tracer tomography and credits the polynomial disjunct-code construction to Kautz–Singleton. Those prior-art claims were not independently audited during intake.
Open verification: Independently derive both identities and verify the exact-rank assumptions; assess whether the required tag/occupation interface is physically available and compare charged resources with ordinary prospective barcoding and tracer methods.

status=source_derived_unreviewed; CQ preserves the exact independent-investigations directory and indexes only scoped claims and failures. Source-reported proofs, finite checks, extracted figure measurements, selective raw-data provenance and literature boundaries were not independently reproduced; no supplied research script was executed. Claim: For the source's ideal model of a random bounded measurable classical signal with a constant clock channel, fixed reciprocal real couplings, coherent ladder evolution and endpoint preparations/readouts, define for each finite channel word w of length r the signed endpoint contrast D_w(lambda)=i^r E[U_w[a;lambda]_{r0}-U_w[a;lambda]_{0r}]. The source reports an exact reciprocity identity and a completeness theorem: the signal law equals its time-reversed law if and only if D_w(lambda)=0 for every finite word w and every positive coupling lambda. The proof route extracts all antisymmetric expected ordered integrals from analytic leading coefficients and uses the clock-augmented integrated path and Stone–Weierstrass to separate bounded signal laws. This is an unbounded hierarchy, not a finite-resource decision procedure.
Interface: The signal is not altered or replayed; the ideal theorem assumes reproducible windows, a noninvasive signal, known bounded channels including a clock, real calibrated reciprocal coherent couplings, phase reference and endpoint readout. A time reversal of increments is defined in the source using the clock-augmented path; it is not ordinary signed path inversion.
Proof spine: Real symmetric instantaneous Hamiltonians imply the propagator under reversed input is the transpose of the forward propagator. Endpoint swapping makes the contrast exactly odd under reversal. Its first nonzero Dyson coefficient is the difference between expected ordered integrals for w and reverse(w). If all contrasts vanish for every positive lambda, analyticity gives equality of all expected iterated integrals; the clock coordinate removes reparameterization ambiguity, and the shuffle algebra plus Stone–Weierstrass yields equality of the bounded path laws.
Costs: For any fixed word, the report gives a bounded-outcome finite-shot concentration bound and a finite-coupling remainder. The complete theorem quantifies over all finite words and positive couplings; it supplies no uniform first distinguishing word length, polynomial-time search, uniform sample complexity, or practical signal-to-noise guarantee.
Failure: The only demonstrated finite-strength separation is from constant commuting integrators. Existing time-resolved and nonlinear correlation sensors can distinguish suitable signals. No physical platform, native signal-to-coupling transduction, calibrated advantage, or new sensor capability was demonstrated. The rotating example is identified as a spin-1 Rabi-class calculation.
Closest comparator: The source cites Chen iterated integrals, sparse path-signature results, Rabi dynamics, SENSIT time-reversal sensing and quantum computational sensing as close prior work; it explicitly withholds novelty. Intake did not independently verify that literature boundary.
Open verification: Reconstruct the completeness proof with the exact path-law topology and reversal convention; check the relation to sparse path characteristic functions and prior time-reversal sensing; require a physical target and matched native-sensor baseline before any capability claim.

N622-conditional-tetragonal-domain-hall-tensor-invariants | Tetragonal-domain averaging gives conditional Hall tensor invariants and a population-independent [111] slope
status=source_derived_unreviewed; CQ preserves the exact independent-investigations directory and indexes only scoped claims and failures. Source-reported proofs, finite checks, extracted figure measurements, selective raw-data provenance and literature boundaries were not independently reproduced; no supplied research script was executed. External correctness, formal certification, historical priority, physical acquisition and claimed scientific interpretation remain UNKNOWN. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Under the source's weak-Hall, local-diffusive model with the same scalar zero-field longitudinal conductivity in every domain and fixed single-domain coefficients a,c, tetragonal symmetry gives K0=diag(a,a,c) and K(n)=aI+(c-a)nn^T. First-order arithmetic averaging is exact under those assumptions: for Q=E[nn^T], tr Q=1, K_eff=aI+(c-a)Q and b_hat·K_eff b_hat=a+(c-a)E[(n·b_hat)^2]. For the three ideal SrTiO3 tetragonal variants and B along [111], every squared projection is 1/3, so the model predicts S_[111]=(2a+c)/3 independent of domain populations. Orthogonal full-tensor slopes sum to tr K_eff=2a+c, invariant under pure orientation redistribution in this model. These are conditional deductions, not measured values of a,c or evidence for a microscopic mechanism.
Interface: Assumes weak Hall response, local diffusion, a common scalar zero-field longitudinal conductivity, fixed a,c across intervention, and arithmetic averaging at first order. Arbitrary inhomogeneous anisotropic composites are outside scope. B projection and contact-normal geometry must not be conflated.
Proof spine: The axial-vector transformation laws make K transform as an ordinary rank-two tensor. Tetragonal D4h symmetry fixes diag(a,a,c); the domain director gives the rank-one form. The uniform zero-field corrector under common scalar longitudinal conductivity makes the first-order effective Hall tensor the arithmetic mean, from which the [111] and trace identities follow.
Costs: The source digitizes plotted vector markers from a published figure and reports descriptive finite-field statistics. Its +/- perturbation range for extraction is a sensitivity interval, not a confidence interval or experimental error model. No suitable matched before/after [111] or full three-axis raw dataset was located in the bounded search.
Failure: The analysis neither statistically rejects the microscopic scattering explanation nor establishes a new natural mechanism. Contact gains, temperature mismatch, heat-flow changes, spatially varying longitudinal anisotropy, domain walls and other scattering changes remain possible. A raw Hall angle is not automatically the zero-field slope.
Closest comparator: The source identifies prior SrTiO3 domain-orientation work and known Hall-sign-inversion examples in inhomogeneous media. It makes no novelty claim; citations and figures were not independently reanalysed during intake.
Open verification: Acquire matched-temperature full-tensor Hall measurements in [111] and three orthogonal geometries with calibrated contact/longitudinal response; then test the invariants against spatially inhomogeneous transport and the source-reported uncertainty.

N623-motor-off-window-data-do-not-identify-delayed-priming | A held-out motor OFF-window trace screen does not identify robust delayed priming
status=source_derived_unreviewed; CQ preserves the exact independent-investigations directory and indexes only scoped claims and failures. Source-reported proofs, finite checks, extracted figure measurements, selective raw-data provenance and literature boundaries were not independently reproduced; no supplied research script was executed. Claim: In the source's selected-trace analysis of 44 traces from 43 cells with a cell-identity-based discovery/validation split, the frozen primary OFF-window classifier labeled one resolved post-pulse onset among 16 validation pulse traces from 15 cells, alongside 15 immediate/unresolved traces. The identity of late events changed under the fixed 200-ms guard and threshold sensitivities; counts across the six fixed settings ranged from zero to two of 16. The report therefore does not identify a robust excess of delayed post-pulse activation over ordinary recovery. This is a source-reported negative analysis, not evidence that mechanical priming is absent.
Interface: The observable is first sustained autonomous rotation during the OFF interval, not stator attachment or occupancy. The report uses selected 4-kHz long-axis/PCA angles, cell-level discovery/validation separation, a fixed Savitzky–Golay derivative, thresholds, persistence rule and edge guards. The 44 traces cover 43 unique cells; one cell appears under both forcing directions within the validation grouping, but no cell crosses the discovery/validation split.
Proof spine: The candidate distinguishes instantaneous activation from a latent mechanically prepared state by comparing first sustained autonomous-motion onset during OFF intervals. Extraction rules were frozen before validation outcomes were parsed, with a documented pre-validation correction. The reported late-event identities are guard/threshold sensitive and ordinary unforced recovery is sparse, so the source closes the candidate as unidentified rather than claiming a mechanism.
Costs: The original multi-gigabyte source ZIP was not fully downloaded; selected entries were fetched by byte ranges and individually CRC/SHA checked in the source record. This intake did not reacquire data, rerun extraction, or fit a calibrated clustered-event model. Reported Poisson tails are explicitly descriptive, not calibrated tests.
Failure: The analysis does not rule out sub-100-ms priming, priming hidden inside the edge guard, mechanical pinning, or attachment masked by bearing/glass effects. It cannot observe molecular attachment. The selected records are too sparse and sensitivity-unstable to establish delayed priming; no causal or molecular claim follows.
Closest comparator: The source identifies Ito, Nakamura and Toyabe (2021) as the experimental source and notes prior hypotheses of rotation-enhanced assembly, gear activation and MotB stretching. The report also records bearing barriers as a rival. Literature and raw source archive were not independently reaudited by intake.
Open verification: Independently reproduce the selected-entry pipeline and cell split; establish an acquisition-complete event model with cell clustering and guard-time control; add an observable or intervention that distinguishes latent priming from torque masking before making a mechanistic claim.

Claim: For a supplied finite DAG of K one-shot events with rational monic quadratic guards that square-complete to source monomials epsilon^{b_i} times rational powers of parent deficits, rational affine nonfeedback resets, explicit touch semantics and distinct tie priorities, the source construction computes exact one-sided event order and output and returns L so the execution is valid for every 0<epsilon<=2^(-L).
Interface: Explicit native guard data are supplied: rational coefficients, nonnegative integer b_i and w_ip, and monomial sources epsilon^{b_i} product_p r_p^{w_ip}; source parents must also be activation parents. Claim: For every simple cubic graph G on n vertices, the source constructs a bounded-degree 2-local Pauli Hamiltonian on 4n qubits with coefficients ±1 and a stated small perturbation connecting the anticommutation graph. Proof spine: Exactly resum each local star to obtain an antiferromagnetic Ising cut polynomial. The beta scaling separates integer cut values by more than the relative approximation margin. A small X perturbation connects the graph while preserving that margin.
Costs: The reduction uses O(n) qubits, terms and coefficient bits, beta O(n), and log Z O(n^2). It is a conditional hardness statement, not a sampler or capability gain.
Failure: This rules out only the stated whole family unless a complexity collapse occurs. It is not an intrinsic sign-problem theorem or an unconditional impossibility for more restricted classes. Source code and rounding margins were not independently checked.
Closest comparator: The source invokes Alimonti–Kann cubic-MaxCut hardness and cites prior thermal/tensor-network methods; this intake did not recheck those applications.

Claim: For arbitrarily large q, there exists a sunflower-free partite code with a specified coordinate whose largest injective sunflower-free subfamily after deleting that coordinate has relative size at most q^(-1/12)+q^(-2), while code rank is Theta(q^4). Thus this prescribed-coordinate delete/prune operation has no uniform constant-retention guarantee.
Interface: The construction represents a linear 3-uniform hypergraph as exact sunflower triples of projection rows, appends an identity coordinate, and blocks each triple with a q-color coordinate. The rank is quadratic in the hypergraph vertex count; the existence proof is probabilistic.
Proof spine: A random triple system with two-color multiplicities is sparsified and collision edges deleted to obtain a linear hypergraph with independence number o(N). The projection representation makes its edges exactly the sunflower triples; erasing the color coordinate leaves maximum safe retention alpha(H).
Costs: This is an existential asymptotic obstruction, not an efficient construction. A separate exact rank-three code has maximum safe retention 1/3 after deleting any coordinate.
Failure: It refutes only a uniform guarantee for a specified coordinate and this operation. It does not make every coordinate expensive, rule out adaptive/simultaneous surgery, yield a superexponential family, or refute the sunflower conjecture.
Closest comparator: The report gives its own probabilistic construction and does not assume a general high-chromatic-hypergraph theorem. Exhaustive priority remains UNKNOWN.
Open verification: Find an adaptive/global invariant controlling total deleted mass; the prescribed-coordinate example leaves adaptive choice open.

Claim: Every finite-alphabet law p has a coupling Q of three copies with marginal p, supported on triples that are all equal or all distinct, and D_KL(Q||p^3)<=log 4; equality holds for a uniform binary law. For three different marginals p_1,p_2,p_3, feasibility is equivalent to nonnegative t_a<=min_j p_j(a), T_0=sum t_a, and sum_j p_j(a)-3t_a<=1-T_0 for every a.
Interface: A one-coordinate finite probability statement on a shared alphabet. Unequal-marginal feasibility is exact; no global multi-coordinate guarantee or input acquisition follows.
Proof spine: The allowed-triple normalizer Phi(u)=1-3 sum u_a^2+3 sum u_a^3 is at least 1/4; entropy duality gives the KL bound. For unequal marginals reserve diagonal mass t_a and apply the fractional matching polytope to residual all-distinct mass.
Costs: The source gives O(q) scalar partition-function evaluation and a finite-dimensional convex optimization but no uniform exact optimizer bit bound. Unequal-marginal feasibility is a linear program plus matching decomposition.
Failure: Local couplings need not glue when conditional histories have different marginals. The packet supplies a separate obstruction to a naive global information charge; no general sunflower solution follows.
Closest comparator: The source presents a sharp local primitive; entropy duality and matching-polytope steps have not been independently audited here.
Open verification: Reconstruct the entropy dual including zero-mass cases and determine which conditional structures permit local-to-global gluing.

Claim: Let n>=1 qubits start in |0^n> and a reference with H_R=sum_{r>=0} r|r><r| start in any finite-mean state rho of mean mu. Under an arbitrary joint unitary commuting with H_S+H_R, retain all outputs and compare the final joint state with |+^n><+^n| tensor the same original rho, uncorrelated. If D is their trace distance, then for every s>0, D >= exp(-s mu)[1-((1+exp(-s))/2)^n], and D >= n/[8e(mu+n)]. Thus for 0<epsilon<=1/(16e), D<=epsilon requires mu>=n/(16e epsilon). A supplied sine-profile reference and explicit conserving interactions attain D<=min(1, pi sqrt(n(n+1))/(2(L+1))) with mean energy n+(L-1)/2, giving optimal Theta(n/epsilon) scaling for this exact joint-return task.
Interface: All system outputs and the reference are retained; the target contains the same uncorrelated reference. U may be arbitrary subject to exact total-energy conservation. Trace distance is 1/2 trace norm. The upper construction assumes the coherent sine reference is supplied; it is not constructed from free inputs.
Proof spine: The invariant bounded effect exp[-s(H_S+H_R)] has expectations L_rho(s) and L_rho(s)((1+exp(-s))/2)^n on actual and target states. Jensen gives L_rho(s)>=exp(-s mu), yielding the all-protocol lower bound. For the upper bound, sector Hadamards yield 2^(-n/2) sum_x |x> T^|x| eta; telescoping shift error and W~Bin(n,1/2) give the uniform overlap bound.
Costs: Mean resource scaling is Theta(n/epsilon) in the stated small-error regime, with a supplied sine reference of mean n+(L-1)/2; no gate-synthesis or reference-preparation complexity is bounded.
Failure: The lower bound is for the entire joint output/reference comparison, not the reduced system channel or a channel diamond norm. The construction prepares no reference and charges no arbitrary-unitary synthesis; initial-reference precision contributes additional error. A fixed-pure-reference overlap optimum is also source-derived but does not imply efficient synthesis.
Closest comparator: The source cites Chiribella, Yang and Renner (2021), “Fundamental Energy Requirement of Reversible Quantum Operations,” https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevX.11.021014, plus finite sine-reference and catalytic-coherence antecedents. Citation and exact priority comparison were not rechecked in intake; no novelty is claimed.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the bounded-witness lower bound and same-reference contract; compare exact error/resource conventions with prior energy-reference results and charge coherent-reference preparation and interaction synthesis.

N634-exact-gaussian-norm-permanent-hardness | Exact standard-Gaussian squared-norm evaluation is #P-hard for integer arithmetic circuits
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The 10 October source packet reports internally derived/reconstructed arguments and coordinator or adversarial checks for the stated scopes. Claim: There is a polynomial-time Turing reduction from the 0/1 permanent to exact evaluation of E[p(G)^2] for integer-coefficient arithmetic circuits p and independent standard real Gaussian inputs G. The proof builds 0/1 Gram factorizations B_t B_t^T=tI+A, uses the complex Wick identity to recover perm(tI+A) from the real and imaginary circuit norms, interpolates at N+1 positive integer t values, and takes an exact integer square root of perm(M)^2.
Interface: The oracle returns the exact rational/integer expectation with all output bits. The reduction makes polynomially many queries to circuits of polynomial size and degree over independent standard real Gaussians. It is a Turing reduction, not one-query or approximate evaluation.
Proof spine: For a bipartite adjacency matrix A=[[0,M],[M^T,0]], construct B_t from edge columns e_i+e_j and t-d_i singleton columns so B_tB_t^T=tI+A. Complex Gaussian moments give E|P_t|^2=2^N perm(B_tB_t^T); split into real/imaginary integer circuits. Interpolation recovers q(0)=perm(A)=perm(M)^2.
Costs: The construction uses N+1 integer parameter points and polynomial-size, degree-N circuits with O(N^2) real Gaussian inputs; outputs and interpolation operands have polynomial bit length.
Failure: No implication is claimed for approximate/additive norm evaluation, norm-zero testing, randomized polynomial identity testing, or general identity testing. The reported finite exact checker is not run by this intake.
Closest comparator: Uses the standard #P-completeness of the 0/1 permanent (Valiant, 1979); the source cites this antecedent. It does not make a new approximate-counting or identity-testing result.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct normalization, circuit construction, interpolation bit sizes, and the exact-query interface; verify the cited permanent-completeness input.

N635-local-complex-gauge-matching-signature-obstruction | One critical EPR tensor has no nonnegative matching signature under independent complex local gauges
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The 10 October source packet reports internally derived/reconstructed arguments and coordinator or adversarial checks for the stated scopes. Claim: For F=[[4,0,0,1],[0,9,4,0],[0,4,9,0],[1,0,0,4]], there are no A_i in GL(2,C) such that (A_1 tensor A_2)F(A_3 tensor A_4)^T is a nonnegative four-port weighted perfect-matching gadget signature in the cited Cai–Liu sense. The same obstruction holds with F replaced by F^k for every integer k>=1 under the stated identical serial grouping.
Interface: The port flattening is (1,2)|(3,4), with each port dimension two. All four transformations are independent and invertible over C; transposes are ordinary, not conjugate transposes. The result is restricted to one tensor and its identical serial powers.
Proof spine: The invariant K(M)=MJM^TJ transforms by similarity and a common scalar under the full local group. F gives roots {25,9,169,25}, normalized to {13,5,5,3}. The necessary complementary-product inequalities for a nonnegative matching signature fail for each possible parity-block pairing; powers give the same strict failures raised to k.
Costs: This is a finite-dimensional algebraic obstruction with four 2-by-2 gauges; no search over k is needed because the inequalities fail for every positive integer power.
Failure: This excludes only the stated local gauges and identical serial powers. It does not imply counting hardness, absence of an FPRAS, or impossibility of nonlocal, approximate, singular, heterogeneous, multiwire, larger-port, or other gadget representations. The imported necessary condition is essential.
Closest comparator: Cai and Liu (2019), https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.10493, Theorem 4.1, supplies a necessary condition only. Four-qubit invariant theory is established context; source states the exact obstruction priority was not audited. No novelty or complexity separation is claimed.
Open verification: Independently verify the full-complex local invariant, imported necessary matchgate condition, parity handling, and the all-k inequalities. Keep the global EPR counting/oracle gate open.

N636-kraus-history-rank-test-positive-compression | Rank-collapsing Kraus histories admit an exact exterior-square test and positive d^4 compression
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The 10 October source packet reports internally derived/reconstructed arguments and coordinator or adversarial checks for the stated scopes. This intake preserves and routes those records only; it did not independently reconstruct the proofs, run research scripts, or validate external correctness or historical priority. Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Given T explicit trace-preserving instruments on C^d with Gaussian-rational Kraus matrices of at most B-bit numerators/denominators, a polynomial-bit algorithm decides whether every length-T history product has rank at most one without listing histories. For a repeated fixed instrument, eventual all-history collapse occurs iff it has occurred by D=binom(d,2) steps. Separately, the exact terminal channel after forgetting outcomes has a representation sum_{j<=d^4} c_j B_j X B_j*, where c_j are positive rationals and every B_j is an actual length-T branch product. If all products have rank at most one, this yields an exact measure-prepare form.
Interface: The instrument and Kraus matrices are supplied. Complexity is polynomial in dense Hilbert dimension d and input bit length, not in qubit count log2(d). Compression preserves only the terminal forgotten-outcome channel; it need not preserve histories, their probabilities, or intermediate intervention responses.
Proof spine: Lift each Kraus operator to the exterior square; the span of all branch images is propagated by V_t=sum_i (Lambda^2 K_i^(t))V_(t-1), and is zero iff every branch product has rank<=1. For a fixed instrument the descending subspace chain stabilizes within D steps. For compression, vectorize branch products into Hermitian Choi rank-one matrices in a d^4-dimensional real space and use exact rational conic elimination with positive weights.
Costs: The source gives polynomial bit complexity in dense dimension d, instrument length and input bit size, with O(sum_t r_t D^3) field operations for the span test and at most d^4 retained products.
Failure: This is not representation-independent entanglement-breaking recognition: the source gives an invertible-Pauli Kraus representation of a depolarizing entanglement-breaking channel that fails the test. d^4 is polynomial in d but exponential in qubits. No generic simulation improvement follows. Its exact combined novelty is unestablished.
Closest comparator: The source identifies exterior algebra, conic Caratheodory elimination and rank-one Kraus/measure-prepare equivalence as standard. It cites Horodecki, Shor and Ruskai (2003), https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0302031. No broad entanglement-breaking theorem is claimed.
Open verification: Independently audit the exact rational bit-growth argument, history-span closure, fixed-instrument cutoff, positive elimination, and terminal-channel-only semantics.

N637-connected-path-loop-selector-exponential-second-moment | An iid loop-selector estimator has exponential second moment on a connected exact path family
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The 10 October source packet reports internally derived/reconstructed arguments and coordinator or adversarial checks for the stated scopes. This intake preserves and routes those records only; it did not independently reconstruct the proofs, run research scripts, or validate external correctness or historical priority. Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For each k>=1, an explicit connected path instance on 2k qubits with 2k-1 gates and positive rational weights has exact partition function Z=26^k(1+epsilon)^(k-1), epsilon=1/(100k), computable in O(k) rational arithmetic, while the specified iid I/C/D loop-selector estimator satisfies E[Y^2]/Z^2 >= exp(-0.02)(189/169)^k.
Interface: The pair gates are F(4,4,1) and bridges F(1,epsilon,epsilon); one selector is drawn independently per gate with probabilities proportional to a,c,d and Y is the product normalizer times the exact selected-word trace. The claim is estimator- and family-specific.
Proof spine: Leaf partial traces give Z=2 product_e(2a_e+c_e+d_e). Condition on all bridges selecting I; pair-gate relative second moments multiply to (189/169)^k, while the bridge probability/normalization factor is bounded below by exp(-0.02). A parity check is required when evaluating selector loops.
Costs: The exact partition function takes O(k) rational arithmetic with polynomial bit lengths; one selector draw and exact path trace are polynomial in k. The second moment grows exponentially in k.
Failure: This refutes the usual variance-based FPRAS argument for this iid estimator on this connected family only. The family itself has an elementary exact algorithm. It proves no counting hardness, no lower bound for all estimators, and no general tensor-network variance barrier. Finite selector checks are source-reported and not rerun here.
Closest comparator: Related to N115 and the existing N190/N191/N193 EPR results, but it is an estimator-specific extension/obstruction and does not settle global EPR sampling.
Open verification: Independently check the leaf-trace identity, estimator normalization, bridge conditioning, and parity treatment; seek a conditional or global acquired estimator without overstating this negative witness.

body:
N638-complex-lee-yang-spectral-finite-product-bounds | Complex Lee–Yang operators have sharp spectral separation and varying products approach rank one
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The 10 October source packet reports internally derived/reconstructed arguments and coordinator or adversarial checks for the stated scopes. This intake preserves and routes those records only; it did not independently reconstruct the proofs, run research scripts, or validate external correctness or historical priority. No historic-scale/foundational breakthrough, physical acquisition, or practical transformative capability is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Define LY(r), r>1, by zero-freeness of the flattened polynomial f_K(z,w)=sum_xy K_xy z^x w^y when all variables lie in the open polydisk of radius r. For every complex 2^n-by-2^n K in LY(r), the maximum-modulus eigenvalue is unique, nonzero and algebraically simple, and every other eigenvalue obeys |lambda/lambda_*|<=r^-2; its rank-one spectral projector factors into LY(r) vectors. Also, if K_1,...,K_T each lie in LY(r), M=K_T...K_1, e=|0^n>, and a=e^T M e !=0, then B=(Me)(e^T M)/a has rank one and ||M-B||_F <= 2(1+r^2)^(n/2)r^(-2T)||Me||_2 <= 2(1+r^2)^(n/2)r^(-2T)||M||_2.
Interface: All matrices may be complex, nonnormal, non-PSD and varying; they share the same supplied whole-layer LY(r) promise. Products and contractions use bilinear transposes without conjugation. The estimate is conditional on the global zero-free promise for every factor.
Proof spine: Import two zero-free contraction/limit facts; establish eigenvector comparison via holomorphic diameter contraction, then use generic perturbation or the product theorem to obtain spectral separation. For varying products, propagate polynomial ratios and apply Parseval to bound the Frobenius residual from the explicit rank-one B.
Costs: The explicit sufficient product length for relative operator-norm error epsilon is T >= [log(2/epsilon)+(n/2)log(1+r^2)]/[2log r], conditional on the shared whole-layer LY(r) promise; this is a theorem bound, not an implementation-cost guarantee.
Failure: A zero-free promise does not recognize itself from local input, compute M e or e^T M, normalize thermal quantities, or provide physical acquisition/nonunitary implementation. No polynomial-cost state-preparation, thermal-normalization or finite-temperature capability follows; exponential postselection examples are explicit. The theorem extends a source-cited PSD mechanism but originality is not claimed.
Closest comparator: Bravyi, Gosset, Liu and Wong, arXiv:2607.14401v1, is source-cited as prior PSD spectral separation/quantum ground-energy work; Rugh (2010), https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2010.171.1707, is cited for projective contraction antecedents. Source-reported citations were not rechecked at intake.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the complex contraction facts, spectral perturbation, nonnormal case, bilinear projector, and varying-product estimate. Separate the theorem from the absent polynomial-cost recognition, preparation, and normalization algorithms.

body:
N639-fixed-copy-ghz-rank-two-local-minimum | The all-copy rank-two functional is locally nonnegative near a specified zero family for each fixed copy number
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The 10 October source packet reports internally derived/reconstructed arguments and coordinator or adversarial checks for the stated scopes. This intake preserves and routes those records only; it did not independently reconstruct the proofs, run research scripts, or validate external correctness or historical priority. No historic-scale/foundational breakthrough, physical acquisition, or practical transformative capability is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For q_n(C)=sum_{S subseteq[n]}(-1/2)^|S| ||Tr_S C||_F^2 on complex matrices in M_(3^n), the universal target q_n(C)>=0 for all n and rank(C)<=2 remains unresolved. The source reports that for every fixed n>=1 there is a neighborhood within the rank-at-most-two variety of C0=|0^n><0^n|+(-1)^(n+1)|1^n><1^n| where q_n is nonnegative, with a smooth local zero manifold of real dimension 4*2^n-6+4n; all its points are critical and the Hessian is positive in normal directions. The radius is not uniform in n. An exact block lift shows that uniform local stability at all diag(R,R,0) rank-two zeros would encode the lower-copy global target; a separate high-rank witness defeats one proposed swap-sector concentration route but is not a rank-two counterexample.
Interface: The local theorem is fixed-n, complex rank exactly two near the specified C0 family (the local neighborhood is separated from rank<=1). The global question quantifies over every n and every complex rank<=2 C. The local radius has no uniform lower bound. q_n uses partial trace over the indexed qutrit sites and Frobenius norm.
Proof spine: Construct the explicit smooth zero manifold, prove stationarity, compute the full rank-two chart Hessian including its kernel and positive normal spectrum, then use a positive normal Hessian in adapted coordinates for higher-order local control. Separately derive q_(m+1)(C(t))=t^2 q_m(X) for the exact rank-two block lift and compute the high-rank swap-sector counterexample.
Costs: The argument is a fixed-n local analysis on a rank-two matrix variety of ambient dimension 3^n; its neighborhood radius and quantitative conditioning are not uniform or supplied as usable bounds.
Failure: This proves neither the global q_n inequality nor an NPT bound-entangled state. The exact lift is a barrier to an overbroad local-to-global argument; the swap-sector witness has high rank and is not a negative rank-two C. Two-copy positivity is cited prior art, not a result of this intake.
Closest comparator: The packet cites Song and Chen, https://arxiv.org/html/2607.23416v1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24479v1 for two-copy work, plus Tran et al. 2017 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.03385), a 2024 paper (https://arxiv.org/html/2402.18037v1) and earlier local-minimum work (https://arxiv.org/abs/0711.2613). Citations and originality are not rechecked; no novelty claim is made.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the full fixed-n Hessian/normal-coordinate proof and exact lift. Keep G-ALL-COPY-NPT-UNDISTILLABILITY open until a proof or valid complex rank-two counterexample covers the universal target.

N641-stationary-path-roulette-response-obstruction | A fixed path-reweighting roulette fails on an explicit finite-state response system
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The source records report internal derivations, audits, and finite diagnostics at the stated scope. This intake preserved files and checked hashes/routes only; it did not execute research code, rerun analyses, or independently reconstruct proofs. External correctness and historical priority remain unresolved. No historic-scale foundational breakthrough is established. The negative result concerns one fixed stationary proposal and a specified common-prefix roulette construction, not chaotic response in general.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For a strictly positive column-stochastic finite-state transition matrix P with positive stationary vector h and a fixed strictly positive row-stochastic backward proposal Q, define K[j,i]=P[j,i]^2/Q[j,i]. The source proves ρ(K)≥1, with equality exactly at the Perron twist Q[j,i]=P[j,i]h_i/h_j. In a supplied two-state deterministic piecewise-affine response example, the proposed common-prefix single-term roulette has infinite absolute expectation (and second moment) for every independent full-support level law, while an exact transfer-operator solve gives the response directly. The source also reports four-state slow-mixing stress cases: for δ=10^-3 and absolute-bias target 10^-3, the exact finite-horizon bias requires n≥6212, while its fixed-proposal response-variance lower bound has log10 at least 486.666 and the stated independent-path count for standard deviation 10^-3 has log10 at least 492.666.
Interface: The proposal is fixed at the differentiation point; finite-horizon score estimators are distinguished from roulette estimators. The deterministic realization has a finite Markov partition and is not a claim about globally smooth expanding maps. The four-state family separates uniform inverse-branch contraction from mixing constants that degenerate as δ→0.
Proof spine: A Perron-vector/Cauchy–Schwarz argument gives the spectral radius and equality condition. The explicit map realizes the finite transition matrix exactly. Conditional increment bounds show divergence of the absolute roulette expectation; direct transfer equations provide the exact small-instance comparator.
Costs: The direct finite-state transfer calculation uses standard finite-dimensional linear algebra; the proposed path method samples O(n) transitions per path and has the reported unbounded/infinite roulette cost in this example. No scaling advantage is established. In the reported δ=10^-3 stress case, the variance/path-count lower bounds make this specific estimator impractical; the exact transfer solve remains available for the finite state model.
Failure: The generic eigenfunction-twist principle is prior work, as the source itself notes. The counterexample only defeats the stated fixed stationary proposal and common-prefix single-term roulette. It is not a lower bound for horizon-dependent/adaptive proposals, resampling, control variates, other couplings, all chaotic-response methods, or smooth systems.
Closest comparator: The source compares the Perron twist to Whiteley–Lee, “Twisted particle filters” (arXiv:1210.0220v4), and the single-term estimator identity to Rhee–Glynn/Vihola (arXiv:1512.01022). Generic twist and exact transfer methods are established; priority of this explicit example is unknown.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the finite-state response and non-integrability calculation, and require any replacement estimator to be compared against an acquired transfer-operator baseline with all proposal, bias, variance, and acquisition costs charged.

N642-bool-fourier-local-entropy-modulus | Boolean coordinate restriction has a sharp entropy modulus, but a prescribed-coordinate ratio diverges
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The source records report internal derivations, audits, and finite diagnostics at the stated scope. This intake preserved files and checked hashes/routes only; it did not execute research code, rerun analyses, or independently reconstruct proofs. External correctness and historical priority remain unresolved. No historic-scale foundational breakthrough is established. The result does not refute FEI or the existential good-coordinate route.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For a Boolean f:{−1,1}^n→{−1,1}, let Δ_i(f)=H(f)−(H(f_i^+)+H(f_i^-))/2 and let I_i(f) be coordinate influence under the stated Fourier normalization. With h(t)=−t log_2 t−(1−t)log_2(1−t) and D(t)=h(t)+1−h(1/2+√(t(1−t))), the source proves 0≤Δ_i(f)≤D(I_i(f)) for every coordinate. For every even m≥2 it gives F_m and a distinguished z with p=2^-m, I_z(F_m)=p, Δ_z(F_m)=p log_2(1/p)+(3/ln 2)p−(19/(6 ln 2))p^2+O(p^3), and D(p)−Δ_z(F_m)=2p^2/ln 2+O(p^3), so Δ_z/I_z=m+3/ln 2+O(2^-m), while H(F_m)≤2I(F_m). Thus no universal bound Δ_i(f)≤C I_i(f) can hold for all Boolean functions and all prescribed coordinates.
Interface: All quantities use the source’s Boolean Fourier normalization. The theorem concerns a specified coordinate; the family need not have every coordinate bad.
Proof spine: Pair Fourier coefficients across coordinate i, express the restriction entropy loss as a weighted binary-entropy comparison, derive the modulus, and evaluate the explicit even-m family to second order. The report states the family remains globally FEI-bounded.
Costs: Finite-dimensional exact mathematical construction; no algorithmic or physical cost claim.
Failure: It does not refute the Fourier Entropy–Influence conjecture, does not show that every coordinate in F_m is bad, and does not disprove existence of some coordinate with Δ_i≤C I_i. It only rules out an all-coordinate linear decrement inequality. The equality statement is one-way: upper-bound equality is possible only at influences 0, 1/2, or 1; influence 1/2 alone is not sufficient.
Closest comparator: The source treats coordinate restriction as an existing FEI proof strategy. N601 is a complex-valued relaxation obstruction; N529 concerns a different absolute-product coordinate criterion. Neither is invalidated, and the existential Boolean selection problem remains open.
Open verification: Reconstruct the sharp modulus and equality cases, then independently resolve the existential coordinate-selection question or pursue another FEI route. Do not infer a Boolean FEI counterexample from the prescribed-coordinate family.

status=source_derived_unreviewed; The source records report internal derivations, audits, and finite diagnostics at the stated scope. This intake preserved files and checked hashes/routes only; it did not execute research code, rerun analyses, or independently reconstruct proofs. External correctness and historical priority remain unresolved. No historic-scale foundational breakthrough is established. The source reports an internally closed proof candidate of a published conjecture; no independent proof verification or priority clearance is claimed.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Let W=(W_ij) have the real Wishart law W_p(ν,Σ), with ν>p−1, Σ positive definite, and a block partition p=p_1+⋯+p_r. Under the source convention E exp(−tr(TW))=det(I+2ΣT)^(-ν/2) for T⪰0, the source reports that for all s_i≥0, E∏_{i=1}^r det(W_ii)^{s_i} ≥ ∏_{i=1}^r E det(W_ii)^{s_i}. It also proves the stronger one-block-versus-rest comparison. The statement covers arbitrary real ν in the stated range and arbitrary block count.
Interface: Finite real symmetric positive-definite Wishart scale; real degrees of freedom ν>p−1; disjoint diagonal principal blocks; nonnegative real powers. Expectations are finite under the stated domain. No computational algorithm is claimed.
Proof spine: Condition on one principal block and represent the complement by an explicitly constructed noncentral Wishart law. Prove determinant-product expectation monotonicity in its mean through a rank-one differential identity and a rank-saving decomposition; use determinant-weighted association of ordered Wishart eigenvalues and Wishart regression to finish. The FKG/MTP2 association and boundary steps require independent reconstruction.
Costs: A finite-dimensional analytic inequality; no runtime or sampling improvement is asserted.
Failure: The source’s proof is not independently checked here. This theorem does not supply a sampling algorithm or a new primitive. Historical novelty is unresolved; the two-block case was already known.
Closest comparator: The statement is Conjecture 1.1 in Genest, Ouimet, and Richards, “On the Gaussian product inequality conjecture for disjoint principal minors of Wishart random matrices,” arXiv:2311.00202v3. The authors state that d=2 was proved earlier; see also their two-minor result arXiv:2409.14512. The source reports the all-partition proof; correctness and priority remain UNKNOWN.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the noncentral Wishart Laplace-transform representation, rank-one identity, exact rank reduction at ν>p−1, determinant/FKG association step, conditioning/regression, and limiting arguments. Compare the complete argument with the published Conjecture 1.1 and the known two-block theorem.

Claim: In a homogeneous spatially flat GR model with separately conserved barotropic components p_i=p_i(ρ_i), ρ_i+p_i≥0, and 0≤c_{s,i}^2=dp_i/dρ_i≤1, allowing a separate constant vacuum term, set x=a^-3 and Y(x)=H^2(x). The source derives Y′≥0 and 0≤xY″≤Y′. Hence Y is convex in x and concave in u=x^2. A source-reported BAO-only check found a sequence satisfying these radial shape restrictions within 0.781 marginal standard deviations of each of six radial measurements, with reported constrained-fit χ²=0.9542; it reports no compelling violation.
Interface: Assumes flat homogeneous GR, separate conservation, barotropic pressure response, the stated null-energy and causal sound-speed bounds, and the source’s DESI DR2 compressed radial-distance likelihood. Does not cover interacting fluids, all scalar-field models, modified gravity, or non-flat cosmology.
Proof spine: Use x=a^-3 and separate conservation to derive xρ′=ρ+p and xρ″=c_s^2ρ′. Sum densities in the flat Friedmann equation to get Y′≥0 and 0≤xY″≤Y′; transform to u=x² for concavity. The report evaluates the finite radial constraints in inverse-square distance coordinates without assuming Gaussian errors there.
Costs: The source reports 13 compressed DESI distances with covariance for its ΛCDM baseline and six radial distances for the shape test; the actual input files and code are absent from this intake, so those calculations are not reproducible from the preserved report alone.
Failure: These are necessary shape conditions, not a characterization or identification of dark energy. An acceptable BAO-only fit does not resolve DESI+CMB+supernova comparisons and is not a new law. The numerical values remain source-reported and unverified by this intake.
Closest comparator: The source identifies barotropic-fluid predecessors. The BAO measurement source is DESI DR2 Results II, arXiv:2503.14738; this intake’s report-level shape check is distinct from the collaboration’s combined-probe cosmological inference.

Claim: For normalized initial and final nuclear states with J_i=3/2 and J_f=1/2, the stated one-body Gamow–Teller operator and reduced transition-density convention imply, for every bounded radial test function |h(r)|≤1, |M[h]|≤√((16/3)N_iZ_f), hence ∫_0^∞4πr²|ρ(r)|dr≤√((16/3)N_iZ_f). For 71Ga→71Ge with N_i=40 and Z_f=32, the source gives 82.6236447191. It also reports the pointwise relaxation |ρ(r)|²≤(16/3)p(r)n(r) and its associated weighted L² constraint. Under its conditional profile normalization, it reports that modified double- and triple-Gaussian fits exceed the bound; the single- and ordinary double-Gaussian fits do not.
Interface: The bound assumes normalized nuclear states, a one-body spin-isospin current with g_A factored out, the specified reduced-matrix-element normalization, and the 3/2→1/2 spin transition. It does not include effective multi-nucleon axial currents.
Proof spine: Removing a proton from the final state and a neutron from the initial state produces vectors in the same residual-nucleus space. Particle-number norms and Wigner–Eckart give a finite spin-coupling matrix whose reported KK† spectrum is {4/3,4/3,4/3,0}; Cauchy–Schwarz yields the coefficient. The source also derives a local density inequality and weighted norm constraint.
Costs: No acquisition or experiment is part of this analytic bound. Profile integrals are source-reported closed-form/numerical calculations; this intake did not rerun them.
Failure: The application depends on an independent audit that the published fitted scalar profiles have exactly the stated reduced one-body density meaning. The captured report omits a fetchable source identifier and the profile files. Passing the bound is not sufficient for physical realizability; failure of selected fits does not rule out all nuclear explanations or solve the anomaly.
Closest comparator: The report states that transition-density realizability is an established research topic and does not claim priority. The source paper/version and density convention need to be recovered from the omitted companion materials before comparing profiles.
Open verification: Recover the exact 30 September 2026 fit paper and profiles, independently verify the reduced-density/electron-kernel normalization, and reconstruct the angular algebra and integral values. Keep one-body and multi-nucleon-current scopes separate.

Claim: For weak mediator interactions additive over neutrons and with isotope-independent electronic response, first-order shifts of transition j satisfy δν_j^new(A,40)=X_j(A−40). A sum or integrable continuum of mediators changes X_j but does not create another isotope direction under these assumptions. In the source’s four-isotope calcium fit, it reports Q_required=+1.979934960 GHz·u² versus Q_recoil=−1.012869689 GHz·u² using published central recoil coefficients.
Interface: First-order perturbative shifts, neutron-additive coupling, isotope-independent electronic response, and the source’s 729 nm/570 nm calcium transitions and four-isotope data. Nuclear polarization is omitted from the comparison.
Proof spine: Linearity makes every mediator contribution proportional to the same isotope vector A−40 for each transition; integrating/summing mediators only changes its scalar coefficient. Eliminating the leading radius term yields the reported opposite-sign required/recoil coefficient comparison.
Costs: The calculation is a finite isotope-shift algebra/fit; source data, covariance, and code are not present in the attached record, and no acquisition/runtime claim is made.
Failure: It does not exclude nonfactorized or nonlinear new physics and is not evidence for a new force. The missing nuclear-polarization contribution is identified by the source as a potentially adequate Standard Model explanation; the comparison is incomplete.
Closest comparator: The source cites the calcium King-plot experiment; the primary PRL reports nuclear polarization as a potentially large remaining Standard Model contribution: https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.134.233002. This intake’s calculation remains source-reported and does not supersede that analysis.
Open verification: Recover the exact isotope-shift dataset and fit artifacts, include a quantitatively supported nuclear-polarization term, and repeat the matched comparison before making a new-force inference.

Claim: Let `alpha` be the unique root in `(1/2,3/5)` of `h(alpha)+(1-alpha) ln 5=ln 4`. For independent one-mode inputs `rho_A=diag(alpha,(1-alpha)/5,...,(1-alpha)/5)` on Fock levels 0..5 and vacuum `rho_B`, the source gives `N(rho_A)=1`, `N(rho_B)=0`. At every gain `G>1`, the output vacuum eigenvalue `alpha/G` exceeds `1/(2G)`, the largest eigenvalue of the entropy-matched thermal output. Universal thermal-output majorization therefore fails for this mixed input at Ky Fan `k=1`.
Interface: One-mode quantum-limited amplifier; independent inputs; finite support; `G>1`; entropy in nats and one-mode `N=g^{-1}(S)`. The mean of `rho_A` is `3(1-alpha)<3/2`.
Proof spine: The Fock transition law leaves output vacuum mass `alpha/G`; comparator thermal mean is `2G-1` and its top eigenvalue is `1/(2G)`. Use `alpha>1/2`.
Costs: Exact finite-support witness; no acquisition, asymptotic, or runtime claim.
Failure: Does not refute scalar von Neumann EPnI, settle pure-product-input majorization, or establish a channel-output entropy counterexample. It closes only the unrestricted spectral-majorization shortcut.
Closest comparator: N557 EPnI remains a separate source-derived, unreviewed claim. The note cites a nearby sharp-Young route; no novelty claim is made.

Claim: At gain two, the vacuum amplifier output `tau` has eigenvalues `2^(-k-1)` and `Tr(tau^m)=1/(2^m-1)`. Claim: For independent pure inputs `f=g=(50|0>+|3>)/sqrt(2501)`, gain `G=2`, and `t=1000`, the source proves `log det_F(I+t rho_output)-log det_F(I+t tau)<0` using an exact rational sign and remainder. Thus thermal Fredholm-determinant dominance fails even for pure product inputs. A separate larger cubic perturbation has a reported outward interval for the full determinant gap.
Interface: Two independent pure finite-energy one-mode inputs to a gain-two amplifier; fixed Fredholm-determinant parameter `t=1000`.
Proof spine: A rationally bounded negative second variation dominates an explicit remainder at `epsilon=1/(100 t^3)`; the separate finite-cutoff check uses an exact tail bound.
Costs: Existence at a fixed gain and determinant parameter; no uniform algorithm or acquisition claim.
Failure: Refutes determinant dominance and the stronger all-pure-product thermal-majorization route only. It does not establish a von Neumann entropy violation or refute EPnI.
Closest comparator: The source says the vacuum-idler Gaussian-channel theorem is unaffected; no novelty or priority claim is made.
Open verification: Independently audit the exact sign and remainder if using this obstruction. EPnI needs another route.

Claim: For the source's two-pure-input gain-two perturbation around vacuum, the second variation of the reduced output's third elementary symmetric polynomial is nonnegative by excitation sector. It vanishes for displacement (`m=1`) and the common-squeezing tangent (`m=2`); transverse sectors are strictly positive, including a uniform rational margin for `m>=4`. This is local at the vacuum product point.
Interface: Two independent pure one-mode inputs perturbed near vacuum under gain-two two-mode squeezing; the object is a local second variation of `e_3` of the reduced output spectrum.
Proof spine: Expand amplitudes to second order, decompose into number-shift sectors and apply exact rational bounds; different sectors have no mixed diagonal-trace term.
Costs: Local perturbation only; no global search or runtime claim.
Failure: Does not prove global `e_3` minimization, determinant order, or arbitrary-input EPnI. Local positivity cannot cover all high-purity inputs.
Closest comparator: A local consistency check for a proof mechanism, not a new entropy theorem or priority claim.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the Hessian and establish the missing global channel-specific inequality before inferring from local stability.

Claim: Take `K=[diag(1,a)]^{tensor n}`, `a=1/4`, `r=3/2`, `T=4`, so each product factor is zero-free because `a r^2=9/16<1`, and `M=diag(1,b)^{tensor n}` with `b=a^T=1/256`. Its best rank-one relative operator error is `b`, but `D(M/Tr M,|0^n><0^n|)=1-(1+b)^(-n)`, exceeding `0.999` at `n=4096`.
Interface: A supplied positive diagonal tensor family and zero-free radius condition; conclusion concerns normalized global state distance, not local observables.
Proof spine: Eigenvalue products give relative operator error `b`; normalization includes all configurations and gives the trace-distance identity.
Costs: Exact product formulas; no general algorithmic lower bound or complexity advantage.
Failure: Blocks only the direct inference from small relative operator error to normalized thermal sampling, partition accuracy or state preparation. Does not invalidate N638 or bound all algorithms/local observables.
Closest comparator: The source calls this an interface counterexample, not a novelty claim.
Open verification: A thermal-transfer claim needs separate normalized partition-mass and end-to-end cost guarantees.
