STATUS AND AUTHORITY
The 16-page source calls itself a research proof draft, says internal analytic checks were performed, and states that external review is pending. This intake preserves the PDF and a page-separated extraction, checked the original/copy hash, and inspected rendered pages. It did not reconstruct the proof, replay scientific diagnostics, verify the imported premises, or check priority. The result remains source_derived_unreviewed; external correctness, formal verification, and historical priority are UNKNOWN.

SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
The classified inputs are finite-dimensional channels supplied by valid rational-complex Choi matrices, with positivity and trace preservation exact. Individual references, code blocks, and blocklengths are finite but have no uniform bound. Q and P denote the usual unassisted regularized quantum and private capacities, respectively; the source allows finite ensembles of mixed states entangled across channel uses. It makes no catalyst, preshared-entanglement, feedback, or postselection assumption.

SOURCE-REPORTED MAIN CLAIM
Assuming the source's uniformly gapped channel-order reduction and complete-order equivalence, exact-zero quantum-capacity and exact-zero private-capacity sets for finite rational channels are each coRE-complete under computable many-one reductions. Their positive-capacity complements are each RE-complete. The claimed reduction maps a machine M and input x to a rational channel T(M,x)=C(M,x) tensor E_{2,1/2}, with

    M(x) does not halt  =>  Q(T(M,x)) = P(T(M,x)) = 0,
    M(x) halts          =>  Q(T(M,x)) > 0 and P(T(M,x)) > 0.

This is an exact zero-versus-positive claim. The source does not claim capacity approximation hardness, a fixed-gap promise result, an efficient reduction, a computable bound on a positive witness blocklength, or a practical code construction.

SOURCE-REPORTED KERNEL INTERFACE
The assumed wrapper data has finite sector spaces H0,H1; finitely many positive rational effects A_i and B_i summing to the identities on their respective sectors; and rational rectangular cross-numerators O_i^s for s in {E,B}. For fixed positive rational gamma, finite rational B, and a common quadratic seminorm V, the companion source supplies the following uniform alternatives. In its nonhalting case, for every finite reference, positive definite baselines R0,R1, and complex cross-coordinate Z, the forms obey F_E-F_B >= gamma V and F_E+F_B <= B V. In its halting case, some finite faithful R0,R1 and some Z satisfy F_E-F_B < 0. The source says these gap parameters do not depend on a halting-witness dimension. N684 reports a physical completion only for this supplied, uniformly gapped family.

REPORTED NEW BRIDGE
The source reports a genuine rational Stinespring completion for the uniformly gapped inverse-Jordan kernel family supplied by the companion N675 channel-order construction. In the positive-source case it claims complete environmental SLD dominance for coherent inputs, arbitrary Hermitian tangents, and every finite reference, without a reference-size or state-conditioning bound; in the negative-source case it transfers a strict finite witness. The proposed construction combines coherent hub-channel control, exact purification duality for the physical leaf scores, sector-copy padding, and rational Gram/Stinespring factors. It is specific to the uniformly gapped source family, not a completion theorem for arbitrary ungapped POVM pairs.

The source also reports a zero-rate compilation of each fixed finite-dimensional half-erasure helper into repeated uses of the fixed qubit half-erasure channel. Random isometric encodings, an input-independent erasure-mask threshold, receiver decoders, and explicit failure flags are claimed to converge to the logical helper in diamond norm as blocklength grows. This removes a finite-helper-dimension dependence for positivity, but supplies no computable or efficient code-length bound. The proof applies continuity after private-to-quantum activation; it does not identify the physical erased subsystem with an ideal helper complement.

The final chain additionally uses the N675 complete-SLD/complete-relative-entropy source equivalence and the N676 fixed-qubit half-erasure capacity criterion. N675 and N676 remain source-derived and unreviewed. Their inclusion here is a reported proof dependency, not validation of either source.

LIMITS AND NEXT REVIEW
The source reports finite-dimensional rational channel descriptions and an exact qualitative classification only. Its positive-capacity witnesses may require arbitrarily large blocklengths; no uniform witness bound, practical implementation, resource advantage, or external correctness certificate is supplied. A specialist review should first reconstruct the rational complementary-channel completion and its unrestricted-reference SLD inequality, then verify the zero-rate helper compiler and the dependency chain from N675/N676 to the exact capacity classification. The source cites MIP*=RE, Smith-Yard activation, and Devetak's capacity formulas; the intake did not independently verify their stated applications.

RELATION TO EXISTING RECORDS
N675 supplies the companion channel-order hardness candidate and unrestricted complete-order equivalence used by the source. N676 already records the fixed-qubit half-erasure zero-capacity criterion and historically noted that a complement-preserving hardness bridge was missing. N684 reports a candidate construction addressing that bridge. This scoped follow-up does not certify the construction or close the mathematical gate. No earlier card or checkpoint was overwritten; the current dossier records the added source and its exact scope.

N685-early-flag-causalization-obstruction | Early flag deadlines obstruct resource-preserving causalization
status=source_derived_unreviewed; the supplied report contains explicit constructions and proof narratives. This intake preserved source bytes and checked routes only. No independent reconstruction, external correctness review, formal verification, or historical-priority assessment was performed. No historic-scale breakthrough is claimed.
frontier_disposition=one scoped continuation of the N683 catalyst-removal/sequential-cost family; not a duplicate of the parent theorem family.
Symbols, costs, and operation interfaces are local to this record. The complete supplied source is updates/DO/package/early_flag_causalization/SOURCE_REPORT.txt.

RESULT: INPUT-INDEPENDENT FLAG, DIFFERENT EARLY-INPUT COST
Let N:AB -> A'B' be a finite-dimensional bipartite channel. Let R discard its input and prepare a fixed product state. For 0<p<1 define

    H_{p,N}(X) = p |11><11|_{F_A F_B} tensor N(X)
                 + (1-p) |00><00|_{F_A F_B} tensor R(X).

For every input X, including one entangled with an external reference, the flag marginal is

    tr_{A'B'} H_{p,N}(X) = tr(X)[p|11><11|+(1-p)|00><00|].

The late-flag task supplies the input before the flag is produced. The early-flag task requires the shared flag to be announced first; the quantum input may be selected in response, and flag 1 requires N while flag 0 requires R. These are ordinary definite-time processes with different output deadlines.

The source reports that if N is separable but outside closure(LOCC), D=d_A d_B, and p=1/D, then H_{p,N} as a complete late-flag channel is LOCC, while the early-flag process is not arbitrarily approximable by causal LOCC. For a product-Kraus decomposition N(X)=sum_j (A_j tensor B_j)X(A_j tensor B_j)^dagger, set a_j=||A_j||_F, b_j=||B_j||_F, and lambda_j=a_j^2 b_j^2. Trace preservation gives sum_j lambda_j=D. Sample a shared index j with probability lambda_j/D and apply local success filters A_j/a_j and B_j/b_j, which are contractions. The exact success subchannel is

    sum_j (lambda_j/D)(A_j/a_j tensor B_j/b_j)X(A_j/a_j tensor B_j/b_j)^dagger = N(X)/D.

On any filter failure reset to R and announce flag 0. This realizes the complete flagged channel with input-independent success probability 1/D. For an early flag, however, the shared memory conditioned on flag 1 remains separable before the fresh input arrives, so its conditional future channel must be LOCC; this contradicts N outside closure(LOCC). Robustness is argued by taking any approximating sequence with success probabilities q_j -> p and conditional channels L_j in LOCC: q_j L_j -> pN and p>0 imply L_j -> N, contradicting N outside closure(LOCC).

FINITE-BLOCK ROUTING AND COST IDENTITY
Let e_N(k,m) denote the infimum adaptive distinguishing error for k sequential uses of N with m supplied ebits; define e_H(n,m) analogously for n early-flag uses. Error is the maximum adaptive external distinguishing advantage, normalized to [0,1]. For K distributed as Binomial(n,p), the report claims, for either unassisted definitions throughout or exact-catalyst-assisted definitions throughout,

    e_H(n,m) <= e_N(k,m) + Pr[K > k],
    e_N(k,m) <= e_H(n,m) + Pr[K < k].

The same entanglement budget is used in each direction. With catalysts, the same catalyst is retained. In the first routing direction, genuine inputs are sent only on successful flags; overflow is exceptional. In the reverse direction, zero flags receive dummy product inputs, and shortage is exceptional. Unused simulator calls are completed with dummy product inputs and discarded outputs, so the simulator reaches its end-of-horizon return condition.

Passing to rates with k near (p+delta)n and (p-delta)n gives the reported exact identities

    E_early(H_{p,N}) = p E_seq(N),
    E_early^cat(H_{p,N}) = p E_seq^cat(N).

These identities are presented for every N under the source's sequential simulation definitions. For catalysts, return is exact as a marginal at the end of the complete simulation for every allowed input interaction; correlations with retained outputs are allowed, catalyst dimension is any finite value with no prescribed bound, and the routing must complete the horizon. The report does not claim the identity under approximate return or a fixed nonadaptive test-only return condition.

DIRECT ARGUMENTS AND PARENT-DEPENDENT CONSEQUENCES
The flag law, late-flag LOCC construction, early-deadline obstruction, finite-block inequalities, and cost-identity reduction are proof narratives in this supplied source and are stated there without relying on the strict-positivity conclusion of N683. The selected-channel conclusion E_early^cat(H_{p,N})>0, and the resulting maximal-error statement for sublinear supplied entanglement when N is outside closure(LOCC), use the source-reported sequential-cost classification in N683. N683 remains source_derived_unreviewed; this dependency does not validate either result.

NINE-DOMINO-STATE EXAMPLE
In C^3 tensor C^3, use the orthonormal product basis

    |1>|1>,
    |0>|0 plus-or-minus 1>,   |2>|1 plus-or-minus 2>,
    |0 plus-or-minus 1>|2>,   |1 plus-or-minus 2>|0>,

where |u plus-or-minus v>=(|u> plus-or-minus |v>)/sqrt(2). Let M(rho)=sum_{j=1}^9 <a_j b_j|rho|a_j b_j> |jj><jj|. Its Kraus operators |j><a_j| tensor |j><b_j| are product, so M is separable. The report cites a strictly positive LOCC discrimination gap for this basis, implying M is outside closure(LOCC), and sets p=1/9. Thus the late-flag block channel is LOCC while the early-flag cost is reported as E_early^cat(H_{1/9,M})=(1/9)E_seq^cat(M)>0, conditional on N683. All external outputs in this example are classical; the asserted resource is the temporal interface, not entanglement in the Choi operator.

NEGATIVE RESEARCH CAPITAL: CAUSALIZATION DOES NOT PRESERVE THE RESOURCE
The report refutes the proposed general principle that an LOCC complete block operation satisfying the no-backward-signalling equations must have an LOCC realization respecting the earlier-output causal order. It also refutes the inference that input-independent success probability makes the normalized successful branch a deterministic/free LOCC channel. Here the successful branch is pN with (pN)^dagger(I)=pI, but N can lie outside closure(LOCC).

This does not contradict semicausal-to-semilocalizable realization results that permit quantum communication; those results do not promise preservation of a zero-entanglement LOCC implementation. It also does not refute the original memoryless parallel question

    N outside closure(LOCC)  =>?  E_parallel^cat(N)>0.

The early-flag task adds an internal interaction stage and is not an ordinary memoryless channel. A general collective block-level test separating N^tensor n from arbitrary collective LOCC, with the required exponential gap, remains missing in the source. The unrestricted parallel entanglement-cost question remains unresolved.

status=source_derived_unreviewed; the supplied report gives a complete proof narrative for its stated infinite-dimensional LOCC model. This intake preserved the report and its hashes; it did not reconstruct the proof or replay its linked finite checks. External correctness, formal verification, historical priority and efficient physical preparation remain UNKNOWN. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.
Symbols and assumptions are local to this card; use the exact report ranges before applying the result.

INTERFACE
For a pure bipartite reservoir c, let C(c) be the finite-dimensional bipartite channels N for which a finite-round LOCC instrument has a success branch S satisfying S(X tensor |c><c|)=p N(X) tensor |c><c| for every input operator X, including reference extensions, with p>0 independent of X. The complete instrument is trace-preserving; the reservoir is returned exactly and uncorrelated on success only. Failure may damage it without restriction. Communication rounds are finite but have no uniform bound; finite or countable outcomes and bounded local Kraus operators are allowed. No uncharged entangled ancillas, infinite-round closure or nonnormal operations are included. This is not deterministic LOCC.

THEOREM CANDIDATE — COMPLEMENTARY SPECTRA
The report constructs computable pure states c_P,c_Q on countable-dimensional local spaces, each with finite entanglement entropy and finite mean energy for H|n>=(n-1)|n>, such that for every finite k>=1,

    C(c_P^{⊗ k})=C(c_Q^{⊗ k})=SEP,
    C(c_P⊗c_Q)=all finite-dimensional bipartite channels.

The first equality requires exact return of the supplied reservoir on success. SEP channels remain available by the source's stated stochastic implementation. The joint reservoir can emit one Bell pair with probability 1/4 and return both reservoirs exactly on that successful branch; m repeated extractions succeed with probability 4^-m. A finite number of Bell pairs then implements any fixed finite-dimensional channel by teleporting its input and output. The protocol permits failure-branch loss and is not deterministic extraction.

PROOF MECHANISM
For squared Schmidt coefficients lambda_1>=lambda_2>=..., write t_n=sum_{j>=n}lambda_j. The report proves that inf_{n:t_n>0} t_{2n}/t_n=0 implies C(c)=SEP, using convex-roof strong monotones E_r and an entangled Choi-state test; it therefore excludes channels with any entangled Choi state, not only distillable outputs.

For a computable partition P,Q of the primes, set M(P)={a>=1: all prime factors of a lie in P}, Z_P=sum_{a in M(P)}a^-3, and |c_P>=Z_P^-1/2 sum_{a in M(P)}a^-3/2 |a,a>. Unique factorization makes c_P tensor c_Q locally equivalent on their supports to |Z>=zeta(3)^-1/2 sum_{n>=1} n^-3/2 |n,n>. A bounded relabelling, parity split and diagonal contraction implement |Z> -> (1/2)|Z> tensor |Phi_2>. An alternating finite-prime construction protects tail bottlenecks for every finite tensor power of each separate state. The report gives exact arithmetic termination arguments and finite energy/entropy bounds.

CONSEQUENCE FOR N680 — DISTINCT RESOURCE CONTRACT
The report further claims that placing this fixed countable-dimensional state Z between B,C gives, for nonzero finite three-tensors T,S, exact bounded local-map conversion T tensor Z >= S tensor Z iff rank(T_{A|BC})>=rank(S_{A'|B'C'}). This is a scoped extension of N680's exact tensor-restriction context, not a change to N680: N680 uses a finite maximally entangled catalyst and separate tensor maps, whereas this consequence uses an infinite-support bipartite pure reservoir, finite-round LOCC, and the exact success-branch/failure-loss contract above. Neither result validates the other.

LIMITS AND REVIEW
Exact infinite support is essential: every finite-support truncation loses the self-returning extraction property. The construction gives no efficient prime-partition runtime, finite exact-state preparation circuit, bounded-time physical realization, positive lower bound for repeated success, or approximate finite-resource theorem. The report supplies a mixed-reservoir counterexample to an unrestricted all-or-nothing extension. It identifies substantial prior work on infinite-dimensional SLOCC, finite-energy tail effects, embezzlement and superactivation; priority for this exact complementary-prime construction remains unresolved. Linked verification code and result files are not included in the supplied files; the report's finite checks are source-reported only.

status=source_derived_unreviewed; the campaign reports internal reconstruction of the fixed-exponent sampler candidate and selected analytic identities. This intake preserved the reports, source pins and diagnostics only; it did not independently reconstruct proofs, run scientific scripts, establish novelty or certify an end-to-end polylogarithmic sampler. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.
Symbols and assumptions are local to this card; exact source reports control.

INTERFACE AND STRONGEST END-TO-END CANDIDATE
For every fixed a>0, the campaign reports a candidate using whole-vector value queries to a globally L-Lipschitz conservative field g=grad F, with F in C^{1,1}, and fixed sigma/L>0, to approximate N(E g(G), sigma^2 I_d) within total variation epsilon using C_a d^a poly_a(1/epsilon) queries on every execution and polynomial real-arithmetic/storage cost. It supplies no derivative, vector-Jacobian, potential-value or conditional-mean access. Exact-real Gaussian seeds are part of the model; a finite-bit output requires comparison to a commonly rounded target. This fixed-a bound does not imply polylogarithmic queries: constants, interpolation order and expression-tree height depend on a, and the attempted retuning incurs larger dimension-dependent cost.

NEWTON–STEIN RIGHT INVERSE — BASELINE ONLY
For symmetric matrix residual R_m in homogeneous Gaussian chaos m, the report constructs a skew-gauge right inverse to the baseline linearized Gaussian Stein operator. With Frobenius norms for matrix fields it reports dimension- and degree-independent bounds

    ||D u||_2 <= ||R||_2,       ||J_u||_2 <= (2+sqrt(2)) ||R||_2.

This exact baseline inverse leaves a quadratic residual for the full nonlinear equation. The full perturbed operator includes K D_G u, unbounded on ordinary Gaussian L2; therefore the baseline bounds do not justify a Neumann series or close the full inverse. Acquiring all actions and implementing a positive full-law Newton step with an every-execution polylogarithmic query cap remain open.

TWO-QUERY BOUNDED STEIN ACTION
Given v!=0, u=v/||v||, Z_perp~N(0,I-uu^T), R=s chi_3, the report defines

    J_s(c;v)=||v|| [g(c+s Z_perp+R u)-g(c+s Z_perp-R u)]/(2R).

It claims E[J_s(c;v)|c,v]=E[Dg(c+sZ)]v and ||J_s(c;v)||<=L||v|| on every execution. A random smoothing scale also supplies the Stein-resolvent action at two value queries. This removes an assumed derivative action but does not produce one realized symmetric matrix, its square root, or the needed Gaussian completion. The uniform–chi_3 representation has classical antecedents; originality of this particular action is unresolved.

FAILURES AND DECISIVE GAP
The frozen-source central-secant rotation fails on g_k(x)=sin(kx)/k: the report gives a nonvanishing small-time variance defect. This refutes that channel, not the exact two-query action or the sampling target. Covariance matching and an unbiased expected matrix action do not specify the full Gaussian law or a realized matrix. The generic expected-matrix-action lower bound is not a lower bound for active deterministic gradient-value queries. The decisive gate remains an acquired positive full-law construction with all adaptive centers, source noise, precision, tail, arithmetic and query costs charged. N125 blocks only its stated positive-Newton exactness route; N590 and N663 have different sampler interfaces and guarantees.

EVIDENCE AND STATUS
The campaign pins Astra at 3922ba9bd94585248f275f29cd1fa4257058d080 and OpenAI/math at fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb. Read the R16, R21, R22 and R28 source files and the scoped findings excerpts before relying on any claim.

status=source_derived_unreviewed; the campaign reports internally developed range and guarded-history arguments plus finite rational diagnostics. This intake preserved their source reports and available code/results; it did not independently reconstruct the proofs or run the diagnostics. No general polynomial-cost encoder, external correctness, formal certification or historical priority is established. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.
Symbols and assumptions are local to this card; exact source reports control.

ANGLE-INDEPENDENT RANGE COMPARISON
For injective maps M,N from the same r-dimensional domain,

    D_tr(unif Ran M, unif Ran N) <= rank(M-N)/r.

The report applies this rank-charge bound to truncate selected connected components in a graph construction, with logarithmic truncation length under its stated component assumptions. The claim concerns uniform states on the ranges themselves; it does not establish the state produced by applying a map to a uniform logical input. Preparing the target range, satisfying the logical constraints and achieving polynomial cost when local dimensions vary remain open.

GUARDED HISTORY LIFT — CONDITIONAL CONTRACT
For an old bad projector C and a fresh site B, the report bounds the low-source component by rank(P_lo)<=alpha d_B rank(C)/(1-eta), retaining the fresh guard on the input effect. A bounded-branch history construction is further conditional: branch count at most b, each lifted creation norm at most sqrt(alpha), alpha<=1/(16 b^2), and t=1/(2 sqrt(b)) give a reported weighted history-resolvent norm at most 2 and eraser norm at most 2/sqrt(3). An acquired common decoder/orthogonal logical chart block and the exact K-valued recurrence are required; with those premises the report states success probability at least 3/16. The recurrence, low-polar implementation, logical root preparation and disconnected-component composition are not supplied as a complete general encoder. This is a conditional acquisition result, not an end-to-end algorithm.

FAILURES, PREDECESSORS, AND NEXT GATE
Bell-projector chains have exponentially small Hilbert–Schmidt word weight but normalized source/range rank fraction 1/d^2 at every length; word weight cannot replace a normalized-state estimate. Keeping the original degree-zero row map and asserting a bounded contracting homotopy would imply a spectral gap, so higher source labels alone do not remove that requirement. The global product-chart argument is identified as existing R01 capital, not a new result. N98 already records that history erasure is not free in general; this continuation gives only a conditional case with acquired structure and does not invalidate that boundary. The decisive next step is an actual positive selected-range encoder/decoder for arbitrary low-rank noncommuting local rows, with normalization, source constraints, precision and variable-local-dimension cost polynomial.

EVIDENCE
Read the R23 and R24 continuation reports, exact findings ranges and preserved diagnostic files under updates/DP/package/foundational_campaign/FINAL_ROUND/. Reported finite diagnostics are not general proof certification.

N689-bounded-exchange-unbiased-rounding-classification | Bounded exchange width characterizes uniformly bounded unbiased rounding
status=source_derived_unreviewed. The pasted report presents a complete proof candidate; no independent proof reconstruction, formal certification, or priority review was done at intake.

For a nonempty Boolean-vertex polytope P=conv(V), V⊆{0,1}^n, define κ(P) as the largest number of coordinates changed by an edge of P. Let R(P) be the least D such that for every matrix A with Euclidean column norms at most one and every x∈P, there is a distribution on V with E[Y]=x and ||A(Y−x)||∞≤D almost surely. The report claims, for k=κ(P)≥1,

    k/2 ≤ R(P) ≤ 4096 k^3 + 48 k.

For a singleton R(P)=0. Thus a family has uniformly bounded R(P) exactly when its exchange widths are uniformly bounded. Exact marginals follow by objective-aware existence for each linear objective and a separation argument; at most n+1 support points suffice.

For matroid bases, k≤2, giving the source-reported existence bound 32864 under the stated column normalization. For a 0–1 matrix with at most Δ ones per column, the stated bound becomes 32864√Δ. The one-objective cost guarantee does not claim that every output of one unbiased distribution is cost-nonincreasing. No polynomial-time sampler or efficient constrained rounding algorithm is established: the proof uses a compact nonconvex minimization for existence.

The reported proof spine is a face-dimension lemma dim(F)≥s(F)/k, an energy-corrected spectral barrier and a finite face-descent argument, followed by separation for exact marginals. The lower bound uses an exposed edge changing k coordinates. A failed quartic minimization example defeats that proposed construction only. An even-cycle example shows why the stated extension does not cover arbitrary intersections of two matroids.

Scope relative to existing Astra records: N14 concerns small-mass cube rounding with supplied signing machinery and a stable-law support counterexample. N24 gives executable rational methods for sparse cube and partition-base settings with separate bounds and costs. N689 is a geometric classification for general Boolean-vertex polytopes with bounded exchange width; its upper proof is existential and does not supply N24-style implementation. It neither revises nor validates N14/N24, and it does not close P-round.

The report attributes the spectral-signing engine to Guo–Fang–Lu (https://arxiv.org/html/2609.23540v1) and compares the matroid application with Bérczi–Liu–Reis–Tarnawski (https://arxiv.org/html/2608.13983v1). These are source-reported prior-art links; exact novelty remains UNKNOWN.

The source reports symbolic identities, rational checks, 255 nonempty cube vertex-subset face tests, and eight floating-point 128-variable curvature diagnostics. No executable package or receipts were attached, and intake did not rerun these checks. An efficient replacement for the nonconvex minimization, standalone proof acquisition, independent correctness, and historical priority remain open. No historic-scale breakthrough is claimed.

N690-contractive-gradient-descent-rate-uncomputability | Contractive gradient descent can have uncomputable loss-decay exponents
status=source_derived_unreviewed. The pasted report provides a proof narrative and reports finite exact checks; this intake did not independently reconstruct the proof, run its code, or review priority.

For each fixed rational 0<ε<1, the report constructs a fixed rational finite-dimensional C^{1,1} objective formed from positive quadratic regularization and nonnegative squared-ReLU terms. It has unique minimizer zero, condition number at most (1+ε)/(1−ε), and the ordinary unit-step full-batch gradient map G is globally ε-contractive. Only a rational starting point varies. A polynomial-time encoding E of a finite program and input is claimed to satisfy

    Λ(E(w)) = lim_{t→∞} −(1/t) log₂(f(G^t E(w))/f(E(w)))

with two fixed values, 2k−2 if the computation accepts and 2k if it never accepts. The report concludes that approximating this actual asymptotic logarithmic loss-decay exponent to 1/3 additive accuracy is undecidable. This is not a claim that minimization is hard: the minimizer is known to be zero. Absolute-error state prediction is source-reported as easy under contraction.

The proposed gradient-exchange mechanism starts from p(a,b)=¼[σ(a+b)^2−σ(a−b)^2−σ(b)^2+σ(−b)^2], with ∇p(a,0)=(0,σ(a)) and ∇p(0,b)=(b/2,0). An extension of a recurrent ReLU map outside its valid nonnegative region supplies the reverse transfer needed for one scalar potential. Ordinary gradient descent then simulates one recurrent update every two steps while the on-trajectory loss stays exactly quadratic. The source further claims a fixed-threshold finite-horizon problem is EXPTIME-complete when T is supplied in binary, and ¼-accurate prediction of the finite-horizon logarithmic rate is EXPTIME-hard.

Reported interface boundaries are essential: exact rational bit lengths grow with time; fixed dimensionality is not fixed memory. The construction does not establish hardness at constant physical precision, for analytic/C² losses, other learning rates, or gradient flow. It establishes neither hardness of finding a minimizer nor general online-gradient universality. The source distinguishes the online-gradient result of Chatziafratis–Roughgarden–Wang (https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.01280) and Welper’s stop-gradient/conditional-gradient construction (https://arxiv.org/html/2007.13664v1); historical priority remains UNKNOWN.

The response reports 777 exact finite algebra/trajectory assertions and a 10-dimensional rate-switch instance with K=584, ρ=1/4096, k=12, and predicted exponents 24 and 22. The universal interpreter is not numerically instantiated. Displayed logarithms were converted to floating point; exact updates/equality checks are source-reported. No elapsed runtime, standalone manuscript, code, or result bundle was included in the upload, and intake did not replay the checks.

The theorem’s undecidability claim, EXPTIME reduction and full universal compiler remain unreviewed. The exact initiating prompt and linked proof/code packages were not supplied. No optimization-hardness claim or historic-scale breakthrough is made.

status=source_derived_unreviewed. The supplied report contains complete proof narratives and source-reported exact diagnostics. This intake did not reconstruct the proofs or rerun the diagnostics. Correctness and historical priority remain UNKNOWN; no historic breakthrough is claimed.

INTERFACE
Let σ_AB be a finite-dimensional bipartite state. A preparation uses a finite-dimensional catalyst τ_{C_A C_B}, separable additional inputs, and a successful branch S of an LOCC instrument such that S(τ)=p Ω_{AB,C} for p>0, tr_C Ω=σ, and tr_AB Ω=τ. The catalyst is returned exactly in its success-conditioned marginal; Ω may correlate output and catalyst. Failure is unrestricted. This is state preparation, not a universally reusable channel implementation.

THEOREM FAMILY — FINITE SUPPORT CRITERION
The report claims these are equivalent:
1. σ admits the stated stochastic marginal-return preparation.
2. range(σ) contains a nonzero product vector.
3. σ=wω+(1−w)χ for a separable state ω and 0<w≤1.

When the criterion holds, the construction uses local catalyst dimensions at most d_A+1 and d_B+1. The necessity proof applies to every finite catalyst and every p>0, and remains valid for separable operations. A stronger reported version allows any fixed source state whose support is spanned by product vectors. All claims remain source-derived and unreviewed.

PROOF SPINE AND SUPPORTING RESULTS
For the positive direction, subtract a sufficiently small separable component from σ, flag the residual state in an active catalyst sector, and use shared randomness to either keep that residual in the catalyst or swap it into the output. The successful joint state has exactly the required two marginals. The construction does not clone the input resource.

For the converse, a product-free target support U admits a strictly positive product informationally complete measurement with a uniform one-copy relative-entropy separation κ_U>0. Data processing then gives E_R(ρ_n)≥nκ_U for every, possibly correlated, output supported on U^{⊗n}. Repeated success preserves this support while every successful branch has Schmidt number at most the finite initial catalyst's Schmidt number r, hence E_R(ρ_n)≤log r. These inequalities contradict each other for sufficiently large n, independent of how small p is. The report extends the iteration argument to product-spanned source supports.

NONCOMPOSABILITY AND ERROR BOUNDARY
The state-level marginal-return relation is not transitive: a flagged Bell/vacuum state is reachable from a free input with correlated marginal-return catalyst, and its active sector yields a Bell state, although the Bell state itself fails the support criterion. Physical postselection consumes the catalyst, despite the state-level marginals.

The report's finite capped reservoir keeps success probability q fixed and bounds output error and unconditioned output–catalyst trace distance by q^K. The stored resource and catalyst dimension grow with K; the catalyst already contains copies of the target. Thus this is not free generation and it does not give return guarantees after every later postselection. The source reports that requiring the catalyst marginal to remain τ after every nonzero product-effect outcome is equivalent to Ω=σ⊗τ; with finite catalysts this stronger product-return condition cannot generate an entangled state from a separable input.

SCOPED CONNECTIONS — CONTEXT ONLY
- N680, rank-drop catalytic tensor restriction: exact tensor restrictions use a different input and an exact uncorrelated product-return contract. N691 is finite-dimensional state preparation from separable inputs with only success-conditioned marginal return, allowing output–catalyst correlations. No implication or contradiction is asserted. The N680 card currently resides on open PR #42.
- N683, protocol-preserving catalyst removal: channel-level protocol replacement and sequential resource-cost conditions differ from N691's state-level success branch. Context only; no proof dependency. The N683 card currently resides on open PR #44.
- N685, early-flag causalization obstruction: a channel/protocol timing and resource-preservation question; related postselection concerns do not make it the same theorem. Context only. The N685 card currently resides on open PR #46.
- N686, complementary Schmidt spectra: exact channel superactivation with infinite-dimensional pure reservoirs differs from N691's finite-dimensional state-preparation criterion. The finite Schmidt-number converse in N691 does not apply to that infinite-support setting. Context only; no contradiction. The N686 card currently resides on open PR #47.

EVIDENCE AND LIMITS
The complete supplied response, including its proof narrative, is preserved at updates/DK/package/finite_support_marginal_return/Pasted text.txt (SHA-256 and exact byte count in SOURCE_MANIFEST.json). It reports exact rational checks of five flagged protocols and 24 capped-reservoir instances. The referenced verify.py and verification_results.json were not supplied as standalone files and were not recreated or run. The exact initiating prompt and runtime were not supplied. The attachment is 527 newline-delimited lines and 21,701 bytes; the accompanying intake description says 1,842 lines, so the manifest records that discrepancy without modifying the source.

The report identifies separable-approximation geometry, Schmidt number, and restricted-measurement relative entropy as established ingredients and cites broader quantum-catalysis literature. These are source-reported antecedents; intake did not perform a literature audit. Independent correctness, formal verification, and historical priority remain unresolved.

body:
N692-polynomial-bit-constructive-matroid-rounding | Polynomial-bit constructive rounding candidate for matroid bases

STATUS AND SCOPE
`source_derived_unreviewed`. The supplied continuation contains a detailed proof narrative, but the linked standalone proof, ZIP, diagnostic program, and receipts were not supplied or located. This intake did not reconstruct the proof, implement the full algorithm, replay its diagnostics, or audit priority. Correctness and historical novelty remain UNKNOWN.

INPUT CONTRACT
Let M be an arbitrary matroid on n elements, accessed through an independence oracle. Let A∈Q^{m×n} have squared Euclidean column norms at most one, x∈P(M) be rational, and c∈Q^n be any rational cost vector. The response claims a deterministic algorithm returning a basis B such that

    cᵀ1_B ≤ cᵀx,                    ||A(1_B−x)||∞ ≤ C,

with C=262336. It claims polynomially many independence-oracle queries and ordinary bit operations in n, m, and the total binary input length; the output basis and all intermediate rational data have polynomial encoding length.

EXACT-MARGINAL CONSTRUCTION
For fixed A,x, the objective-aware basis procedure is used as a separation response in an ellipsoid metarounding argument. The response claims a deterministic polynomial-time construction of rational probabilities λₗ and at most n+1 bases Bₗ satisfying

    Σₗ λₗ=1,   Σₗ λₗ1_{Bₗ}=x,   ||A(1_{Bₗ}−x)||∞≤C for every support point.

The cost guarantee belongs to the one-objective basis procedure; the report does not claim every atom of the unbiased distribution is cost-nonincreasing. The probability law is constructed deterministically. Exact sampling by rational-probability rejection is claimed to take polynomial expected time; no uniformly bounded fair-random-bit sampler is claimed.

REPORTED CONSTRUCTION
The proposed algorithm combines inherited spectral-barrier/face-descent machinery with two computational controls:

- **Face-preserving precision reset.** After an exact local move reaches a matroid face, a rational linear program finds a nearby rational point inside that face, a dyadic box, and the retained exact input-defined affine equations. Determinant bounds reset coordinate bit length independently of the previous denominator. Moving spectral constraints are allowed a bounded numerical-error budget rather than being preserved exactly.
- **Quantitative negative-curvature progress.** The proof claims a feasible rational direction with inverse-polynomial negative curvature while retaining objective and protected-row equations. A full step decreases the potential by a fixed amount; a short step reaches a proper matroid face. At most n short face losses occur. Rational approximation is used for spectral derivatives; exact transcendental operations are not assumed.
- **Independence-oracle interface.** Matroid separation is reduced to submodular minimization of r(S)−y(S), with rank evaluations from independence queries. The report also describes recovery of the minimal face, exact line endpoints, and the linear precision-reset problems through this separator.

The source gives conservative fixed parameters (including K=64) and a reported local-update count O(n⁹(m+n)¹²). It states that the full algorithm has not been implemented end to end and is far from practical. Its broader transfer principle is limited to Boolean-vertex polytopes with bounded exchange width, polynomial separation, and controlled rational description; it is not a theorem for arbitrary polytope intersections.

CONSEQUENCES AND LIMITS
For a Boolean matrix W with at most Δ nonzeros in each column, scaling by q=⌈√Δ⌉ gives the source-claimed discrepancy bound C⌈√Δ⌉ for arbitrary matroid bases, with the stated one-objective or exact-marginal interface. The long-edge obstruction remains for arbitrary intersections of two matroids; no general intersection algorithm is claimed. A fixed finite-step lower bound is not assumed, and independent dyadic coordinate rounding is explicitly rejected as an exact feasibility repair.

The response reports exact checks of dimension/progress inequalities, one precision-reset example, and 80 face-recovery and terminal-cost cases over five small matroid families. These diagnostics are source-reported only: their code and receipts were unavailable and were not rerun.

RELATION TO EXISTING CAPITAL
- **N689**, bounded exchange width: scoped constructive continuation. N689 claims a broader Boolean-polytope existence classification with upper bound 4096k³+48k; its matroid-base specialization is an existence claim. N692 reports an algorithmic candidate for matroid bases specifically, with a larger constant and polynomial-bit claim. N692 does not validate N689 or extend the algorithm to all bounded-exchange Boolean polytopes.
- **N24**, executable cube and partition-base rounding: related algorithmic interface only. N24's acquired inputs, algorithms, guarantees, and K4 feasibility gate remain its own record; N692's source-reported general-matroid construction is not independent validation or an automatic replacement.
- **Guo–Fang–Lu**, [arXiv:2609.23540v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.23540v1): source report attributes the spectral-signing engine to this work, whose stated model is exact real arithmetic. The claimed additional contribution is a rational polynomial-bit transfer to general matroid bases and an explicit exact-marginal law; priority is UNKNOWN.
- **Bérczi–Liu–Reis–Tarnawski**, [arXiv:2608.13983v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.13983v1): source-reported comparator for matroid-constrained discrepancy. The report describes its guarantee as constructive and linear in column sparsity, and contrasts the proposed square-root dependence; exact comparison and novelty were not independently reviewed. The very large constant and polynomial degree make no practical dominance claim.

PROVENANCE AND OPEN OBLIGATIONS
The original submission is preserved byte-for-byte at `updates/DQ/package/constructive_matroid_rounding/ORIGINAL_PASTED_SOURCE.txt` (SHA-256 and source limits: `updates/DQ/package/SOURCE_MANIFEST.json`). The response links a separate `proof.md` and `ASTRA_Constructive_Matroid_Rounding.zip`, but those artifacts were not attached or located. The exact initiating research prompt and elapsed runtime were not supplied. Full algorithm implementation, independent proof reconstruction (especially face recovery, curvature margins, rational bit bounds, and ellipsoid separation), exact-version prior-art review, practical resource comparison, external correctness, and historical priority remain unresolved. No 9–10/10 breakthrough is claimed.

For fixed A,x, an ellipsoid metarounding step is claimed to construct at most n+1 bases with rational probabilities, exact mean x, and the same discrepancy bound at every support point. The algorithmic claim is specific to matroid bases; it does not promote the broader N689 Boolean-polytope existence classification to an algorithm.

For an explicitly represented graph G=(V,E), |V|=2n, with nonnegative rational edge weights, let G_S retain exactly the edges crossing S and V\S, and let Z_S be its weighted perfect-matching partition function. The report derives the exact positive identity sum_{S subset V} Z_S = 2^n Z_G. The joint law Pi(M,S)=w(M)/(2^n Z_G) 1{M subset E(G_S)} has matching marginal w(M)/Z_G. Its exact conditionals are: choose one endpoint of each matching edge for S given M, and use the weighted perfect-matching law on G_S for M given S. Existing bipartite machinery gives polynomial-time approximate implementations of the latter conditional; the report’s exact ideal-chain spectral-gap calculation is separate from those approximation costs. This is an exact representation, not an efficient general-graph counting algorithm.

The source further derives E[Y^2]/Z_G^2 = E_{M,N~pi_G} 2^{c(M,N)}, Cov(X)=1/4(I-R), while every graph has a negative-semidefinite log-Hessian at the all-ones point; a six-cycle derivative supplies a counterexample to global log-concavity of the lift polynomial. The proposed alternating conditional chain has exact gap 2^(1-n) on C_{2n}; a gadget family obstructs simple alternating-walk repairs while allowing an exact rational small-gadget elimination. The report also proves, under its stated input promise, that a polynomial-time sampler within TV 1/8 of uniform alternating simple cycles would imply NP=RP.

Scope boundary: these are obstructions to specified estimator/move primitives, not hardness of approximate perfect-matching counting. No general weighted perfect-matching FPRAS, polynomial-mixing sampler, or polynomial-cost general compressed elimination was obtained. N419 is linked as the existing downstream matching-reduction family; its theorem and open general-matching dependency remain unchanged and unvalidated by this report.

N694-codimension-threshold-global-spectral-regularity | A codimension threshold for recovering global spectral regularity
status=source_derived_unreviewed; the pasted report contains detailed proof arguments, preserved unchanged. The universal mathematical claims and cited imported results were not independently audited.

Let C_P(mu)=sup_f Var_mu(f)/int |grad f|^2 dmu. The report claims:

1. If n>=3 and a smooth positive rotationally invariant probability density on R^n has a codimension-two marginal that is kappa-strongly log-concave, then C_P(mu)<=n/((n-1)kappa). The full density need not be log-concave.
2. For every fixed n>=4 there are smooth positive isotropic rotationally invariant measures whose marginals of dimension at most n-3 are 1/500-strongly log-concave while C_P tends to infinity. They also obey E exp(<t,X>)<=exp(|t|^2/2) for all t.
3. For fixed n>=5, 0<eta<1/2 and K>0, there is a smooth positive isotropic rotationally invariant mu with D(mu||gamma_n)<=eta, every projection onto a subspace of dimension 1 through n-4 having curvature at least (1-eta)I, and C_P(mu)>=K. A witnessing bottleneck separates two sets each of probability at least 1/3.

The positive proof reconstructs the radial law from the codimension-two marginal by adding an independent Exp(1) energy: R_*=W^{-1}(W(S)+E). It then combines radial and angular control. The higher-codimension examples show that marginal curvature (even near-Gaussian marginal curvature plus small full KL divergence) need not control the global Poincare constant.

The transport corollary is scoped: separately contractive Gaussian transports of almost-full marginals do not yield a uniformly Lipschitz Gaussian representation of the full law. The source explicitly says this is not failure of distributional identification by all projections and not generic sampling hardness; its displayed construction admits Gaussian rejection sampling. Rotational symmetry is essential to the positive argument, and the non-radial extension remains open. Figalli–Jerison is credited for the simpler non-log-concavity observation; Caffarelli’s contraction theorem is imported. No foundational or historical-priority claim is certified.

N696-conditional-copy-polymatroid-conservativity | Closed conditional-copy-stable classes admit simultaneous marginal completion
status=source_derived_unreviewed; the complete pasted report contains a detailed proof narrative. This intake preserved the report but did not independently reconstruct it, verify cited prior art, or formally certify it. Historical priority and correctness remain UNKNOWN.

CENTRAL THEOREM
For each finite ground set E, let C_E be a closed class of polymatroids, stable under restriction/relabeling and under conditional copying with extensions remaining in the corresponding class. For every h∈C_E and protected family F, the report proves there is g∈C_E preserving every protected marginal, satisfying I_g(A;B|C)=0 for every partition separating F, and with g(E)≥h(E). The proof maximizes total rank on the compact fiber of protected marginals; any positive separating conditional-mutual-information defect can be removed by an internal copy while increasing total rank by exactly that defect.

COPY-HIERARCHY CONSEQUENCE
For K_E=∩_P Q_P(E), where P ranges over finite Shannon/conditional-copy programs, the report argues that K is itself closed and copy-stable. Thus MAXE and GMAXE completions remain inside K, and the closed consequence cones of finite copying and mixed copying/MAXE agree. This is a closure statement: it does not turn every boundary inequality into an exact finite-copy proof or characterize the almost-entropic cone.

FINITE CERTIFICATES AND LIMITS
For rational L valid on K and every rational ε>0, the report derives a finite-copy certificate for L(h)+εu(h)≥0. A one-step MAXE certificate with multipliers totaling Λ yields the explicit depth-T consequence L(f)+(Λ/T)(u(f)−f(E))≥0, using at most m∑_{t=0}^T q^t labels and an exponential-size Shannon rank system in the resulting label count. No polynomial-time entropy algorithm is claimed.

The attempted bound controlling the whole profile by copy defect is refuted by the report's entropy-level example. Lattice-quantized rank classes terminate exactly, but a uniform quantization/finite-termination principle for general real profiles remains open. The target equality K_E=closure(almost-entropic cone) is unresolved. The source's prior-art discussion credits existing MAXE/GMAXE questions and a same-field linear-polymatroid result; exact novelty is not established.

body:
N697-increasing-weight-union-closed-uniformization | Increasing-weight union-closed laws admit uniform lifts with the same abundance constant
status=source_derived_unreviewed; the complete pasted report contains detailed proof arguments and a randomized construction, but no separate executable package or receipts were supplied. This intake did not independently reconstruct the proofs, replay the construction, or verify prior art. Correctness and historical priority remain UNKNOWN.

UNIFORMIZATION
Let F be an explicitly finite union-closed family, |F|=m≥2, and p a strictly positive law on F satisfying p(A)≤p(B) whenever A⊆B. For k≥1 set b=ceil(log₂m), L_k=2kb+1. The report defines a product-likelihood superlevel family U_k={(A_1,…,A_k)∈F^k: ∏_j p(A_j)≥τ_k}. For a suitable threshold it is closed under coordinatewise union and invariant under block permutations. If Q_k is uniform on U_k, then Q_k(x)≤4L_k p^⊗k(x), and for 1≤ℓ≤k,

D((Q_k)_{1:ℓ}||p^⊗ℓ)≤(ℓ/k)log(4L_k),
TV((Q_k)_{1:ℓ},p^⊗ℓ)≤√(ℓ log(4L_k)/(2k)).

The report's randomized threshold selection and capped rejection replace 4L_k by 8L_k with controlled failure probability. For an explicitly listed F and rational p with B-bit probabilities, it reports polynomial bit work and O(kL_k log(L_k/δ)) draws from p for failure tolerance δ; U_k may be exponentially large and is not enumerated.

CONSEQUENCE AND NON-RESULTS
For every universal constant c, the uniform-family abundance statement is equivalent to the increasing-weighted version over nontrivial union-closed supports. This is a reduction/equivalence, not proof of Frankl's half-frequency conjecture or any improved constant. The exact criterion for when self-union coupling cannot raise entropy is already recorded in N504/LA224; it is not promoted again here.

The report's projected maximum-entropy repair fails submodularity on an explicit five-set family; this refutes that proposed assembly route only. It does not prove a general impossibility. Existing weighted formulations and specialized weighted results are credited in the source; priority for the arbitrary-weight uniformization theorem remains unknown.

RELATIONS
N503–N505 concern the same join-closure setting; N504 already stores the entropy-stagnation criterion. N563 contains separate unproved candidate inequalities for Frankl. This record neither uses those inequalities nor resolves them. These are scoped research links, not proof dependencies.

N698-finite-population-horizon-uniform-automaton-completion | Finite-population completion approximates automaton terminal laws uniformly in horizon
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The source account reports complete internal proof reconstructions and scoped exact-rational replays. This intake preserved the account/evidence and checked repository structure; it did not independently reconstruct the theorem or rerun research scripts. External correctness, formal verification, and historical priority remain UNKNOWN. No historic-scale breakthrough is claimed.
Symbols and contracts are local to this card.

INTERFACE
Let Q be a d-state set, A a finite alphabet, q0 an initial state, and f:Q×A→Q a supplied total deterministic transition table. The supplied input law μ on A is rational; zero-mass letters are deleted, r=|supp μ|, and α=min_{μ(a)>0} μ(a). At horizon n≥1, R_n is the set of terminal-state laws generated by arbitrary joint laws on X_1,…,X_n with every one-coordinate marginal X_t~μ. Arbitrary correlations, including dependence on the past state, are allowed. No independence, fixed stochastic kernel, blind-control, or exact accepting-support condition is assumed.

HORIZON-UNIFORM FINITE-POPULATION THEOREM (source-reported)
For integer P≥1, let H=binom(P+d−1,d−1), a_P=d/(2P), and b_P=d/(Pα+d). Vertices are state histograms x∈N^Q of total P. An allocation z∈N^{Q×A} gives an edge x→y when x_s=Σ_a z_{sa}, y_u=Σ_{s,a:f(s,a)=u}z_{sa}, and |Σ_s z_{sa}−Pμ(a)|≤d for each letter. Let G_{P,n} be the terminal histograms divided by P reachable in exactly n graph steps. Then, for every n,

    sup_{p∈R_n} dist_TV(p,G_{P,n}) ≤ d/(2P),
    sup_{g∈G_{P,n}} dist_TV(g,R_n) ≤ d/(Pα+d).

The same constants are independent of n. Also d_H(cl(⋃_{n≥1}R_n), ⋃_{1≤n≤H}R_n)≤a_P+b_P. The argument applies to every finite semigroup, including noncommutative ones, by adjoining a formal initial identity and using f(s,a)=sa; no mixing or semigroup-structure premise is needed.

PROOF MECHANISM
Scale any exact-marginal joint path law to an n-layer labelled flow of total P, add terminal-to-sink flow, and round the whole integral-balanced flow edgewise within its floor/ceiling intervals. The rounded complete paths have terminal TV error at most d/(2P); the error does not accumulate over time. Conversely, any relaxed population path has per-position letter frequencies μ'_t. A filler law with marginals q_t=[μ−(1−b_P)μ'_t]/b_P is nonnegative, and mixing this one global filler branch with the population path in weights 1−b_P,b_P restores every input marginal to μ exactly. The terminal error is at most b_P.

COMPUTATIONAL AND SAMPLING CONSEQUENCES
- For supplied rational target ν, exact rational graph distances give an interval for min_{p∈R_n} dist_TV(ν,p); P=ceil(2d/(αε)) gives a reported ε-accurate approximation. The arbitrary-positive-horizon optimum is a computable real, with the finite graph cutoff H.
- A fixed positive-gap promise (v_n≤a versus v_n≥a+γ) is in PSPACE for binary-supplied n and for arbitrary positive n. This is a membership result only: no PSPACE-hardness, exact cutpoint decision, or exact finite-horizon attainment algorithm is claimed.
- After graph acquisition, binary-horizon reachability/optimization uses O(H^3 log(n+1)) Boolean operations. The number of histogram vertices is H; candidate allocations number B_P=binom(P+dr−1,dr−1), with acquisition cost B_P·poly(d,r,b,log P) for rational input bit length b.
- A witness DAG gives a succinct exact-marginal joint law, exact terminal evaluation, and consistent adaptive coordinate queries in O(log(n+1)) lookups after compilation. Its reported atom bound is P+(r−1)E+1, E≤H². Printing all n letters still costs Ω(n); exact integer rejection sampling has expected finite random-bit cost but no bounded worst-case number of flips.
- For a stationary rational k-block law κ on A^k whose (k−1)-prefix and suffix marginals agree, an augmented-history construction preserves every overlapping k-window exactly and excludes zero-probability local patterns. Its filler uses F=dM² slots for denominator M, so costs can be exponential in the binary length of M. This extension has proof text but is not implemented by the one-coordinate diagnostic solver; it does not impose a conditional Markov kernel.
- For a fixed DFA, a uniformly positive-gap promise makes the yes-horizon language ultimately periodic. For a finite catalogue of control symbols, the corresponding uniformly gapped control-word language is regular. These are source-reported consequences under their stated promises; exact cutpoint predicates may remain nonperiodic.

REPORTED REPLAY
The preserved exact-rational receipt reports a 10^12-step noncommutative DFA example with 3 states, P=12, H=91, 6,188 allocation candidates, 111 witness-DAG nodes, 8 leaf allocations, 2 shared-quantile intervals, and at most 14 word atoms. It reports exact witness checks and graph-optimum recomputation. These are source-reported scoped diagnostics; this intake did not rerun them. The account also records a positive-gap example with a certified interval; see the exact certificate and replay receipt in the source package.

RESOURCE AND CLAIM LIMITS
The account charges explicit transition-table acquisition and graph construction. Complexity is not jointly polynomial in automaton dimension and log(1/ε); small rational α, large dimensions, accuracy, and block-statistic denominators can make compilation expensive. Random-access sampler tables are not claimed to fit in PSPACE. The theorem optimizes over unrestricted correlations with exact unconditional marginals; it does not solve general stochastic-MDP reachability, blind-control, fixed-kernel, or exact accepting-support problems. It does not settle the exact cutpoint/Skolem interface retained in related semigroup work.

RELATION TO N674
N674 classifies eventual exact product laws for finite commutative semigroups under its full-support assumptions. N698 supplies a broader DFA/finite-semigroup horizon-uniform approximation and acquired-input compiler, but only approximates terminal laws and does not decide exact attainment. These are complementary interfaces; no proof dependency, status transfer, or replacement is asserted.

For a strongly connected loopless digraph G with adjacency B, N>=2 and spectral radius r>0, replace each vertex by the transitive tournament T_m and each original arc by all cross-block arcs. The source derives rho(B tensor J_m + I_N tensor T_m)=1/((1+1/r)^(1/m)-1), preservation of directed girth and delta-plus(G[T_m])=m delta-plus(G). For D_m=C4[T_m], rho(D_5)>20/3 although girth=4, and rho(D_m)/(4m)->1/(4 log 2)>1/3. These graphs have minimum outdegree density 1/4: they refute the proposed spectral implication, not Caccetta–Häggkvist. The substitution construction is acknowledged prior mathematics; originality of the calculation is unestablished.

Define beta(M)=max_{w>=0,1^T w=1} min_i (Mw)_i=min_{p in Delta} max_j (M^T p)_j. For nonempty finite blocks H_i, the source proves beta(G[H_1,...,H_n])=beta(A_G+diag(beta(A_Hi))). Acyclic blocks have beta=0, so acyclic substitution preserves beta even for unequal block sizes; beta(D_m)=1/4. This distinguishes distinct-neighbour mass from walk growth and supplies no universal one-third bound.

On Z/10, include increments +1,+3 everywhere and +2 where i mod 5 is in {0,1,3}. The source gives girth four, det A=5, w=(3,1,2,2,1,3,1,2,2,1)/18 and p=(2,2,1,3,1,2,2,1,3,1)/18, with Aw=A^T p=(5/18)1. Positivity plus invertibility gives unique optimizers p!=w. This excludes identifying the two optimal measures; it does not exclude every weighted or stationary method.

The remaining assertion is beta(A+I/3)<=1/3 for every finite triangle-free oriented adjacency A, equivalently for every w in Delta some i obeys (Aw)_i<=(1-w_i)/3. The response derives equivalence to the directed-triangle Caccetta–Häggkvist target, using lexicographic powers of C4, continuity and rational independent-clone blowups. The assertion itself is unproved. Computing or naming beta has not removed the original obstruction.

Inputs/costs: explicit finite adjacency matrices, graph substitutions and simplex optimization; no efficient universal triangle certificate or new complexity bound is established. N618 is a separately sourced earlier failure of a stationary-neighbourhood inequality, mentioned only as background; neither its script nor OpenAI/math formalizations were replayed here. The intermediate progress line about cubic Gibbs observables is retained as transcript data and is not promoted to a separate result. The source explicitly reports that its major foundational completion standard was not met.

Let H=(V,E) be a finite simple graph with n vertices and m>=1 edges, p>1 and B>1. Kernels W:[0,1]^2->[0,infinity) are nonnegative, symmetric, have row integral exactly one almost everywhere and ||W||_p<=B. The observable is t(H,W)=integral product_{uv in E} W(x_u,x_v); discrepancy is the usual cut norm, not merely pairwise pointwise or operator approximation.

Define gamma_H(p) by minimizing d(V) over nonnegative edge scales k_e with sum k_e=1 and increasing supermodular set functions d with d(empty)=0, d(uv)>=p k_uv, d(uv)-d(u)>=k_uv and d(uv)-d(v)>=k_uv. The proposed sharp criterion is gamma_H(p)>1: all counts are finite and |t(H,U)-t(H,W)|<=C ||U-W||_square^((gamma-1)/(m-1+gamma-1)) for cut-norm differences <=1. If gamma<=1, the response constructs bounded finite-step normalized symmetric kernels W_L with ||W_L-1||_1->0 but liminf t(H,W_L)>1 for each B>1. For a bounded connected C^{1,beta} filled conductor in R^3 (0<beta<1), let alpha be its free-space static SI polarizability, alpha=epsilon0 M, and fill only electrically shielded closed cavities. The source imports the PEC endpoint Hashin–Shtrikman inverse-trace inequality V Tr(M^(-1))<=1, citing Colbrook–Sadeghi arXiv:2608.20466v1 Theorem 4.2. Cauchy–Schwarz then gives Tr(alpha)>=9 epsilon0 V. With one known homogeneous material, m=rho(1-phi)V and R=Tr(alpha)/m, it derives R>=9 epsilon0/[rho(1-phi)]. An actually covered upper measurement bound R_U yields phi<=1-9 epsilon0/(rho R_U), independent of exterior shape within the admitted class. Large response returns UNKNOWN, not a porosity diagnosis. This is neither an open-pore bound nor a printed-part-integrity guarantee.

For per-particle density rho<=rho_max, nonmetal mass fraction <=eta_max and physical trace >=(1-epsilon_alpha) times the PEC trace, the reported robust constant is K=9 epsilon0(1-eta_max)(1-epsilon_alpha)/rho_max and phi<=1-K/R_U. Bulk assays do not supply those per-particle promises. A denser hollow shell or suppressed coating response can hide the mass deficit. A negative inferred upper void bound indicates inconsistent premises/measurement, not automatic acceptance. Useful dense-powder acceptance yield is separately unknown.

At a fixed conductor configuration, net charge and environment in exactly affine imposed free-space fields e+Gx (G symmetric trace-free), the reported finite-body identity F=qe+Gp and linear p imply (1/4)sum_{s,t=+/-1} st F(se,tG)=G alpha e. Three explicit harmonic geometries recover the scalar x trace coefficient E0 g Tr(alpha)/3. Signed data weights are essential: equal four-sign exposure cancels the desired mean force and requires resolved metrology plus separate sorting. It does not inherit the unipolar 103 micrometre kick as an achieved measurement signal. Moving/rotating particles, electrode images, nonlinear fields and finite-frequency coating response are outside that ideal proof.

The exact scoped obstruction uses spherical conducting shells with off-center closed cavities, centered on known mass centers. Their electrical centers d vary with the cavity, while exterior alpha=a I. Force contains a G^2 d. Universal positive-weight cancellation of its x component requires sum_k w_k ||G_k e_x||^2=0; every useful x cross-force therefore vanishes. This blocks the specified universal positive-exposure affine-field architecture, including naive isotropic-gradient averaging. It does not exclude signed sensing, separately acquired electrical centers, bounded residuals, restricted shapes or other forces.

Assumed scales: a solid 30 micrometre Al sphere at rho=2700 kg/m^3 has mass 3.817e-11 kg, so 1 kg/h requires 7.277e6 particles/s. For assumed E0=1e6 V/m and g=1e9 V/m^2 the unipolar illustration gives acceleration 9.84 m/s^2 and 103 micrometre displacement after a 1 ms kick/10 ms drift. These are conditional calculator outputs, not measurements or whole-device simulations. Three 0.2% material margins leave R_U/R_sphere<=1.00406 for a 1% void target. Dense prolate shapes can exceed this cutoff. The source's illustrative one-hour risk target and assumed Gaussian tails require roughly 7.17 standard deviations, with random response precision near 0.046% under those margins; no tail coverage is established. Nominal repeatability 0.2% is insufficient to certify bias or industrial reliability.

Failure to cover admitted hollow particles rejects the certificate-acquisition claim. Then test neighboring particles and separate rejection actuation; only later attempt a 500–1000 particle/s lane (1000/s is about 0.137 g/h), followed by a measured multi-lane tile. Equipment, cost, energy per accepted kilogram and industrial scaling remain unknown. No experiment was performed.

The source proposes a deterministic finite-bit compiler for the Euclidean subgradient flow u'+partial F(u) contains 0, u(0)=x0, where x0 is rational and feasible. For rational 0<epsilon<1 and an acquired positive rational R>=||x0-z_*|| for a minimizer, output is a rational polygonal trajectory ending at an exact minimizer s and constant thereafter, with sup_{t>=0}||v(t)-u(t)||<=epsilon R and ||s-u_infinity||<=epsilon R. Time/output size are claimed polynomial in explicit input bits and epsilon^-1 using an imported rational convex-QP algorithm, without active-regime enumeration, unique minimizer or supplied spectral gap. This is a source-reported theorem, not independently established correctness or a general physical simulator.

The source explicitly credits the BEN/Fenchel variational action and prior dissipation-based error analysis. A_F(v)=integral[F(v)+F*(-v')]+(||v(T)||^2-||x0||^2)/2 controls squared state error by 2A. Feasible latent endpoint lifts and dual variables satisfying Hw_i+g+A^T lambda_i=P^T(x_{i-1}-x_i)/h_i, lambda_i>=0, bound this action by an explicit rational convex quadratic objective J. Feasibility and objective value, not trust in optimality, provide the proposed verifier interface. For N intervals the stated program has N(2D+m) variables, ND equalities and 2Nm inequalities; the initial lift, latent dimension and all inequalities are charged input.

With initial lift energy upper bound E0>0 and a=R^2/(2E0), h_i=min{eta(a+t_{i-1}),T-t_{i-1}}, the proximal witness and energy-distance inequality give J<=eta R^2/2. The reported N=ceil(log(1+2TE0/R^2)/log(1+eta)) is logarithmic in numerical T and O(epsilon^-2) at the chosen relative state accuracy. This does not give logarithmic precision cost: absolute error a_abs charges R/a_abs. Mesh rational numerators/denominators, QP bit sizes and optimizer operations all count.

For n two-level emitters, Q=sum_i q_i and supplied classical finite-precision C in C^(r x n), collective photon jumps are L_mu=sum_i c_mu,i sigma_i^-. The model includes a supplied commuting diagonal H0=sum_i d_i q_i+sum_ij u_ij q_i q_j, exchange Hamiltonian, coherent drives Omega_i, local pumps sqrt(p_i)sigma_i^+ and dephasing sqrt(kappa_i)Z_i. Inhomogeneous coefficients and arbitrary connectivity are allowed and charged; no permutation symmetry is assumed. Input support is Q<=k0; k0=n allows an unrestricted unknown state entangled with a reference. Output is the full Markovian channel to diamond error epsilon and specified observables, not a laboratory-validated microscopic model.

Writing omega=sum|Omega_i|, p*=sum p_i and kappa*=sum kappa_i, the source derives E exp(theta J_T)<=exp[theta k0+T(2sinh(theta/2)omega+(exp(theta)-1)kappa*+(exp(2theta)-1)p*)] for theta>0. J counts all photon, pump and the specified Z-dephasing events. A tilted positive state weighted by exp(theta Q) cancels collective lowering in its generator; it is a proof device, not an assumed quantum oracle. With baromega=sum(|Re Omega_i|+|Im Omega_i|), R=ceil(k0+2T baromega+2T kappa*+7T p*+log(32/epsilon)) bounds overflow probability by epsilon/32 uniformly. An absorbing flag retains all probability; the channel penalty is at most twice overflow probability. No survival renormalization or rare-event postselection is used. The budget is representation-specific, not invariant under arbitrary Lindblad gauge changes.

The explicit factor A=sum_i |i> tensor sigma_i^- has A^dagger A=Q. A/sqrt(n) is constructed by reversible Hamming-weight arithmetic, an occupied-index selection and cleanup with O(n poly(b)) gates, including the vacuum failure branch and a globally normalized unitary. Coefficient row-state preparation implements C/||C||_F in O(rn poly(b)) gates without QRAM; it does not receive a free data oracle. The emitter label must be erased coherently after combining C with A; retaining it destroys collective interference and dark states. Physical mode labels remain. The stacked normalization is g^2=n||C||_F^2+p*+kappa*. Frobenius rather than spectral normalization incurs up to sqrt(r) in this jump scale. H0 phases cost O((n+|E0|)poly(b)); the remaining Pauli LCU has h=sum_exchange(|Re J_ij|+|Im J_ij|)+baromega. The same commuting interaction-picture improvement is granted to the comparison algorithm.

This proposed consequence depends explicitly on the unreviewed N701 loss-complete first-event implementation, not merely its conservation identity. Using a power-of-two W between R+1 and 2(R+1), windows T/W, coherent suffix selectors and padded identity calls, at most W+R first-event operations implement a fixed isometry with an inverse. The claimed query count is O-tilde(R+1+g sqrt(T(R+1))+hT). Binary grid indices and arithmetic charge log(M), not an uncharged explicit list of M time slices. With lambda0=sum|d_i|+sum|u_ij|, a=g^2/2+h and D=a^2+2lambda0(g^2+h), the source supplies a Lipschitz/discretization and hybrid-error budget; exact constants and the inherited compiler remain review obligations. Quantum workspace is O(n+(R+1)poly(b)) when all event records are kept coherently.

D_in=rn+n+|E0|+|Eex| gives G_sim=O(D_in poly(b)[R+1+g sqrt(T(R+1))+hT]); reading B0-bit coefficients costs Omega(D_in B0), and preprocessing O(D_in poly(b)). Coherent preparation and inverse cost C_in and a bounded effect 0<=F<=I costs C_F. Estimating that effect to additive delta with failure zeta claims O-tilde(P_pre+(G_sim+C_in+C_F)delta^-1 log(1/zeta)), with simulation error O(delta). Copies-only access instead costs delta^-2 shots. Photon mode/time-bin counters and rB log(R+1) storage are charged separately. Simultaneous pair-Pauli estimates use O(delta^-2 log(n/zeta)) shots and O(n^2) classical processing per shot, storage and output; no claim writes an n^2 correlation map for free.

For fixed r, bounded-degree diagonal/exchange graphs, per-emitter collective couplings of order gamma, pump/drive/dephasing rates O(gamma), and T=Theta(1/gamma), the source obtains ||C||_F^2=Theta(gamma n), g^2=Theta(gamma n^2), hT=O(n), R=O(n+log(1/epsilon)). It proposes O-tilde(n^(5/2)) logical gates versus an instantiated general-algorithm upper bound O-tilde(n^3), using identical explicit oracles and interaction picture. One bounded observable adds delta^-1 with coherent access, delta^-2 with copies. This is an improved pair of upper bounds in a specified model; it proves no lower-bound separation or universal advantage over specialized classical/quantum algorithms. The Dicke collective rate Theta(gamma n^2) is real; for the early flash T=Theta(1/(gamma n)) the bounds can be comparable. No certified stationarity time follows.

For ||C-C'||_F<=e_C, ||H-H'||<=e_H and total pump/dephasing rate errors e_p,e_kappa, the source states diamond distance <=T(2e_H+4ns e_C+2n e_C^2+2e_p+2e_kappa), s=||C||_F. Acquiring/calibrating coefficients and validating the Markov approximation remain external tasks. Strong drive/pumping can eliminate the advantage; hT remains, symmetric/solvable subclasses may be easier, and retardation, non-Markovian dynamics and fault-tolerance overhead are outside the logical-gate result. An observable of norm S with absolute error delta_abs charges delta=delta_abs/S. Tiny probabilities and normalized rare outputs have no free relative accuracy. Reported small-system diagnostics do not establish independent correctness, priority, executed circuitry or technological readiness.

N705-bounded-coupling-local-thermal-faithfulness-and-finite-band | Bath-uniform local thermal faithfulness and finite-band bounds are proposed under bounded coupling
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported mathematical arguments only. For finite H_S tensor H_B, d=dim(H_S), H=I_S tensor K+V with Hermitian K,V and ||V||op<=v, all subsystem-only terms and subsystem-bath coupling belong in V. At beta>0 let rho=exp(-beta H)/Z and X=x tensor I_B for any possibly non-Hermitian x. No bath dimension, bath energy scale, geometry, gap, commutation or mixing restriction is assumed. The claimed local KMS bound is K_rho(X)=Tr(sqrt(rho)X^dagger sqrt(rho)X)>=4 exp(-4 beta v)||x||op^2/(9d)>=4 exp(-4 beta v)Tr_S(x^dagger x)/(9d^2). This is a quadratic form, not ordinary uncentered variance or a transport coefficient. When v=0 it is exactly Tr_S(x^dagger x)/d.

More generally, lambda>sqrt(3) gives (1-3/lambda^2)^2 exp[-(lambda+1)beta v]||x||op^2/d. The singular-profile extension for lambda>0 replaces the numerator by sum_a(s_a(x)-3||x||op/lambda^2)_+^2. For Hermitian A,B with ||A-B||<=v, low/high spectral projections separated by g obey ||QP0||<=v/g, using a Sylvester integral. If X commutes with P0, compression error is <=3||QP0||^2||X||. Applied to I tensor K versus H, each low bath level supplies a copy of x; retained singular values after widening by lambda v are thermally integrated and divided by the scalar min-max bound Z<=d exp(beta v)Z_B. No false operator-order monotonicity of exp or efficient spectral-projector access is assumed.

The finite-band form K_{rho,Omega}(X)=sum_{|E_i-E_j|<=Omega}sqrt(p_i p_j)|X_ij|^2 obeys K_{rho,7v}(X)>=exp(-5 beta v)||x||op^2/(72d). Width-v bath windows enlarged by 3v on each side and a bounded overlap count supply this absolute floor. It is not a constant fraction of all KMS weight, excludes no zero-frequency contribution, and gives no nonzero-frequency absorption, conductivity, rapid mixing or finite-resolution measurement algorithm.

For Hermitian A centered at its thermal mean, BKM covariance dominates KMS. Static susceptibility is at least (4beta/(9d))exp(-4beta v) Var_tauS(A). For traceless local basis F_a with tauS(F_a F_b)=delta_ab, fixed bath K and fixed coupling V0, and ||V0+sum h_a F_a tensor I||<=v throughout a convex parameter region, Hessian(log Z)>=beta^2 kappa I, kappa=4exp(-4beta v)/(9d). Thus ||h-h'||_2<=(9d/(4beta))exp(4beta v)||m(h)-m(h')||_2. This is conditional local-field identifiability with fixed environment, not identification of an unknown bath/coupling. The explicit commuting h Z_S+b Z_B+J Z_S Z_B example gives indistinguishable local Gibbs states for different h when bath/coupling vary.

With q bounded observables ||F_a||<=L, supplied independent exact equilibrium copies, and a fit with stated residual, the note gives the sufficient count q+81q^2 L^2 d^2 exp(8beta v)log(2q/alpha)/(2beta^2 epsilon^2) for parameter error epsilon. It does not efficiently compute the expectation map, log Z or the fit. Copy preparation costs multiply this count by the actual T_eq; independence, preparation bias, measurement implementation and optimization remain charged. The theorem supplies no Gibbs sampler or equilibrium-time bound.

The low-temperature qubit H=hZ has susceptibility beta sech^2(beta h)~4beta exp(-2beta v), so universal polynomial-beta-v conditioning is impossible; exponent constants are not claimed optimal. For even d>=4, an explicit bath of dimension d-1, M=4log d, r=2/(sqrt(M^2+4)+M), local traceless Hermitian x=diag(1,-1,r^2,-r^2,...) and norm-one disjoint two-by-two perturbations gives beta=v=1, thermal mean zero, K<=3/d and tauS(x^2)>=1/[2(4log d+1)^4]. Their ratio tends to zero. This excludes a dimension-free KMS-to-tracial comparison in this general class, not a fixed-locality bounded-degree global covariance theorem or a dimension-free impossibility for BKM itself.

For k-qubit support with incident interaction norm sum <=gk, d=2^k,v<=gk yields ||X||tau <=(3/2)2^(k/2)exp(2beta gk)||X||rho,KMS. The source compares this linear-beta exponent with Chen--Anshu--Nguyen arXiv:2504.02706v1 Lemma III.6 and Bergamaschi arXiv:2610.01074v1 Lemma 3.6, which have beta log(beta) behavior in the specified inequalities. This is not exhaustive novelty clearance or a complete learning-algorithm speedup. The desired global BKM covariance bound Cov(sum u_a P_a,sum u_a P_a)>=c(beta,J,k,Delta)sum u_a^2 independent of size/term count remains open. Applying a local bound to the whole support makes d exponential and v extensive; positive termwise variances do not control off-diagonal cancellation. Learning-SYK arXiv:2610.02178v1 retains an explicit term-count denominator in the cited comparison.

The downloaded original LaTeX, PDF, check script, recorded numerical output and producer manifest are preserved alongside the exact pasted report, whose duplicated mathematical rendering is not silently repaired. Finite checks and archive/hash agreement establish no independent proof correctness, historical priority, global theorem, novel physical law or technology readiness. The stronger operation required is global quantum tensorization/anti-cancellation with a feasible acquisition and learning interface. Intermediate bosonic/irreversibility remarks stay transcript history rather than separate promoted claims.
