SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
There are m bosonic modes, m a positive integer, and theta,kappa,nu > 0. The supplied conservative evolution has isotropic constant bath rates b = kappa nu/theta and d = b+kappa, with a well-defined time-dependent Hamiltonian satisfying [H_t,K]=0 for total photon number K = sum_j a_j^dagger a_j. The observer pools every monitored loss output and receives every aggregate count time, without a port label. The count map is J_t(rho) = theta c_t sum_j a_j rho a_j^dagger, where c_t is known and predictable from the common aggregate record and shared independent randomness, 0 <= c_t <= c_max, and theta c_t <= d. Monitoring only one mixed output is a different instrument. The initial supplied state is the product thermal state with mean nu/theta photons per mode; the result also holds for any initial density with the same distribution of K.

EXACT CLAIM
For a scalar f(K), the adjoint generator closes as
  L* f(K) = b(K+m)[f(K+1)-f(K)] + dK[f(K-1)-f(K)],
and the detected-count adjoint is J_t* f(K) = theta c_t K f(K-1). The Hamiltonian term vanishes because it commutes with K. With the Poisson kernel K|S=s ~ Poisson(s/theta), the kernel PGF P_s(z)=exp[(s/theta)(z-1)] intertwines both the number generator and the detected-count map with the CIR generator dS=kappa(m nu-S)dt+sqrt(2 kappa nu S)dW and Cox count likelihood c_t s. The jump identity includes the detected photon subtraction, not only unconditional moments.

Therefore the complete quantum aggregate count record through T together with terminal K has exactly the law of the CIR Cox count record through T and a terminal Poisson(S_T/theta) draw. The equality holds branch by branch under shared record-dependent controls and common classical randomness, while H_t remains number-preserving. The gamma-root coordinates give the conditional physical PGF directly: w(z)=beta theta/(beta theta+1-z), F_K(z|record)=w(z)^m P_J(w(z)). A proved joint TV error epsilon for (record,S_T) transfers to (record,K) with the same epsilon and no quartic bridge allowance.

BOUNDARIES
Strong number-preserving hopping and interactions can change internal states but cannot steer the distribution of total K in this quotient; c_t changes readout efficiency. This is an exact predictive result for pooled aggregate counts and terminal total number, not general nonlinear quantum control. It does not represent the full conditional quantum state, port labels, interferometric observables, individual-mode numbers under general hopping, or the unobserved photon-number path. Coarse first-port latch bins do not reveal the fine aggregate event times required by the root filter. Physical parameters and control calibration are supplied, not learned. The Poisson sampling implementation needs its own finite-arithmetic and sampling error accounting.

The exact terminal Poisson kernel adds no quartic bridge allowance; finite arithmetic and sampling error are still charged. The bath, detector calibration and preparation are supplied, not acquired measurements or a learned model.

body:
N988-xh1-product-negative-library-proposal | Chemical-state-negative filtering proposes a product-qualified ribosomal display library

STATUS | mechanism proposal from the selected XH1 source; chemical capture/display compatibility and the integrated library remain unacquired. Source-preservation and arithmetic checks do not establish a working assembler, chemical performance, novelty, or advantage.

EXACT CLAIM
The source proposes encoding distinct nonstandard peptide products on separate mRNA templates, using established ribosomal elongation and mRNA-display linkage, then applying a downstream chemical-state-negative filter to a completed genotype-linked library. In its example, an uncyclized hydrazinoester product retains an exposed hydrazinyl nitrogen that can react with aldehyde, while the desired cyclic product has consumed that nitrogen. Marking/removing the linear products could qualify library members before functional selection. The source proposes adapting known hydrazone chemistry to intact mRNA fusions; selective capture in an RNA-compatible environment, fusion survival, side-reaction rates, and false tagging have not been demonstrated. The immobilized aldehyde scavenger is speculative.

SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
Proposed completed genotype-linked library, credited ribosomal cyclic-backbone synthesis and puromycin display; selective removal must distinguish the exact linear/cyclic products while preserving their attached nucleic acid. This combined selective capture/display interface remains unacquired.

DECODING AND REUSE CONDITIONS
Two different chemical instructions in one common pool need distinguishable codon/charged-tRNA decoding registers. Mixing distinct monomers on the same tRNA species or codon is not individually addressable merely because there are two mRNA programs. Lee's established AUG/GAC/CGU assignments demonstrate prescribed placement, not arbitrary late per-chain rewriting. The puromycin-linked mRNA/product fusion is a consumed library object; translation catalysts can be reused, but the fusion is not a reusable assembly catalyst.

BOUNDARIES
The proposed purge happens after synthesis of the full product. It does not make each ribosomal elongation step wait for a product-state certificate, guarantee chemical identity, or correct ring closure on the ribosome. The donor-empty aliasing failure is recorded separately in N989. Correct transfer onto the next tRNA distinguishes transfer from hydrolysis for the stated two-state comparison; it still does not certify the later intramolecular ring-closing reaction. Chemical-state-negative library selection is therefore a distinct mechanism from product-gated progression at every assembly step.

SUBSTRATE-SPECIFIC PURITY ARITHMETIC
The cited approximately 22% cyclic / 78% linear result is for one tested six-membered-ring substrate, not the different Lee et al. Figure 8 double-ring experiment. If p=0.22 and a later filter retains fractions t and w of correct and incorrect products, respectively, then q=pt/[pt+(1-p)w]. Reaching q>=0.99 requires w/t<=0.002849, or at least 351-fold relative discrimination. If t=0.9, at least 99.744% of incorrect molecules must be removed. The source's multi-motif p^2 calculation assumes independence that was not measured; do not apply the 22% example to the double-ring substrate. The companion Python performs Bayesian and sampling arithmetic only; it was not executed during this intake.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
Credit the existing ribosomal cyclic-backbone chemistry of Lee et al. (2025), established mRNA display linkage from Roberts and Szostak (1997), and the 2026 genetically reprogrammed cyclic glycopeptide mRNA-display result of Johansen-Leete et al. These sources already demonstrate substantial chemistry and genotype-linked selection; this intake did not independently audit their literature. Lee's example is substrate-dependent, and other substrates reportedly cyclize much more efficiently, so those are stronger comparators before adding a filter. Specialized monomers, charged tRNA, flexizyme, GTP-driven translation, puromycin linkage, chemistry-compatible purification, and product recovery remain costs. No integrated synthesis/display/filter machine, measured RNA-compatible capture, or practical advantage is established.

NEXT OBLIGATION
Test whether selective aldehyde marking/removal works on the exact uncyclized and cyclized products while intact puromycin-linked mRNA survives; control false tagging at other nucleophiles and identify truncations by product mass. Then test two separately encoded products in one common translation pool with correct mRNA/product identity and quantify the retained library. The source's stated comparison is high-diversity discovery against matched automated synthesis and current mRNA-display/ribosomal methods; no such matched experiment has been run.

body:
N989-xh1-empty-carrier-false-completion | An empty-carrier signal aliases productive transfer and hydrolysis in the stated assembly states

STATUS | accepted internally for the exact stated pair of reaction-state descriptions, at the version bound by knowledge/reviews/A989-p1-xh1-selected-scope.json. This does not assert how often hydrolysis occurs in an apparatus.

EXACT CLAIM
For upstream 3'-O-acylated DNA donor U-O-CO-P_n, the listed productive transfer to a downstream aminated adaptor and hydrolysis of the acyl linkage both leave the upstream carrier in state U-OH. A downstream polymerase that senses only U-OH cannot distinguish the two outcomes. Thus donor-empty is not, by itself, a completion certificate. The failure is observational: an adequate next-address rule must also read a product-qualified receiving state, or the hydrolysis leakage must be separately bounded for the intended use.

SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
Only the empty upstream donor is observed under the two supplied reaction-state alternatives; no receiving-adaptor occupancy or free-product observation is supplied.

RIBOSOME CONTRAST
For the source's ribosomal two-state comparison, peptidyl transfer leaves tRNA_P empty and places the chain on A-site tRNA_A, whereas donor hydrolysis leaves tRNA_P empty, releases free chain, and leaves tRNA_A unchanged. Checking the next carrier's product occupancy distinguishes these two listed outcomes. This does not imply the ribosome independently senses perfect chemical identity or that correct transfer certifies the later cyclization step.

N993-dots-binary-balanced-entropy-transfer | Balanced entropy forms of two fixed positive operators admit an exact scalar testing-measure transfer
status=accepted_internally_verified; the completed scoped source audit is preserved in A993, and A1012 binds this corrected current card version. Mathematical scope, remaining gaps and physical acquisition stay separate.

EXACT CLAIM
For faithful positive A,X on the same finite-dimensional space, with no commutation assumption, the positive measure mu=h'' of h(t)=Tr(A-tX)_+ represents the positive and negative traces of every real pencil alpha A+beta X by the scalar densities alpha r+beta against mu. Consequently, for nonnegative mixture coefficients alpha_j,beta_j and real c_j satisfying both sum_j c_j alpha_j=0 and sum_j c_j beta_j=0, the balanced entropy combination of the mixtures equals its scalar integral against mu. Every scalar inequality of this balanced form, with optional linear trace terms, holds for all such operator pairs iff it holds for all nonnegative scalar pairs. Singular finite matrices follow by the stated epsilon-identity regularization and entropy continuity.

SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
Two fixed positive operators on the same finite-dimensional space; nonnegative mixtures; both coefficient-balance equations; singular inputs only by the stated continuity extension.

BOUNDARIES
Does not cover three or more independent sources, arbitrary products or log-Euclidean means, partial transposes, general matrix-valued functional calculus inequalities, or unbalanced entropy combinations. The testing measure is abstract and does not represent one physical measurement.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
An exact finite-dimensional identity in nats with natural logarithms. Matrix dimension and numerical precision are not assigned an algorithmic or experimental cost by the source.

NEXT OBLIGATION
Any use with three or more sources needs a separate proof; the retained trine obstruction rules out a blanket three-source scalar-to-matrix lift. General WH3 remains open.

N994-dots-fixed-prior-binary-sdpi | A binary-input channel has the same fixed-prior Umegaki SDPI constant with any finite quantum reference
status=accepted_internally_verified; the completed scoped source audit is preserved in A993, and A1012 binds this corrected current card version. Mathematical scope, remaining gaps and physical acquisition stay separate.

EXACT CLAIM
For every finite-output classical channel T with binary input and every full-support fixed prior pi, let K=A_0+A_1, Y_y=T_{y0}A_0+T_{y1}A_1, and q_y=(T pi)_y. For arbitrary positive A_0,A_1 on any common finite-dimensional quantum reference, sum_{y:q_y>0} D(Y_y || q_y K) <= eta(T,pi) sum_{i=0}^1 D(A_i || pi_i K), where eta(T,pi) is the scalar fixed-prior Umegaki SDPI constant. Scalar references give the matching lower bound, so allowing an arbitrary finite quantum reference does not change this fixed-prior constant.

SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
Finite-output stochastic channel with input alphabet {0,1}; full-support fixed prior pi; arbitrary finite-dimensional positive operator weights A_0,A_1; omit zero output-prior symbols.

BOUNDARIES
This fixes the binary transmitted alphabet and the prior. It is not the global-prior binary coefficient in N970, not an arbitrary-alphabet theorem with arbitrary references, not a reduction of multi-symbol quantum-memory problems, and not a t log t matrix-SDPI separation.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
An exact finite-dimensional inequality for Umegaki relative entropy; no acquired channel experiment, measurement protocol, complexity bound, or resource estimate is supplied.

NEXT OBLIGATION
Historical priority of this direct consequence remains UNKNOWN. General multi-symbol fixed-prior reference equality remains outside this result.

body:
N995-dots-three-source-trine-obstruction | A qubit trine obstructs a universal three-source balanced entropy transfer
status=accepted_internally_verified; the completed scoped source audit is preserved in A993, and A1012 binds this corrected current card version. Mathematical scope, remaining gaps and physical acquisition stay separate.

EXACT CLAIM
The scalar balanced third finite difference s(a+b+c)-s(a+b)-s(a+c)-s(b+c)+s(a)+s(b)+s(c), for s(t)=-t log t, is nonnegative for all a,b,c>=0. For the three real qubit trine projectors P_0,P_1,P_2, the corresponding balanced matrix trace-entropy expression is (3/2)log(3/4)<0, since the sum has spectrum (3/2,3/2), each pair has spectrum (3/2,1/2), and each individual projector has spectrum (1,0). The scalar-to-matrix transfer therefore fails in this explicit three-source case, and negativity persists under sufficiently small positive epsilon-identity perturbations.

SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
Three positive semidefinite operators on C^2; entropy S(Y)=-Tr Y log Y with natural logarithms; compare the same balanced coefficients as the scalar third finite difference.

BOUNDARIES
This is an obstruction to one universal balanced three-source entropy lift. It is not a W3 counterexample, does not contradict the older arbitrary-classical-channel/qubit-reference global mutual-information theorem, and does not establish a t log t fixed-prior matrix-SDPI separation.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
Exact 2x2 spectral evaluation and a continuity argument for faithful perturbations; no channel construction, physical measurement, or computational advantage is asserted.

NEXT OBLIGATION
A multi-source result needs additional hypotheses or a different mechanism. The general coherent WH3 target and a compatible fixed-prior SDPI separation remain open.

body:
N996-p3-acquired-operator-law-procedure | Acquiring operator laws with defects yields scoped corrected procedures
status=accepted_internally_verified; completed scoped acceptance is recorded in A997-p3-operator-law-procedure-source-review-v2, and A1017 binds this corrected current card version. Scientific limits and physical acquisition remain separate.

EXACT CLAIM
For a fixed finite-dimensional exact-rational linear interface exposing vector and transpose actions for A and B, a declared bounded word/rank/degree search can acquire a relation such as AB=q BA+cI+UV^T, then retain its defect factors and degree-filtered left/right modules. Fresh exact-vector checks give a randomized all-input identity certificate with a stated false-accept bound. Conditional on that accepted identity, the retained representation produces exact corrections for later bounded-degree word and polynomial programs and computes their validity domains without new native acquisition calls. A separate shared-probe route can instead acquire a small faithful operator algebra when closure fits its dimension budget. Unsupported or non-unique cases remain UNKNOWN; full rank in the tested quadratic library excludes only a nonzero rank-one law in that library.

METHOD
1. Query exact vector and transpose actions under the supplied fixed linear-map contract and declared word/rank budget.
2. Recover a scalar and low-rank residual candidate, or linearize the rank-one condition over the fixed library (I,A,B,A^2,AB,BA,B^2). A one-dimensional decomposable minor-kernel gives uniqueness only within that library; fresh native checks separately test existence.
3. Factor the residual R=UV^T and acquire degree-filtered left/right modules. Their row space gives the maximal common protected domain for bounded-degree uses of the ideal law.
4. Normalize later words to ideal normal forms plus retained defect corrections. New bounded-degree procedures can be synthesized with no further native acquisition calls; corrected execution remains all-input conditional on the accepted law. If a small closure is acquired instead, checked multiplication tables represent all finite polynomial programs in those same primitives.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
The n=64 degree-eight differentiation control acquired sigma=1, c=7/3 and rank-one defect in 68 primitive actions versus 128 for dense tomography; its common protected domain has dimension 57. The unlabelled q=2, degree-five example synthesized with zero new native calls and executed in four B actions versus twelve direct actions, after 96 acquisition actions versus 64 for tomography. Other source controls did not save total acquisition actions: kinetic 250 versus 192, Chebyshev 86 versus 80, and fermionic finite-algebra acquisition 96 versus 40. The vector width, returned field elements, arithmetic, bit growth, storage and primitive costs remain part of an application budget. These examples establish no universal cost win or superiority over an equally informed retaining method.

BOUNDARIES
Linearity, exact arithmetic, transpose access, bounded search grammar and source stability are supplied assumptions, not inferred physical properties. Noisy, nonlinear, drifting, or unacquired physical interfaces are outside scope. For the Chebyshev projection, P x^2 P differs from (P x P)^2; the learned procedure does not acquire a physical force law. A scalar-query lower bound does not transfer to the richer vector/transpose API. QuickSpec, MinRank, block Krylov, randomized range finding, displacement methods, and reusable-program systems are established comparators; no priority, general-intelligence, physical, or whole-project advantage is claimed.

NEXT OBLIGATION
The procedure is conditional on the supplied fixed exact-rational vector/transpose API and its bounded grammar and degree or closure budget. Rank-one exclusion is only within the tested quadratic word library; higher-degree or higher-rank cases and closure beyond budget remain UNKNOWN. The saved finite controls are source-reported; producer scripts/data were not replayed here. External/formal certification, physical measurement, a working device, priority, or practical advantage remain unestablished. The Chebyshev projection mismatch blocks interpreting that computational procedure as an acquired physical force law.

DISTINCTION
This record is distinct from N929's stationary-adjoint residual acquisition and N938's correlated reaction-entrance interface. It records an exact operator-law-plus-defect acquisition route for constructing later computational procedures. The separately supplied 24 October campaign closeout is already preserved in the run-closeout packet; this record does not revise its NOT_ACHIEVED or paused-goal status.

REVIEW SCOPE
Capital's receiving review checked the cited derivation, uniqueness conditions, domain argument, procedure identity, selected implementation paths and cost/boundary passages at the copied versions. Producer scripts were not executed here; their saved finite-control results are source-reported. No external specialist review, formal certification, physical measurement, practical advantage, or historical-priority determination is claimed.

N997-p3-retained-uncertainty-task-directed-experiments | Retained exact and uncertain operator histories compile task experiments and usable certificates
STATUS | accepted_internally_verified at the version-bound conditional mathematical scopes; software controls remain source-reported and physical/practical claims remain separate.

EXACT CLAIM
For a fixed exact-rational linear forward map H:Q^n->Q^m, certified independent relations CH=D and all retained forcing-response pairs determine precisely H=H0+NZT. Columns of N span ker C and ker T is the span of all queried inputs. A new linear response functional <W,H> is already determined iff N^T W T^T=0; otherwise exactly rank(N^T W T^T) additional full-vector forward experiments suffice and are necessary for deterministic exact worst-case answers over the unrestricted rational completion class. The generated inputs can have infinity norm at most one; all new responses are retained after evaluating the old factorization. The1143square-response software extension replaces exact-response semantics by the common feasible set K={H:||BH-I||_2<=rho, |HF-Y|<=delta}. Every explicit multiplier U yields a valid task interval by a nuclear-norm support bound plus the charged response boxes. Two explicit compatible operators can certify information insufficiency within this set. A checked software Jacobi contraction supplies a real precision/sweep menu; fixed-menu deterministic residual-ball minimax error pairs the smallest noise budgets with the largest task singular values.

INTERFACE AND ASSUMPTIONS
Fixed linear source, exact rational full-vector forward actions in known coordinates, certified relation rows and consistent complete retained observation history, and a newly supplied linear functional W. No native transpose is assumed. The uncertain interface requires fixed square linear H, justified individual response enclosures, a frozen invertible B and a valid simultaneous defect calibration. The demonstrated instrument checks supplied rational diagonally dominant source coefficients; it is scientific software, not physical calibration.

BOUNDARIES
The earlier exact rank-query lower bound is not for scalar observations, randomized bounded-error methods, noisy acquisition, coefficient-bit-size promises, supplied source formulas, transpose access or additional structural restrictions. An equally informed retaining algorithm uses the same laws/data and ties the query bound. Learned relations do not identify a unique microscopic mechanism. This does not supersede N996's different vector/transpose defect-calculus theorem. The exact theorem is retained separately; finite noisy data do not establish exact couplings. Norm-and-box ambiguity alternatives need not preserve a supplied path topology/nonnegative transport class. Residual-directed experimental design under the full historical set is heuristic, and a witness need not shrink that whole set enough. Missing result JSONs remain missing. At full input rank, ordinary retaining inversion yields a slightly tighter data-only interval and ties the final zero-query transfer without the random calibration event.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
Each query returns m scalars. Local relation discovery can cost a combinatorial support search. The reported two tasks use two queries each and leave 16 response parameters unresolved; input/output rationals reach 170/200 bits. Initialization costs 4,645 Fraction operations; generic task plans 14,913/18,147; a zero-query specialization reduces 16,129 to 76 operations. These are source-reported software controls, not total-runtime or architecture-superiority evidence. The source reports32calls/1024returned coordinates per source plus earlier support acquisition, failed repeated calls, rational proof work and retained histories. Its costed precision plan uses18 versus2520Jacobi sweeps and3616 versus474003Fraction calls; these are reported software costs, not hardware/time superiority. A dense growing history is retained; no fixed-width update theorem.

NEXT OBLIGATION
Acquire informative structure without reaching full input span on substantial new tasks, while retaining honest enclosures, ambiguity witnesses and equally informed source-code/tomography controls. The old exact-rational theorem remains valid; source changes/refits require fresh calibration. No general nonlinear mechanism discovery, physical calibration or exclusive program-search advantage is established.

notices.clarification: The continuation minimal-monomial conjecture S_p<=m Pr(F!=0), equivalently W<=m k for fair bits, is exactly refuted: g(OR4(A)-OR4(B)) has m=k=30 and W=1024>900 in every nontrivial finite abelian group. Growing/tensor OR families rule out every fixed multiplier and give an all-group lower exponent above1.12197. A paired-literal binary-matroid construction raises the lower exponent to log2(1+sqrt(2)) for GF(2) and groups with a nonzero order-two element; no such per-group claim is made for odd-order groups. A separately proved group-safe dyadic/support-dependent repair survives, including an all-group m^2 fallback. These are proposal-cost bounds for the named mixture; factored OR/matroid examples have easy direct samplers after their representation is supplied. The decoder and arbitrary conditional-sampling problem remain intact. Historical open-conjecture wording is retained as history; a source paired-literal arithmetic typo is explicitly corrected in the new proof.

assumptions: One weak resonant transfer channel with exponential amplitude memory; common supplied d0>0.
Fixed orientation over cycles, prepared donor population, linear differential Stark response over all peak and frequency support.
Positive cubature and traversal occupy real time; filtering adds carrier defect. No arbitrary instantaneous control or multi-channel norm coverage.
field_details.conservation_and_thermodynamics: Parseval normalizes Fourier weights; waveform RMS and peak are accounted separately. Rate suppression is not free energy, population preparation, longer lifetime or chemical yield.
field_details.energy_balance: UNKNOWN actual energy. RMS field is not delivered power; charge field generation, geometry/losses, preparation/readout, heating, ionization and damage. Higher peak/bandwidth may erase any practical benefit.
field_details.error_budget: Charge field and timing errors, finite-bandwidth carrier residual, orientation drift, norm distribution, additional channels, resonance shifts, bath mismatch and readout/model uncertainty.
field_details.governing_equations: Gamma=2J^2 sum_n |c_n(u)|^2 kappa/(kappa^2+n^2 Omega^2); Gamma0=2J^2/kappa. Uniform filtered bound Gamma/Gamma0<=(2*pi^(t+1)/(t+1)!+A/B)^2+(kappa/Omega)^2.
field_details.input_acquisition: Obtain a same-species d0/kappa/J calibration satisfying the exact weak-transfer model plus actual three-axis amplitude/phase transfer function and frozen-orientation interval.
field_details.materials: Actual molecular species/channel, differential Stark vector, environment and orientation stabilization unacquired. Do not combine Stark slopes and IVR rates from different systems.
field_details.reliability: Control every admitted frozen orientation only under the theorem premises. Numerical average over 200 orientations is not that uniform guarantee or a molecular population lifetime.
field_details.resources: Calibrated preparation, suitable same-species channel, vector field bandwidth/peak and time-resolved leakage metrology are unacquired; estimated apparatus cost UNKNOWN.
field_details.units_and_tolerances: Angular frequencies for kappa/Omega/B; source wavenumber conversion must distinguish amplitude and population decay. Numerical quadrature/alias estimates exclude roundoff certification.

Their positive conductances force equal electrochemical potentials, not freely selected K/Cl concentrations. Apply the shared finite mass/water and capacitor-charge identities, then osmotic balance. The required added pump current balances the actual stationary sodium leakage. Osmotic balance reduces composition to one scalar volume root for each Vm.

body: Let Delta_n=T_n-T_(n-1). The backward equation gives n*u*Delta_n=1+(m-n)*a*Delta_(n+1), with Delta_m=1/(m*u). Iterate downwards and sum Delta_n to obtain the formula. The n=1 binomial sum yields the lower bound, proving exponential trapping for fixed positive a/u as m grows. Suppressing rebinding changes the kinetic law to the harmonic case, but active displacement and a selective sink must be acquired for the actual multi-adapter covalent island; a single-donor off-rate does not establish it.

body: Read each round until its first missing frontier edge; the retained prefix crosses L successes and each failure starts another round, giving the negative-binomial law and Var[R]=L*(1-p)/p^2. For each ordered pair i<j, frontier i fails on average(1-p)/p times before crossing; later j independently succeeds with probability p in each such erased round. Thus each pair contributes1-p wasted correct links. Sum all pairs. Retaining disconnected islands instead has completion law[1-(1-p)^r]^L after r rounds under its own ideal model. Packetting assumes independent roots and excludes fusion/root removal; rooted continuity also cannot screen a stable wrong link or infer order from mass/end labels.

assumptions: Incomplete clearance, source exhaustion, register changes and damaged roots violate the renewal. Packet roots/fusion are additional unacquired operations.
costs: Count all formed then discarded correct links, rounds, donor refill and reset. Round counts alone are not total physical time or material/energy usage.
contract.obstruction: Qualify real reset and packet fusion instead of assuming that a small modeled waste count supplies them.
provides: For L>=1 edges, independent per-round per-edge correct probability0<p<=1, no wrong bonds or damage, perfect removal of every unrooted island and unchanged rooted register, R=1+NegBin(L,p) counts failures before L frontier successes. E[R]=1+L*(1-p)/p and E[discarded successful downstream bonds]=(1-p)*L*(L-1)/2. Independently rooted b-edge packets with b dividing L reduce only within-packet waste to(1-p)*L*(b-1)/2.
requires: Perfect full-island clearance, retained original rooted register, independent identical edge opportunities, no permanent wrong link/damage, and all unresolved downstream edges attempted each round.
contract.units: L,b,R and wasted links are counts; p is dimensionless; no conversion to measured material/time is supplied.

body: On an all-correct path with r pairs left, correct hazard is r*k and wrong hazard r*(r-1)*beta. Multiply the next-event correct probabilities as r decreases. For fixed n and small rho=beta/k, log Pcorrect=-rho*n*(n-1)/2+O(rho^2*n^3); this is not a uniform large-n asymptotic without controlling n*rho. With bounded access, next-event success is at least1/(1+D*rho); induction yields the alternative bound. For physically isolated b-edge packets and independent connector failure q, the separately assumed product law is Pcorrect(b)^(L/b)*(1-q)^(L/b-1). Neither the access bound nor independent fusion is supplied by a template label or small-packet success alone.

assumptions: All-to-all and bounded-access are distinct interfaces; the quadratic exponent is not a universal chemistry impossibility.
Packet product requires b dividing L, physical isolation and independently qualified connectors.
costs: All handle preparation, wrong products, isolation, connectors and finite-time completion remain charged; Pcorrect here concerns eventual competing-clock outcomes.
contract.obstruction: Acquire the actual spatial wrong-partner hazards and fusion interface before claiming long-program fidelity.
provides: For n desired one-use handle pairs with intended rate k>0 and every ordered wrong partner rate beta>=0, an all-to-all constant-rate exponential race has Pcorrect=product_{j=0}^{n-1}(1+j*beta/k)^(-1). If instead every surviving state bounds each remaining site's aggregate wrong rate by D*beta while correct rate remains k, Pcorrect>=(1+D*beta/k)^(-n).
requires: Constant exponential hazards and one-use handles; any wrong bond is an absorbing product failure.
The bounded-access alternative requires the same D bound in EVERY surviving reaction state, not only initially.
contract.units: k,beta are inverse time; beta/k and probabilities are dimensionless; n,L,b and D count pairs or bound access.

body: Here P4(q)=1-2*(1-eta*q/2)^4+(1-eta*q)^4. Conditional Poisson thinning gives the zero-weld expression. Its small-time expansion is P4(q(t))=3*(eta*k*t)^2+O(t^3). Scale t by N^(-1/2) in the exponential-clock integral; positive times bounded away from zero contribute exponentially little, leaving the Gaussian half-integral and stated constant. A deterministic time floor makes P4 uniformly positive, giving the exponential upper bound. Retaining a catalyst alone does not guarantee active enzyme, acceptors, water or molecular contact throughout T0. These are model-conditional laws, not calibrated repair reliability or an all-mechanism two-hit lower bound.

assumptions: Independent per-candidate windows and a common regional window are different interfaces. The N^-1/2 tail is fixed-parameter asymptotic, not a finite-N calibrated estimate.
Single-hit/preanchored or otherwise changed mechanisms require their own short-time law. Real correlated regions need separate analysis.
costs: Extra linker abundance pays N supply; guaranteed T0 pays actual enzyme/reactant/water/contact retention and duration. Physical calibration and donor harm are not supplied by the asymptotic.
contract.obstruction: Measure the actual joint access/reaction/retention process before importing the shared-clock reliability law.
provides: For four-arm independent retained grafts with symmetric old/new access and eta>0, fixed k,d>0, T~Exp(d), q(T)=1-exp(-k*T) and Poisson(N) independent candidates conditional on T, zero-weld failure F_N=E[exp(-N*P4(q(T)))]. Jensen gives F_N>=exp(-N*E[P4]). As N->infinity at fixed parameters, F_N~d*sqrt(pi)/(2*eta*k*sqrt(3*N)). If catalytic access truly lasts T+T0 with guaranteed T0>0, F_N<=exp(-N*P4(1-exp(-k*T0))).
requires: Exactly the declared four-arm two-hit independent-graft model with old/new fraction theta=1/2, conditional independence given one common T, Poisson candidate mean N, eta>0 and fixed k,d>0.
For the improved bound, a deterministic positive catalytic period with all actual reaction prerequisites retained, not just a longer expected access time.

body: At k=d, q=1-exp(-d*T) is uniform on[0,1]. Conditional useful count is Poisson(X*q); integrate its CDF below m and substitute z=X*q to obtain the gamma expression. This explains the changed N^-1 law versus the earlier two-hit N^-1/2 process: a real mechanically useful preanchor removes one required chemical event. At fixed arbitrary k/d=r>0, the one-link small-time linear law similarly gives F1~1/(r*X). These are not equal-mass/energy comparisons. Old-side targeting theta and individual later survival S multiply supply only under the declared candidate-thinning model. A guaranteed active T0>0 gives the m=1 bound F1<=exp(-X*(1-exp(-k*T0))) if enzyme, acceptor, water and contact genuinely persist. body: Count chains as supplied mass divided by molecular mass, then multiply by the declared useful-end factors. For long and short chains at otherwise equal factors, the long/short opportunity ratio is(M_short/M_long)*(a_long*e_long*theta_long*S_long)/(a_short*e_short*theta_short*S_short). The source's200-versus880 kDa example therefore needs more than4.4-fold improvement in the useful factor product to beat the shorter chain at equal mass. Multiple usable ends, changed accessibility/rates or different retained mechanical function require a different comparison. AFM adhesion-energy enhancement is not a shear-strength multiplier or a measurement of S.

body: Exclude the no-old and no-new events and add back no-graft. The two excluded powers have a convex sum in theta, so their minimum is symmetric. One arm cannot form this two-sided bridge, and a chemical graft lacking retention in its donor network does not supply a useful end. If separate old/new fibre ends have iid Poisson(mu) useful-junction counts, for K>=0 and mu>=0 the capped weaker-end expected count is sum_{j=1}^floorK Pr[Pois(mu)>=j]^2+(K-floorK)*Pr[Pois(mu)>=floorK+1]^2. This is a count identity under a separate independence/cap model, not a measured force or fracture-energy law.

assumptions: Balanced staging comparison freezes total per-arm retained success; allosteric changes, selective loops or a persistent preanchor change the interface.

provides: For integer v>=1 independent identical arms, each yields a retained old graft with probability u*theta, retained new graft u*(1-theta), or no retained graft1-u. Pcross=1-(1-u*theta)^v-(1-u*(1-theta))^v+(1-u)^v. At fixed total u in[0,1], theta=1/2 maximizes Pcross; splitting unchanged opportunities into old/new stages cannot exceed that balanced model.
requires: Independent identical arms with exclusive old/new/none retained outcomes and actual molecular contact; u=q*eta only when the declared graft/retention decomposition is valid.
A Poisson weaker-end load count additionally needs independently justified endpoint populations and actual mechanical assumptions.
contract.units: u,theta,q,eta and Pcross are probabilities; v and capped junction counts are dimensionless. Force is not obtained without a supplied mechanical law.

Known arithmetic and nonzero scaling convert a noiseless native action into an X-action on W, so the eta=0 signed-inertia result applies. Scaling is not a free noisy oracle transformation. With noisy native reports use Lhat=tr(T*Sc)+sum y_j^T*(z_j-Sc*q_j). Any q_j,y_j then gives the sound bound (1/2)||D^(1/2)*(T-sum sym(q_j*y_j^T))*D^(1/2)||_*+sum eta_j*||y_j||. A containing OUTER interval supports this upper bound, but not the exact-family lower/query theorem or automatic sharpness. Arbitrary old noisy observations need not acquire the entire interval. body: The competing fixed vector phi=(sqrt(lambda),-1,0)/sqrt(1+lambda) obeys R_eta*phi=0 for every real eta and (H_eta+I)*phi=-a*|d>/sqrt(1+lambda). Duhamel gives ||U_T*phi-phi||<=a*T/sqrt(1+lambda) after removing the common energy phase. The input distance is sqrt(2-2*sqrt(lambda/(lambda+1))); target overlap is sqrt(lambda)/(lambda+1). statement: Let C,W,H,Droot be the exclusive per-encounter correct, wrong, harmless and root-death probabilities, summing to1, with mean encounter time t. After H, competence is destroyed with probability delta in[0,1]; otherwise the same competent initial state returns after additional time tau>=0. For Zterm=C+W+Droot+delta*H>0, eventual correct-root yield is C/Zterm, expected encounters 1/Zterm and mean time to any terminal decision [t+H*(1-delta)*tau]/Zterm. The delay is charged only on successful nonterminal recovery.

body: The ideal product follows n independent competing progress/off-rate hazards. For the leak model, let a_i=k/(k+u_i+ell); early-commit probability sums ell/(k+u_i+ell)*sum_{j=0}^{n-2}a_i^j, followed by survival a_i^(n-1) to final competition k/(k+u_i). Sum the geometric series to obtain the formula. A departed donor must destroy/ invalidate its own progress while leaving the parent competent; persistent controller progress usable by a different donor violates this model. The source reports a memory-retention CTMC and quantitative joint thresholds, but its code is absent: no numerical m threshold or optimized n is accepted. Activated NHS donor chemistry cannot simply be assigned ell=0; latent activation and safe escaped-donor handling are separate unacquired operations.

assumptions: Do not infer these hazard rates or reset from published product ratios/fluorescence. Donor carry-away authorization and controller memory change the network.
Fixed ell>0 defeats the large-n ideal benefit; this does not compute an experimentally optimal checkpoint count.
costs: Pay every discarded donor, fuel/reset, wait/residence time, premature bond and death/escape risk. No physical throughput follows from odds alone.
contract.obstruction: Acquire donor-conditioned reset and chemically noncommittal intermediate states before transferring DNA recognition into organic-bond selectivity.
provides: At donor arrival rates lambda_C,lambda_W>0, equal checkpoint rate k>0 and off-rates u_C,u_W>0, complete reset on departure and commitment only at the nth transition give q_i=[k/(k+u_i)]^n and wrong/correct eventual odds=lambda_W*q_W/(lambda_C*q_C). If each of the n-1 intermediate bound states also commits prematurely at ell>0, q_i(n)=ell/(u_i+ell)*[1-(k/(k+u_i+ell))^(n-1)]+(k/(k+u_i+ell))^(n-1)*k/(k+u_i). Then q_W/q_C tends to(u_C+ell)/(u_W+ell), so arbitrarily many checkpoints do not retain exponential discrimination.
requires: The fixed exponential race network, identical competent-parent renewal and fully donor-owned reset; every arrival class is correctly identified.
n>=1 integer; the last transition is actual irreversible chemistry, with no earlier chemistry in the ideal model. The leak variant specifies ell in every earlier state.
contract.units: k,u_i,ell,lambda_i use one inverse-time clock; n and q_i are dimensionless.

body: S switches to A at q and exits by wrong reaction wS, harmless hydrolysis hS or root destruction dS. A reshelters at r and exits by correct k, wrong wA, harmless hA, root destruction dA or escape e; escape is wrong with probability chi and harmless otherwise. Put Z=DS*DA-q*r. First-step equations give C=q*k/Z; W=[wS*DA+q*(wA+e*chi)]/Z; H=[hS*DA+q*(hA+e*(1-chi))]/Z; Droot=[dS*DA+q*dA]/Z; encounter duration t=(DA+q)/Z. These sum to one because their numerators sum to Z. Dividing W by C cancels Z. Ideal renewal gives correct-root yield C/(C+W+Droot), encounters 1/(1-H) and terminal-decision time t/(1-H); multiplying numerator and denominator by Z removes hS from yield and time. Donor consumption still changes. Increasing r at fixed other rates adds wS/(q*k) to d(rho)/dr, strictly worsening odds only if wS>0. The full governing note retains dA; the shorter response omits that hazard and cannot replace the full formula. This is a fixed-network comparison, not a claim that shielding cannot help a real molecule whose other rates change. A switch must change actual wrong-reaction competition or recruitment to improve selectivity; hydrolysis survival alone does not supply that change.

assumptions: Wrong, harmless and destroyed-parent classes are chemically distinct. Root death is a permanent decision, not successful incorporation.
The floor compares the same active chemistry and fixed rates; DNA-mediated changes in recruitment or wrong chemistry require their own evidence.
costs: Count all donor encounters and eventual root loss. Instantaneous replacement omits real recovery, fuel, reagent and waste costs; no finite-time manufacturing guarantee follows.
contract.obstruction: Acquire the actual protected-state aminolysis, active wrong/correct competition, escape and rooted-parent recovery before interpreting hydrolysis protection as proofreading.
provides: For a shielded S/reactive A exponential race, q,k>0, all other hazards nonnegative and chi in[0,1], define DS=q+wS+hS+dS, DA=k+wA+hA+dA+e+r. Wrong/correct absorption odds are rho=(wA+e*chi)/k+(wS/q)*(DA/k), independent of hS at fixed other rates and at least(wA+e*chi)/k. With instantaneous independent harmless replenishment to the same competent S, mean time to any permanent correct/wrong/root-death outcome is (DA+q)/[(wS+dS)*DA+q*(k+wA+e*chi+dA)], also independent of hS.
requires: Fixed declared two-state exponential hazards; q,k>0, chi in[0,1], all other rates nonnegative; the specified escape outcome law.
For renewed yield/time, every H immediately and independently restores the same competent shielded parent with no delay, damage, poisoning or changed rates.
contract.units: All hazards are in one inverse-time clock; t has time units, Z inverse-time squared, C,W,H,Droot,rho dimensionless.

body: First-step conditioning resumes the parent only on f*(1-h), so divide terminal probabilities by1-f*(1-h). A formed irreversible product that never passes is culled/stalled, not restored to the original parent. Its reader accepts eventually with r/(r+c) if pass and irreversible cull probabilities per repeated read are r,c and r+c>0. When c=0 and r>0, unlimited iid reads eventually pass with probability1. Thus reducing false pass speed without culling/repair does not save indefinite readout. The powers require independent identical stages (or the corresponding conditional factorization) and nonzero output probability for conditional purity. Here output means controller-declared advancement; false advancement need not create a chemically full-length molecule. Preserve persistent/stalled/dead roots in the denominator when assessing manufacturing yield.

assumptions: A constant iid false-read law is required for eventual false acceptance1; arbitrary correlated/adaptive tests need their actual joint observation law.
Pure selected products do not imply high yield per starting root or finite completion time.
costs: Charge all attempts, irreversible losses, culls, chemistry/readout time and roots that never finish.
contract.obstruction: Prevent wrong irreversible bonds before commitment or acquire real excision/repair; filtering alone does not restore lost roots.
provides: For identical attempts with exclusive correct irreversible p, wrong irreversible w, death d and harmless f=1-p-w-d, false advancement h on harmless failures, and eventual correct/wrong reader acceptance A_C,A_W, the terminal good and bad advancement probabilities are G=p*A_C/(p+w+d+f*h), B=(w*A_W+f*h)/(p+w+d+f*h). With the declared identical independent stage law, correct-root yield is G^L, controller-declared-complete output fraction (G+B)^L and conditional correct purity [G/(G+B)]^L. Even ideal postbond rejection with d=h=0 gives root yield at most[p/(p+w)]^L.
requires: Valid exclusive p,w,d,f,h and a positive terminal denominator; every harmless retry restores the same competent parent.
Actual product-acceptance probabilities and declared long-chain stage law; no repair or reversal of an irreversible wrong bond is supplied.
contract.units: Dimensionless probabilities/counts; purity conditional on output and yield per original root have different denominators.

body: Variational TV bounds every bounded randomized acceptance function. Bayes odds among admitted products are w*beta/(p*alpha), yielding the conditional purity formula and required ratio. A common downstream stochastic transformation cannot create distinguishability absent from the full available observation. Repeated readings are covered only when O denotes their complete joint record: equal one-read marginals alone need not imply equal joint laws. Covalent continuity may separate a joined product from an unjoined donor while failing to distinguish two stable rooted bond sites. This statement neither asserts all actual PNA products are observationally identical nor supplies a molecular assay. A source-reported hypothetical TV target is not an acquired measurement.

assumptions: No amount of processing a fixed observation can supply omitted chemical information; additional chemistry-sensitive interventions change the interface.
The false class here is stable wrong covalent product, not a freely departing unjoined donor. Do not substitute a wash decay for beta.
costs: Acquire site/sequence-sensitive information and account for accepted fraction, culling and original-root yield separately.
contract.obstruction: Establish the actual wrong-site observation separation before treating a DNA receipt as a certificate of chemical identity.
provides: For complete available observation O with laws P_C,P_W under correct and stable wrong-site covalent products, every randomized receipt delta(O) in[0,1] has alpha-beta<=TV(P_C,P_W), alpha=E_C delta,beta=E_W delta. For p,w>0,alpha>0 and the specified identical independent accepted-stage law, L-stage conditional purity is[1+(w/p)*(beta/alpha)]^-L. Target F in(0,1] requires beta/alpha<=(p/w)*(F^(-1/L)-1). Identical observation laws forbid discrimination by downstream logic alone.
requires: Correct and wrong SITE/sequence classes and their actual complete observation laws, including all repeated/adaptive data used by the controller.
For purity, positive p,w,alpha and identical independent accepted-stage behavior or a justified conditional product model.

body: The affine update has contraction factor(1-p)*q<1. Solve its fixed-point equation and multiply by1-p for the post-damage fraction; solving that inequality for q gives the recovery threshold. At r=0 the fixed fraction is0. The formula is a steady-cycle result: if the initial fraction is below the fixed point it does not certify the startup cycles; initial preparation/recovery must be charged. An initially higher fraction decreases toward the fixed point. The effective active fraction is not a probability that every region or load path survives, and no fracture/fatigue law is inferred from it. Slow cellular replacement of consumed matter is a distinct operation from re-forming sacrificial interactions between loading events. The source code reports convergence/threshold checks, but no actual wet-cellulose recovery rate is supplied or replayed.

assumptions: Nonuniform loads, stochastic population failure, correlated/common damage, irreversible scission and different recovery kinetics need their own models.
Cell growth and an effective sacrificial-network rate have different clocks; a measured chemical conversion cannot supply r or a fatigue threshold.

The arbitrary schedule(3,2,1) at n=6,k=3 has three establishments rather than two and is outside the periodic contract; no arbitrary-partition survival theorem is asserted. The unreset stack counts1+...+n; chemical renewal does not remove those mechanical dependencies. A direct-host route may avoid old seams only by establishing a real load-bearing bypass. When n is a large multiple of k and boundaries/discrete costs are neglected, negative log survival per repair=a*(k+1)/2+c/k; continuous minimization gives k≈sqrt(2*c/a), then integers/boundaries must be checked. body: The reference has top a/bottom b and test top c/bottom d. Force balance gives M*u=Delta*(a,c), M=[[a+b+k,-k],[-k,c+d+k]]. Its determinant is G; subtract the two inverse-matrix solutions to obtain the gap. Positive springs give positive equivalent boundary stiffness Keff, so positive force preserves the sign. For two reference branches with Ai=ai+bi+ki, test midpoint U=Delta*[c+sum_i(ki*ai/Ai)]/[c+d+sum_i(ki)-sum_i(ki^2/Ai)]. The measured gaps are gi=[(ai+bi)*U-ai*Delta]/Ai. These are the actual code Schur complement, not two independent copies of the single-probe formula. To encode two desired crossings dH<dS, solve jointly for positive physical references satisfying g1(dH)=0 and g2(dS)=0. Existence/positive implementability must be established for the chosen design; source solver values are reports. With a valid calibration each gi decreases with d at fixed Delta>0, so its sign implements the specified crossing. Required excitation, reference drift, noise, geometry and probe backaction remain physical costs. At Delta=0 every gap is zero, and compression reverses the sign interpretation.

assumptions: Load magnitude independence concerns the sign/zero in this linear model, not displacement amplitude, noise margin or arbitrary service geometry.

For Delta>0, sign(g)=sign(c*b-a*d), so the zero occurs at d=c*b/a. Positive force control has the same sign because Delta=F/Keff>0. Finite k changes signal amplitude but not this single-probe zero. body: Uniform scaling multiplies both sides of the prescribed-displacement equilibrium by lambda, leaving displacements unchanged; forces and equivalent stiffness scale. Include the sensing spring in that scaling. This exact full-gap alias is not asserted under fixed force, where extension changes. At the hardening example zero gap, both midpoints equal Delta/2 and the probe carries no force. Balance Delta/2=d*Delta/2+h*(Delta/2)^3 to obtain the neutral threshold. Unknown strain can therefore mimic repair; a calibrated deformation regime or richer model is required. Equal small-strain stiffness also does not specify rupture/fatigue behavior. In the two-world action toy, J=0 in both worlds. Any observation-only randomized policy chooses A with the same probability p in both; success is[p+(1-p)]/2. The bound assumes only those two full-unit actions and no additional informative probe/intervention. Extra resources permitting both actions or additional distinguishing observations change the problem. These are scoped failures of the specific observation interface, not universal impossibility of sensing or biological repair.

body: Integrate d(e^-2)/dt=2*A to obtain the cubic closure law. It models opening proportional to remaining stiffness error, laminar slit flow proportional to opening cubed and instantaneous conversion to useful repair; it is not the delayed-stock model. A positive tolerance is attainable in finite model time, so asymptotic exact equality alone does not prove failure of every useful repair target. Maintenance thresholds or finite resources require their actual laws. For the delayed model, differentiate d+eta*z; the maturation terms cancel. After q=0, z=z(t*)*exp[-(t-t*)/tau] and the stated remaining stock contributes eta*z(t*). The finite-budget bound follows by integrating q and taking nonnegative remaining stock. This analytic consequence was reconstructed from the supplied ODE and code; it is not a reproduced numerical trajectory. q,z,d use calibrated source-normalized stiffness-equivalent units and eta is fixed useful conversion; real mass, attachment and orientation need their own mapping. The two-stage mechanical gate can choose q using calibrated comparator signs, but source final stiffnesses and noisy repair populations remain reports. Feedback detects missing function; it cannot make eta positive or create a missing load-bearing attachment.

assumptions: Do not silently transfer the instantaneous cubic law to delayed cells or a different fluid geometry.
Finite-budget or post-cutoff predictions do not acquire positive conversion, structural integration, maintenance supply or a calibrated biological time.
costs: Count feedstock, oxygen, finite transport, maturation time and stock remaining when the gate shuts; target a specified useful tolerance.
contract.obstruction: Acquire productive nutrient flow and actual useful incorporation; a correct mechanical feedback signal cannot supply either interface by itself.
provides: Under the separate instantaneous model e_dot=-A*e^3 with A>0,e0>0, e(t)=[e0^(-2)+2*A*t]^(-1/2)>0 for finite t; reaching positive tolerance eps<e0 takes [eps^(-2)-e0^(-2)]/(2*A). A positive minimum productive flow can stop growth earlier. Separately, for fixed eta in[0,1], tau>0 and z_dot=q-z/tau, d_dot=eta*z/tau, d+eta*z changes at rate eta*q. If feed stops at t*, eventual d is d(t*)+eta*z(t*), assuming all remaining stock follows this maturation law. With total subsequent feed <=B, d_final<=d0+eta*(z0+B).
requires: For cubic closure only: instantaneous growth response, fixed A>0, e0>0 and the stated opening/flow/error conversion; tolerance 0<eps<e0.
For stock conservation separately: fixed tau>0, eta in[0,1], q,z>=0, no additional stiffness decay or stock loss, consistent normalized units; all remaining stock matures as stated.
contract.units: e,d,z have source-normalized stiffness-equivalent units; A has inverse-time/inverse-error-squared units, q has stock/time, tau has time, eta dimensionless.

body: Differentiate E_k: dE_k/dk=delta0^2*(1-k*R)/[2*(1+k*R)^3]. The nonzero-gap optimum follows; if delta0=0 every k stores zero energy. The quadratic port potential follows by integrating the port potential gradient (delta-delta0)/R. Phi(0)-Phi(delta0)=delta0^2/(2*R) is a difference between specified states. Starting at the free minimum and pulling the port to0 instead costs that amount. Connecting/preloading a spring or driving the outer boundaries also requires an actual preparation path; a stationary matrix computation does not supply it. Thus the source label available_energy is not accepted as free work from an already relaxed comparator or as a universal bound under arbitrary boundary motion. A prepared zero-gap release can leave an optimized spring with one-quarter of that potential drop; neither that ratio nor the stationary stored energy certifies a complete actuator/reset cycle. In the source symmetric bridge a=b=c=K0,bottom=K0*d with K0>0,d>0, delta0=Delta*(1-d)/[2*(1+d)] and R=(3+d)/[2*K0*(1+d)]. For e=1-d near0 at fixed Delta,K0, delta0=Delta*e/4+O(e^2) and the conditional potential drop is K0*Delta^2*e^2/32+O(e^3). A fixed switching-work demand therefore needs separately charged energy, a prepared storage path or a vanishing-work actuator near balance. No cycle counts or source numerical table were replayed.

assumptions: Stored spring energy is not a proof of a feasible valve, coupling/release path or repeatable harvesting cycle.
The near-balance asymptotic uses the specified symmetric linear bridge at fixed K0,Delta; it is not a universal passive-work bound under arbitrary driving.
costs: Pay loading, port constraint/latch, reset, capture/storage losses and required valve work. Levers trade stroke for force without creating work.
contract.obstruction: Acquire the initial-state preparation and complete work/reset trajectory before treating a precision signal as powered actuation.
provides: For a linear port with free gap delta0, compliance R>0 and an attached zero-rest spring k>=0, delta=delta0/(1+k*R) gives stored spring energy E_k=k*delta0^2/[2*(1+k*R)^2]. Its maximum is delta0^2/(8*R) at k=1/R when delta0!=0. The port potential Phi(delta)=(delta-delta0)^2/(2*R)+constant drops by delta0^2/(2*R) on the specified release from a constrained delta=0 state to free delta0 at fixed boundaries. A port already relaxed at delta0 has no such releasable drop without a newly paid preparation or changed drive.
requires: R>0,k>=0 and the stated quasistatic zero-rest-spring port; fixed boundary displacement/geometry while evaluating equilibrium.
For work release, an actual initial constraint delta=0, subsequent release toward delta0 and paid preparation/loading/reset. A freely relaxed initial state does not satisfy this premise.
contract.units: delta,delta0,Delta are lengths; R length/force; k,K0 force/length; E,Phi work. d,e are dimensionless normalized stiffness/error.

Completion under irreversible retained footprints is exactly the event that this permutation respects all block constraints; any blocked clock event leaves an unfinished site forever. For unequal positive constant rates the probability of a permutation is the product of each next rate divided by the remaining total rate, not1/n!. The actual source hyperblock branch checks legal ports along each sampled order; its pairwise branch equivalently forbids firing a blocker before any unfinished target. An independent blocking pair succeeds with probability1/2; multiplying over500 independent pairs gives2^(-500), only under that cross-pair independence. Harmless repeated chemistry changes nothing if effective first-success clocks keep the stated law. Outcome-confirmed staging can choose an order; blind finite staging pays missed-attempt probabilities and cannot assume persistent dead sites recover.

body: Explicit domain clarification from v1: omit self arcs. A site has no own product-guide footprint before its first reaction, so a one-site self-loop imposes no chemical release requirement even though literal graph FVS would delete one vertex. The source exhaustive graph generator uses i!=j. Every unreleased edge i->j requires j before i. A directed cycle of such edges makes these strict time inequalities impossible, so every cycle must contain a released source. Conversely, if released set R hits all directed cycles, deleting its outgoing edges leaves a DAG; any reverse topological order is feasible, releasing R immediately after each successful reaction. Cycles in this outgoing-deleted graph are exactly cycles avoiding R, so the minimum equals the usual directed feedback vertex set. This is a standard graph-theoretic reduction within the chemical model, not new graph theory. Additional chemical prerequisites can introduce opposite ordering constraints; multiple ports and cooperative blocking sets require the more general state search. The source-reported four-vertex4096-graph histogram is not independently replayed or accepted as a new numerical result.

body: Correct transfer must consume the sole target amine without exposing a new nucleophile and preserve the rooted amide through all later feeds; a competent miss restores the same parent. First correct success at feed k+1 requires k misses, yielding the geometric sum. Permanent wrong acylation absorbs the site and cannot be washed into a harmless miss. For target alpha in(0,1), even the limiting L-site ceiling is below alpha when w>p*(alpha^(-1/L)-1); finite feeds need a separate residual-miss allowance. The source m14/p=.6/w=1e-6/L1000 value is an illustrative report, not measured kinetics. At m=0 the empty sum is zero even when p+w=1; for m>=1 and p+w=1 it is p. Source protected_transfer_yield instead returns p^L at p+w=1 for every permitted m>=0, so its zero-feed boundary is erroneous. Preserve the original code, use the analytic law and do not extend acceptance to that branch. No current result JSON/log is supplied. Persistent dead sites, reactivity after correct transfer, cross-acylation, depletion and guide occlusion violate this simple retry interface. Donor self-cleavage alone supplies neither product-qualified progress nor noncovalent guide removal.

body: The jam event is the intersection of two retention events; Frechet bounds follow from containment and inclusion-exclusion. At r=.9, independent-pair no-jam is.99 but common-mode pair no-jam is.9. The100-motif products in the source additionally assume motifs independent; a shared global failure across motifs cannot be replaced by those products. This concerns the retained pair at the final challenge, not an acquired dynamic wash process. Chemical cleavage of a donor linkage does not imply physical duplex ejection or restored access; hydrolyzed and trapped strands also need clearance. A proposed four-cohort assay presets neither/A/B/AB products, challenges C at common t, and under homogeneous first-order kinetics uses k_x=-ln(1-p_x)/t and eta=1-k_AB*k0/(k_A*k_B). Positive eta rejects the specified multiplicative-inhibition null, not uniquely steric causation; electrostatics, salt/density and competing nucleophiles are confounders. Require0<p_x<1,t>0 and measured product identity, then test selective guide displacement or an alternate C approach.

body: Each capture is followed by a competing irreversible commitment or chemical reversal back to the same competent uncaptured root. First-step success equations weight each capture by its commitment probability; reversing branches renew. Dwell-time equations retain time in both precursors and yield the displayed numerator. Chemical disassembly is the relevant r, not merely loss of a DNA duplex after covalent precursor formation. The actual source function has only capture, commitment and reversal arguments; its common-off loop changes shared chemical reversal and preserves capture-ratio odds. Any DNA-state coupling must demonstrably change actual chemical rates or prevent access. A self-silencing end product does not itself supply selective precursor capture. The source256-donor concentration/reversal numbers extrapolate an isolated component proxy under equal accessibility, fixed kinetics and a supplied correct-capture rate; scaffold exclusion/caging can invalidate those premises. Heterocyclic end products, donor-DNA ejection and site-specific identity remain separate physical interfaces.

assumptions: Wrong chemical capture before recognition is permitted by the model; mismatch does not prove chemical exclusion.

With no other permanent exit, P_C=A/(A+B) and mean completion time T=[1+alpha_C/(c_C+r_C)+alpha_W/(c_W+r_W)]/(A+B). If correct/wrong commitment and reversal kinetics match, B/A=alpha_W/alpha_C; a DNA label or departure alone adds no discrimination.
requires: Finite nonnegative rates with alpha_C>0,c_C>0,c_W+r_W>0, hence A>0 for the B/A ratio; initial competent root and identical competent state after reversal.
No other permanent exit, aging, donor depletion or history change; real rate coupling to recognition must be separately supplied.

body: C is an expectation. At q<1 any finite retry count can be exceeded with positive probability; no hard material/time bound follows. Renewal gives C=A+(1-q)C with A including both child costs and join overhead on every attempt. Interpret p as correct new-junction acceptance, not a promise that previously wrong children become correct. A persistent wrong bond passing the same connectivity test is not removed by repeated identical washing. Boundary-only q_i,c_i independent of chosen child sizes/protocol give C(i,j)=min_k[C(i,k)+C(k+1,j)+c_k]/q_k, O(L^3) time/O(L^2) storage; size-dependent protocols require additional state. The acquired size_dependent_cost code uses n=2,4,...,L as TOTAL NEW PRODUCT length in q(n)=q0*exp(-kappa*n). Thus C_L=L*q0^(-log2 L)*exp(2*kappa*(L-1)). If n instead denotes each child length, the multiplier is exp(kappa*(L-1)). Retain the convention; neither is a measured steric law. Obtaining a verified-correct product additionally requires an actual discriminating reader and its full costs.

assumptions: Material per accepted product is not material per verified-correct product, throughput or practical advantage.
Size-law n must be defined; the written exponent2 uses total output length, not child length.
costs: Count all rebuilt leaves, lost children, connectors, join operations, purification, wash/time and final validation; no free oracle for correctness.

For constant q,zero overhead,L=2^k, expected C_L=(2/q)^k; q<1 gives unbounded retry support, not a finite worst-case budget. requires: IID per-node accepted attempts independent of child history/resources; rejected attempts destroy both submitted children; explicit leaf/join costs.
Constant-size-independent q for the polynomial law; local junction error independence and correct leaves for the purity product; boundary q/c unchanged by subprotocol for the stated DP.

It excludes only terminal azide-alkyne cyclization, not Glaser/side chemistry, wrong bonds, incomplete intermediates or transient bridge loops. An even target needs a separate B finishing step with its remaining port consumed/passivated. During fusion the two inputs expose four A ports, and safe storage alone says nothing about which two the connector chooses.

One creates correct fusion, two consume both termini of the same fragment and make a ring, and three create wrong orientations/crosslinks. Therefore correct=1/6, ring=1/3, other wrong=1/2. This is not a prediction of real collision rates, but demonstrates that safe completed endpoints DO NOT ensure safe ternary fusion.

Its stationary equation makes a linear functional coefficient negative below the threshold and positive above. Pointwise minimization followed by Cauchy–Schwarz proves the bound over every measurable admissible curve. Continuous curves approach the infimum without a slope bound. Actual switches need measured local contrast/dynamics; timescale, mean, threshold error and charging cannot be silently rescaled away.

body: Nonnegative variation of constants supplies the path contribution. Assign each next path edge a successive full-period window, so any original phase order can transmit over repeated periods. Retention is at least exp(-k delta P). Reverse the same undirected path to preserve the lower bound. Other clamped terminals absorb the perturbation, so union connectivity alone is insufficient. The theorem excludes finite perfect isolation in this class, not large finite ratios or interference/nonreciprocal primitives.

assumptions: A path through another clamped terminal is not a transmitting path. General SPD storage cannot inherit compartment positivity. The comparator requires feasible mean contacts; no assertion for every nonconvex actuator budget or every individual current at distinct temperatures. Finite isolation is possible; Float64 zero is not exact zero. At z800 reverse1.5282810767e-351 survives while the saved Float64 coefficient underflows. No universal approximate-router no-go. No acquired measurement, fabricated device, historical priority, efficient algorithm or practical advantage is inferred from these mathematical/model results. Mission NOT_ACHIEVED.

body: Apply the finite single-port construction separately at two real Laplace points. Their diagonal slope is C_i/h_i, breaking the old congruence gauge only because C is independently known. A finite rectangular pulse approximates each response with the explicit exponential tail and white-noise variance in the parent. Taking T large reduces tail but does not eliminate variance or inverse conditioning. The completed audit checked exact calibrations and retained0/8 physically valid noisy direct returns. This is a conditional reconstruction, not self-created absolute calibration.

assumptions: Exact real identifiability/count optimality does not imply robust physical recovery. Positive diagonal shunts cannot remove the hidden-loss depth barrier under the specified readout model. The stronger transient all-signed-input bound charges squared input, not physical work. Unequal-variance extension compares Gaussian KL, not Blackwell order. All8 noisy direct calibrations rejected or left the physical class; ordinary constrained joint fitting was stronger but small port error did not identify internal parameters. body: For a two-component vector w let U have its columns, G=U*U and E_i=U*Q_i U. Projection gives ||X*w||²>=d*G+ d, d=sum_i E_i x_i. Equality is realizable on rank G<=2 by support-restricted inverse square roots; conjugate averaging makes real data sufficient. The normalized moment SDP and common-center dual then preserve the exact coefficient. Saved rational unnormalized E_i,h_i encode Q_i=G^-1/2 E_i G^-1/2 and u_i=G^-1/2 h_i, while the ratio is evaluated exactly without a rational square root. Strict channel positivity supports faithful limits; it does not eliminate the vacuum lift or its logarithmic convergence costs.

body: Leijdekker–Spreij (2008), Papaspiliopoulos–Ruggiero (2014), and Kon Kam King et al. (2023) establish the CIR gamma-mixture/dual-filter ingredients. The scoped reusable operation is the positive Poisson-times-real-root factorization with root interlacing, lifetime tags, an explicitly paid mean-preserving reset, and the resulting joint-law/expected-memory bounds. The independent check derives the key inequalities from the displayed equations. No external correctness, novelty, or complete finite-bit implementation claim follows.

assumptions: m,kappa,nu>0; thermal Gamma(m,1/nu) initialization; complete fine count times; one shared predictable control functional in both compared laws.
Reset is a known-state computational approximation Bernoulli(p)->Poisson(p), not a physical reset or unknown-posterior oracle.
Fixed threshold 0<tau<1; finite horizon T>0 and 0<epsilon<2 c_max m nu T when choosing tau from epsilon. The finite-horizon joint-law guarantee is for 0<=t<=T.
Anytime rule: c_max,t0>0 and 0<epsilon<2 c_max m nu t0; each inherited tag keeps its birth threshold. This differs from fixed tau.
Any external long-history controller memory is not included; both laws use the same predictable control functional.
costs: The bounds count expected stored real parameters. Root bracketing, arithmetic, rate integration, event-time precision and numerical likelihood error require separate accounting. Fixed-tau error grows with T; the anytime schedule has log-growing expected state size.
contract.obstruction: No constant worst-case memory or rare-history conditional guarantee. Exact linear predictive Hankel rank is infinite for the stationary scalar count process. Binary nonempty bins destroy the finite Poisson-times-Bernoulli class. No port-sensitive/interferometric or general nonlinear quantum filter is proved.

STATUS | Source-derived theorem and implementation-audit report; scoped review pending. The claim concerns the altered protocol with physical local cuts and private onsite noise. It is not a simulation of the uncut experiment or an established practical advantage.

EXACT CLAIM
For a finite-dimensional lattice with a supplied block partition of maximum size B maintained by visible local measure-and-prepare cuts, apply independent private full-rank onsite replacement noise after each sweep. Under the stated finite-operation and model conditions, a positive block-state observer maintains a uniform trace-distance allowance for every supported current record and for future physical experiments started from the encoded state. The state uses at most (N/B)d^(2B) independent real coordinates, with sufficient precision growing logarithmically in N and inverse tolerance when d, B and noise strength are fixed. Dependence on B remains exponential.

PHYSICAL CONTRACT
The cut is part of the physical protocol: it separates the measured site while retaining the conditionally updated remainder of its former block as one component. Remote entanglement is not split by assuming spatial adjacency. Private noise labels are not observer inputs. The initial state, local operations, maximum block size, finite work between sweeps and noise lower bound must satisfy the source contract.

SOURCE-REPORTED FINITE EXAMPLE
The selected report describes an N=4, B=2, b=34 two-qubit control with 512 sweeps, 2048 weak marks and 510 visible endpoint cuts, with a uniform current-state allowance 31/67108864. Its independent audit text reports 48 exact noise/rounding cases. No producer code was selected or replayed in this intake. The 10,000-site, 4.8 MB coordinate payload is a theoretical scaling calculation, not an execution; it excludes partition, model, controller, cache and working-array costs.

LIMITS AND COMPARATORS
A fixed current-state error does not give a fixed error for the whole infinite record; that requires a separate summable error schedule with growing precision. The theorem is exponential in B and the cuts/noise change the experiment. The positive finite-dimensional cone floor does not transfer to the unbounded bosonic thermal space using mean energy alone. Conventional density filters and tensor methods receive the same information and are direct comparators; exclusive advantage is not established. This result is distinct from N959's classical local-preparation record and does not validate that claim.

The governing theorem, dedicated block-partition proof, internal audit, finite example and non-transfer limits are indexed in the attached source index. Internal source exposure is not external review; external correctness, novelty, physical value and practical advantage remain UNKNOWN.

body:
N991-p3-intervention-response-kernel-acquisition | First-contact dose interventions acquire a bounded response kernel without finite-mean kinetics

STATUS | Source-derived theorem and synthetic acquisition report; scoped review pending. No physical assay or hidden kinetic network was acquired.

EXACT CLAIM
Let a native experiment have an arbitrary possibly non-Markovian hidden path, finite terminal category B, and almost-surely finite stopping time. Before the first probe hit, a nonnegative dose vector c changes only independently driven competing capture clocks with predictable path susceptibilities b_j(t), under the stated dose-linearity and no-interference contract. If each integrated susceptibility A_j is finite almost surely (without a finite-mean or maximum-rate bound), then the no-hit outcome subprobabilities are K_b(c)=E[1{B=b} exp(-c·A)]. A weak mixed-dose challenge acquires the common continuity modulus L(h)=K_hit(h,...,h). A finite-net procedure can acquire uniform bounded-dose predictions and a set of compatible joint measures; it does not identify the hidden microscopic network or rates.

FIRST-CONTACT REPORTING EXTENSION
A source theorem allows arbitrary post-contact dynamics after an untagged contact if the persistent-tag probability q applies conditionally to relevant first contacts. This q is an instrument/design premise, not estimated by the synthetic data. For q<1 the actual response retains a bounded residual; the q=1 arbitrary-accuracy result is not transferred to the whole actual response by increasing repetitions or numerical degree.

SYNTHETIC SOURCE RECORD
The selected source describes a five-state hidden transient, two native categories, two probe channels, 12 dose arms and 12,000 categorical draws per arm (144,000 total; seed 2026102503). No physical data or terminal times were generated. The selected interval JSON states a 36-member simultaneous family. The source return lacked interception_operators.json and interception_contact_operators.json; this intake does not replay the fit or certify the reported dual/contact calculations from those unavailable operator artifacts.

LIMITS AND COMPARATORS
The finite-data procedure stops almost surely under its source contract but has no model-uniform experiment-count bound; the dose net is generally exponential in channel count and the smallest realizable dose can limit precision. The conditional first-contact coverage premise is not measured by these observations. No physical kinetics, novelty, optimal dose allocation, advantage, or superiority to nonparametric frailty, moment/SDP, imprecise-process, trajectory or tensor methods is established. This response kernel is distinct from N744's stationary flux polytope and does not validate its reset or microscopic-source contract.

EVIDENCE
The exact representation, finite-data construction, contact extension, synthetic observation configuration and intervals are indexed in the attached source index. Producer scripts were not run.
